column6: Tā zhōngyú zhǎodào le chènxīnrúyì de gōngzuò.
column7: She finally found a job that suits her perfectly.
column9: An idiom for getting just what you hoped for: a job, a home, a purchase. It is also a common good wish: 祝你稱心如意. 稱 is read chèn in this word, not chēng as in its meaning "to weigh". Taiwan reads 稱 here as chèng.

column3: A spoken adverb that goes before a verb, usually with a hint of spite: 成心气我 (do it to annoy me), 成心找麻烦 (look for trouble).
column4: 你是不是成心气我？
column5: 你是不是成心氣我？
column6: Nǐ shì bù shì chéngxīn qì wǒ?
column7: Are you doing this on purpose to annoy me?
column9: A spoken adverb that goes before a verb, usually with a hint of spite: 成心氣我 (do it to annoy me), 成心找麻煩 (look for trouble).

column3: Formal and warm, used before a noun for feelings you put into words: 诚挚的感谢 (thanks), 诚挚的问候 (greetings), 诚挚的友谊 (friendship).
column4: 我要向你表示诚挚的感谢。
column5: 我要向你表示誠摯的感謝。
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng nǐ biǎoshì chéngzhì de gǎnxiè.
column7: I want to express my sincere thanks to you.
column9: Formal and warm, used before a noun for feelings you put into words: 誠摯的感謝 (thanks), 誠摯的問候 (greetings), 誠摯的友誼 (friendship).

column3: Used for taking on a construction job, a piece of land or a shop under a contract: 承包工程, 承包土地. The party that does it is the 承包商. 承 shows a kneeling person with both hands, holding something up.
column4: 这家公司承包了新大楼的建设。
column5: 這家公司承包了新大樓的建設。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī chéngbāo le xīn dàlóu de jiànshè.
column7: This company took the contract to build the new building.
column9: Used for taking on a construction job, a piece of land or a shop under a contract: 承包工程, 承包土地. The party that does it is the 承包商. 承 shows a kneeling person with both hands, holding something up.

column3: The castle of fairy tales and European history, as in 童话里的城堡. A Chinese city wall is a 城墙, and an old walled town a 古城.
column4: 山顶上有一座古老的城堡。
column5: 山頂上有一座古老的城堡。
column6: Shāndǐng shàng yǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
column7: There is an old castle on top of the mountain.
column9: The castle of fairy tales and European history, as in 童話裡的城堡. A Chinese city wall is a 城牆, and an old walled town a 古城.

column3: A verb for putting food into a bowl or plate: 盛饭, 盛汤, 盛一碗. The other reading, shèng, means flourishing.
column4: 请帮我盛一碗汤。
column5: 請幫我盛一碗湯。
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ chéng yī wǎn tāng.
column7: Please ladle me a bowl of soup.
column9: A verb for putting food into a bowl or plate: 盛飯, 盛湯, 盛一碗. The other reading, shèng, means flourishing.

column3: Mostly a bound character that joins another: 盛开 (bloom), 盛行 (be popular), 盛大 (grand), 繁盛 and 旺盛 (thriving, vigorous). The same character is read chéng when it means to hold or ladle out food.
column4: 春天，公园里百花盛开。
column5: 春天，公園裡百花盛開。
column6: Chūntiān, gōngyuán lǐ bǎihuā shèng kāi.
column7: In spring the flowers bloom in profusion in the park.
column9: Mostly a bound character that joins another: 盛開 (bloom), 盛行 (be popular), 盛大 (grand), 繁盛 and 旺盛 (thriving, vigorous). The same character is read chéng when it means to hold or ladle out food.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: parents, teachers or the law 惩罚 someone, and the person 受到惩罚 or 接受惩罚. Often for a deliberate penalty meant to teach a lesson.
column4: 做错事就要受到惩罚。
column5: 做錯事就要受到懲罰。
column6: Zuò cuò shì jiù yào shòudào chéngfá.
column7: If you do wrong, you have to be punished.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: parents, teachers or the law 懲罰 someone, and the person 受到懲罰 or 接受懲罰. Often for a deliberate penalty meant to teach a lesson.

column3: Most often figurative: to set the record straight, as in 澄清事实, 澄清误会, 澄清谣言, typically in a statement or an interview. The literal sense is clear, limpid water. When liquid settles and becomes clear, 澄 is read dèng.
column4: 公司发表声明，澄清了这个误会。
column5: 公司發表聲明，澄清了這個誤會。
column6: Gōngsī fābiǎo shēngmíng, chéngqīng le zhège wùhuì.
column7: The company issued a statement clearing up the misunderstanding.
column9: Most often figurative: to set the record straight, as in 澄清事實, 澄清誤會, 澄清謠言, typically in a statement or an interview. The literal sense is clear, limpid water. When liquid settles and becomes clear, 澄 is read dèng.

column3: On its own it is mostly a color word, 橙色, or part of 橙汁. For the fruit, the mainland says 橙子 and Taiwan usually 柳丁 or 柳橙.
column4: 这件衣服是橙色的。
column5: 這件衣服是橙色的。
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì chéng sè de.
column7: This piece of clothing is orange.
column9: On its own it is mostly a color word, 橙色, or part of 橙汁. For the fruit, the mainland says 橙子 and Taiwan usually 柳丁 or 柳橙.

column3: The scale for weighing, from market steelyards to kitchen scales; the measure word is 把 or 杆. Figuratively, 心里有杆秤 means having a sense of what is fair.
column4: 请用秤称一下这些苹果。
column5: 請用秤稱一下這些蘋果。
column6: Qǐng yòng chèng chēng yīxià zhèxiē píngguǒ.
column7: Please weigh these apples on the scale.
column9: The scale for weighing, from market steelyards to kitchen scales; the measure word is 把 or 杆. Figuratively, 心裡有桿秤 means having a sense of what is fair.

column3: A verb-object phrase, a trait praised in people: 能吃苦, 不怕吃苦, 吃得了苦, and the set phrase 吃苦耐劳 (hardworking and able to endure hardship). 吃 also means to suffer, which is why you "eat" hardship.
column4: 年轻人要不怕吃苦。
column5: 年輕人要不怕吃苦。
column6: Niánqīngrén yào bù pà chīkǔ.
column7: Young people should not be afraid of hardship.
column9: A verb-object phrase, a trait praised in people: 能吃苦, 不怕吃苦, 吃得了苦, and the set phrase 吃苦耐勞 (hardworking and able to endure hardship). 吃 also means to suffer, which is why you "eat" hardship.

column3: Said of a person's mind or senses, mildly negative: 反应迟钝 (slow to react), 感觉迟钝 (dulled senses), 头脑迟钝. For slow progress or development, 迟缓 fits better.
column4: 他的反应有点迟钝。
column5: 他的反應有點遲鈍。
column6: Tā de fǎnyìng yǒudiǎn chídùn.
column7: His reactions are a bit slow.
column9: Said of a person's mind or senses, mildly negative: 反應遲鈍 (slow to react), 感覺遲鈍 (dulled senses), 頭腦遲鈍. For slow progress or development, 遲緩 fits better.

column3: Describes slow movement, development or progress, a little formal: 行动迟缓, 进展迟缓, 发展迟缓. A slow mind or reaction is 迟钝 instead.
column4: 经济的发展很迟缓。
column5: 經濟的發展很遲緩。
column6: Jīngjì de fāzhǎn hěn chíhuǎn.
column7: Economic development is slow.
column9: Describes slow movement, development or progress, a little formal: 行動遲緩, 進展遲緩, 發展遲緩. A slow mind or reaction is 遲鈍 instead.

column3: To pause before acting or answering, common in narration: 迟疑了一下, 毫不迟疑 (without hesitation), 迟疑不决 (undecided). 疑 began as a picture of a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.
column4: 她迟疑了很久，才点头答应。
column5: 她遲疑了很久，才點頭答應。
column6: Tā chíyí le hěn jiǔ, cái diǎntóu dāying.
column7: She hesitated for a long time before nodding yes.
column9: To pause before acting or answering, common in narration: 遲疑了一下, 毫不遲疑 (without hesitation), 遲疑不決 (undecided). 疑 began as a picture of a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.

column3: Goes before a noun or follows 很: 持久战 (a protracted war), 持久的和平, 效果持久, 香味持久. It describes what keeps its effect over time.
column4: 这种香水的香味很持久。
column5: 這種香水的香味很持久。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xiāngshuǐ de xiāngwèi hěn chíjiǔ.
column7: This perfume has a very lasting scent.
column9: Goes before a noun or follows 很: 持久戰 (a protracted war), 持久的和平, 效果持久, 香味持久. It describes what keeps its effect over time.

column3: A geography word. It builds 赤道地区 (equatorial regions) and the country name 赤道几内亚 (Equatorial Guinea).
column4: 赤道附近的气候终年炎热。
column5: 赤道附近的氣候終年炎熱。
column6: Chìdào fùjìn de qìhòu zhōngnián yánrè.
column7: The climate near the equator is hot all year round.
column9: A geography word. It builds 赤道地區 (equatorial regions) and the country name 赤道幾內亞 (Equatorial Guinea).

column3: The usual partners are 财政 and 贸易: 财政赤字, 贸易赤字. Verbs are 出现 and 弥补 (to make up); the opposite is 盈余 (surplus).
column4: 政府今年的财政赤字很大。
column5: 政府今年的財政赤字很大。
column6: Zhèngfǔ jīnnián de cáizhèng chìzì hěn dà.
column7: The government's budget deficit is large this year.
column9: The usual partners are 財政 and 貿易: 財政赤字, 貿易赤字. Verbs are 出現 and 彌補 (to make up); the opposite is 盈餘 (surplus).

column3: It is followed by the role taken on, often a temporary or stand-in one: 充当翻译, 充当桥梁. A thing can do it too: a box can 充当 a table.
column4: 他临时充当我们的翻译。
column5: 他臨時充當我們的翻譯。
column6: Tā línshí chōngdāng wǒmen de fānyì.
column7: He acted as our interpreter for the time being.
column9: It is followed by the role taken on, often a temporary or stand-in one: 充當翻譯, 充當橋梁. A thing can do it too: a box can 充當 a table.

column3: It describes something abundant and flowing, mostly energy or nature: 精力充沛, 体力充沛, 雨量充沛, 阳光充沛. For a plain count of things, such as people or books, it is not used.
column4: 他每天都精力充沛。
column5: 他每天都精力充沛。
column6: Tā měitiān dōu jīnglì chōngpèi.
column7: He is full of energy every day.
column9: It describes something abundant and flowing, mostly energy or nature: 精力充沛, 體力充沛, 雨量充沛, 陽光充沛. For a plain count of things, such as people or books, it is not used.

column3: It is used for things that overlap: schedules, areas, duties, shapes. In grammar it also names reduplication, as in 看看 and 散散步. 重 is read chóng here, meaning to repeat, and zhòng when it means heavy.
column4: 两个会议的时间重叠了。
column5: 兩個會議的時間重疊了。
column6: Liǎng ge huìyì de shíjiān chóngdié le.
column7: The times of the two meetings overlap.
column9: It is used for things that overlap: schedules, areas, duties, shapes. In grammar it also names reduplication, as in 看看 and 散散步. 重 is read chóng here, meaning to repeat, and zhòng when it means heavy.

column3: It is a strong, formal word for admiration felt toward someone great: a hero, a scholar, a teacher of long standing. It is stronger and loftier than 尊敬 and is not said of an ordinary boss or acquaintance. Often 对…充满崇敬.
column4: 我们都很崇敬这位老科学家。
column5: 我們都很崇敬這位老科學家。
column6: Wǒmen dōu hěn chóngjìng zhè wèi lǎo kēxuéjiā.
column7: We all deeply revere this old scientist.
column9: It is a strong, formal word for admiration felt toward someone great: a hero, a scholar, a teacher of long standing. It is stronger and loftier than 尊敬 and is not said of an ordinary boss or acquaintance. Often 對…充滿崇敬.

column3: It is for things packed closely together: 人口稠密, 住户稠密, 稠密的居民区. It does not describe thick liquids; for porridge or soup that is thick, use 稠 alone (粥很稠).
column4: 这个地区人口稠密。
column5: 這個地區人口稠密。
column6: Zhège dìqū rénkǒu chóumì.
column7: This area is densely populated.
column9: It is for things packed closely together: 人口稠密, 住戶稠密, 稠密的居民區. It does not describe thick liquids; for porridge or soup that is thick, use 稠 alone (粥很稠).

column3: It is for organizing something big ahead of time, such as an event, a wedding, a shop opening or a committee: 筹备婚礼, 筹备工作, 筹备委员会. It is both verb and noun; 筹备中 means "in preparation". The 筹 also means to raise money, as in 筹款.
column4: 我们正在筹备明年的展览。
column5: 我們正在籌備明年的展覽。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài chóubèi míngnián de zhǎnlǎn.
column7: We are preparing next year's exhibition.
column9: It is for organizing something big ahead of time, such as an event, a wedding, a shop opening or a committee: 籌備婚禮, 籌備工作, 籌備委員會. It is both verb and noun; 籌備中 means "in preparation". The 籌 also means to raise money, as in 籌款.

column3: It is about what is morally ugly, not what looks plain: 丑恶的嘴脸, 丑恶的行为, 丑恶现象. For a face or a coat that is simply unattractive, say 难看. 恶 is è here, meaning evil, but wù when it means to hate, as in 厌恶.
column4: 他的丑恶行为终于被揭露了。
column5: 他的醜惡行為終於被揭露了。
column6: Tā de chǒu'è xíngwéi zhōngyú bèi jiēlù le.
column7: His vile conduct was finally exposed.
column9: It is about what is morally ugly, not what looks plain: 醜惡的嘴臉, 醜惡的行為, 醜惡現象. For a face or a coat that is simply unattractive, say 難看. 惡 is è here, meaning evil, but wù when it means to hate, as in 厭惡.

column3: Mostly it means to betray: 出卖朋友, 出卖国家, 出卖秘密, 出卖灵魂. For ordinary selling in speech, say 卖; 出卖 for goods sounds formal or like an old notice.
column4: 他为了钱出卖了自己的朋友。
column5: 他為了錢出賣了自己的朋友。
column6: Tā wèile qián chūmài le zìjǐ de péngyou.
column7: He betrayed his own friend for money.
column9: Mostly it means to betray: 出賣朋友, 出賣國家, 出賣秘密, 出賣靈魂. For ordinary selling in speech, say 賣; 出賣 for goods sounds formal or like an old notice.

column3: It describes being so absorbed that you are lost to the world, whether in thought or in something enjoyable. It usually follows a verb with 得 (看得出神, 听得出神) or takes 了 (看出了神).
column4: 孩子们听故事听得出神。
column5: 孩子們聽故事聽得出神。
column6: Háizimen tīng gùshi tīng de chūshén.
column7: The children listened to the story, completely absorbed.
column9: It describes being so absorbed that you are lost to the world, whether in thought or in something enjoyable. It usually follows a verb with 得 (看得出神, 聽得出神) or takes 了 (看出了神).

column3: It is nearly always said of a person's future promise, mostly in 有出息 (will make something of themselves) and 没出息 (a scolding for someone with no ambition or drive). Parents and elders say it about children and young people.
column4: 他儿子很有出息，在大学当教授。
column5: 他兒子很有出息，在大學當教授。
column6: Tā érzi hěn yǒu chūxi, zài dàxué dāng jiàoshòu.
column7: His son has done well for himself and is a university professor.
column9: It is nearly always said of a person's future promise, mostly in 有出息 (will make something of themselves) and 沒出息 (a scolding for someone with no ambition or drive). Parents and elders say it about children and young people.

column3: It is the circumstances a person is in, usually hard ones: 处境困难, 处境危险, 处境尴尬. It goes with a person (他的处境), and 了解 or 同情 someone's 处境 is a common phrase. 处 is read chǔ here, meaning to be in a position, and chù when it means a place.
column4: 他的处境越来越困难。
column5: 他的處境越來越困難。
column6: Tā de chǔjìng yuèláiyuè kùnnan.
column7: His situation is getting harder and harder.
column9: It is the circumstances a person is in, usually hard ones: 處境困難, 處境危險, 處境尷尬. It goes with a person (他的處境), and 了解 or 同情 someone's 處境 is a common phrase. 處 is read chǔ here, meaning to be in a position, and chù when it means a place.

column3: It is a formal word for dealing with an incident, a case or a person, used by authorities and in reports: 妥善处置, 处置不当, 依法处置. It sounds more official than 处理 and can mean punishing.
column4: 警方已经妥善处置了这起事故。
column5: 警方已經妥善處置了這起事故。
column6: Jǐngfāng yǐjīng tuǒshàn chǔzhì le zhè qǐ shìgù.
column7: The police have already handled the accident properly.
column9: It is a formal word for dealing with an incident, a case or a person, used by authorities and in reports: 妥善處置, 處置不當, 依法處置. It sounds more official than 處理 and can mean punishing.

column3: It is both verb and noun, for stock kept for future need, often on a large scale: 外汇储备, 粮食储备, 人才储备, 知识储备. For ordinary saving at home, say 存. Taiwan reads 储 as chú.
column4: 国家储备了大量粮食。
column5: 國家儲備了大量糧食。
column6: Guójiā chǔbèi le dàliàng liángshi.
column7: The country has stockpiled a large amount of grain.
column9: It is both verb and noun, for stock kept for future need, often on a large scale: 外匯儲備, 糧食儲備, 人才儲備, 知識儲備. For ordinary saving at home, say 存. Taiwan reads 儲 as chú.

column3: It is a formal word for breaking a law, a rule or a taboo, or for crossing someone's dignity: 触犯法律, 触犯规定, 触犯众怒. For offending a person in daily life, 得罪 is the usual word.
column4: 这样做会触犯法律。
column5: 這樣做會觸犯法律。
column6: Zhèyàng zuò huì chùfàn fǎlǜ.
column7: Doing it this way would break the law.
column9: It is a formal word for breaking a law, a rule or a taboo, or for crossing someone's dignity: 觸犯法律, 觸犯規定, 觸犯眾怒. For offending a person in daily life, 得罪 is the usual word.

column3: It is a written, descriptive idiom, and in practice it is about traffic and crowds, not rivers: 车辆川流不息, 行人川流不息. It paints a busy, unbroken scene. Taiwan reads the last syllable xí: 川流不息 is chuān liú bù xí there.
column4: 街上的车辆川流不息。
column5: 街上的車輛川流不息。
column6: Jiē shàng de chēliàng chuānliúbùxī.
column7: Cars stream along the street without stopping.
column9: It is a written, descriptive idiom, and in practice it is about traffic and crowds, not rivers: 車輛川流不息, 行人川流不息. It paints a busy, unbroken scene. Taiwan reads the last syllable xí: 川流不息 is chuān liú bù xí there.

column3: It is a fairly formal verb that goes with the space you pass through: a tunnel, a desert, a city, a border. It is also the name of the time-travel story genre: 穿越小说, 穿越剧.
column4: 火车穿越了长长的隧道。
column5: 火車穿越了長長的隧道。
column6: Huǒchē chuānyuè le chángcháng de suìdào.
column7: The train passed through a long tunnel.
column9: It is a fairly formal verb that goes with the space you pass through: a tunnel, a desert, a city, a border. It is also the name of the time-travel story genre: 穿越小說, 穿越劇.

column3: It is for passing on skills, knowledge or experience from someone who has mastered them, such as a master, an elder or an expert: 传授技艺, 传授经验. For teaching a class, 教 is the everyday word. 传 is read chuán here, meaning to pass on, but zhuàn when it means a biography.
column4: 老师傅把手艺传授给了徒弟。
column5: 老師傅把手藝傳授給了徒弟。
column6: Lǎo shīfu bǎ shǒuyì chuánshòu gěi le túdi.
column7: The old master passed his craft on to his apprentice.
column9: It is for passing on skills, knowledge or experience from someone who has mastered them, such as a master, an elder or an expert: 傳授技藝, 傳授經驗. For teaching a class, 教 is the everyday word. 傳 is read chuán here, meaning to pass on, but zhuàn when it means a biography.

column3: It is a formal collective word for ships and boats of every kind, seen in port notices, shipping law and news reports. In everyday speech people just say 船.
column4: 港口有很多船舶进出。
column5: 港口有很多船舶進出。
column6: Gǎngkǒu yǒu hěn duō chuánbó jìnchū.
column7: Many ships come and go at the port.
column9: It is a formal collective word for ships and boats of every kind, seen in port notices, shipping law and news reports. In everyday speech people just say 船.

column3: It splits like a verb and its object: 喘口气, 喘了一口气. 喘口气 is also the usual way to say take a short break from busy work, and 喘不过气来 describes being unable to breathe or being overwhelmed.
column4: 他跑得太快，停下来直喘气。
column5: 他跑得太快，停下來直喘氣。
column6: Tā pǎo de tài kuài, tíng xiàlái zhí chuǎnqì.
column7: He ran so fast that he stopped and gasped for breath.
column9: It splits like a verb and its object: 喘口氣, 喘了一口氣. 喘口氣 is also the usual way to say take a short break from busy work, and 喘不過氣來 describes being unable to breathe or being overwhelmed.

column3: It is everyday and informal: to claim more than is true, so a friend may say 你别吹牛了. The fuller 吹牛皮 means the same. It splits like a verb and its object (吹了牛, 吹什么牛).
column4: 他总爱吹牛，说自己会五种语言。
column5: 他總愛吹牛，說自己會五種語言。
column6: Tā zǒng ài chuīniú, shuō zìjǐ huì wǔ zhǒng yǔyán.
column7: He is always bragging that he speaks five languages.
column9: It is everyday and informal: to claim more than is true, so a friend may say 你別吹牛了. The fuller 吹牛皮 means the same. It splits like a verb and its object (吹了牛, 吹什麼牛).

column3: It is critical in tone: praise that is excessive or insincere, usually to win favor. It takes a person as its object (吹捧上司) and often appears as 互相吹捧.
column4: 他们互相吹捧，谁也不批评谁。
column5: 他們互相吹捧，誰也不批評誰。
column6: Tāmen hùxiāng chuīpěng, shéi yě bù pīpíng shéi.
column7: They flatter each other and nobody criticizes anybody.
column9: It is critical in tone: praise that is excessive or insincere, usually to win favor. It takes a person as its object (吹捧上司) and often appears as 互相吹捧.

column3: It is a picturesque, slightly nostalgic word for the smoke of a village at mealtime: 炊烟袅袅, 缕缕炊烟. It evokes home and the countryside more than an actual chimney. 炊 takes its sound from 吹, which fits blowing on a fire to get it going.
column4: 村子上空飘着缕缕炊烟。
column5: 村子上空飄著縷縷炊煙。
column6: Cūnzi shàngkōng piāozhe lǚlǚ chuīyān.
column7: Wisps of cooking smoke drift above the village.
column9: It is a picturesque, slightly nostalgic word for the smoke of a village at mealtime: 炊煙裊裊, 縷縷炊煙. It evokes home and the countryside more than an actual chimney. 炊 takes its sound from 吹, which fits blowing on a fire to get it going.

column3: In math and building, 垂直于 says what a line or wall is perpendicular to (垂直于地面), and the other direction is 水平. It is also used for anything straight up and down, like a cliff or a drop: 垂直的峭壁. 垂 began as a picture of flowers hanging from a plant.
column4: 旗杆和地面垂直。
column5: 旗桿和地面垂直。
column6: Qígān hé dìmiàn chuízhí.
column7: The flagpole is perpendicular to the ground.
column9: In math and building, 垂直於 says what a line or wall is perpendicular to (垂直於地面), and the other direction is 水平. It is also used for anything straight up and down, like a cliff or a drop: 垂直的峭壁. 垂 began as a picture of flowers hanging from a plant.

column3: On its own it is rare, and the everyday hammer is 锤子 (铁锤 for a heavy iron one). As a verb it means to hammer, as in 千锤百炼 (tempered by a thousand blows); thumping someone's back is 捶背, with 捶.
column4: 他用锤子把钉子敲进墙里。
column5: 他用錘子把釘子敲進牆裡。
column6: Tā yòng chuí zi bǎ dīngzi qiāo jìn qiáng lǐ.
column7: He drove the nail into the wall with a hammer.
column9: On its own it is rare, and the everyday hammer is 錘子 (鐵錘 for a heavy iron one). As a verb it means to hammer, as in 千錘百鍊 (tempered by a thousand blows); thumping someone's back is 捶背, with 捶.

column3: It is abstract: motives, reasons, luck, a style or a feeling. It often sits before 是 to say it is nothing but that: 纯粹是误会, 纯粹是运气. For pure water or gold, use 纯 alone (纯金).
column4: 这纯粹是个误会。
column5: 這純粹是個誤會。
column6: Zhè chúncuì shì ge wùhuì.
column7: This is purely a misunderstanding.
column9: It is abstract: motives, reasons, luck, a style or a feeling. It often sits before 是 to say it is nothing but that: 純粹是誤會, 純粹是運氣. For pure water or gold, use 純 alone (純金).

column3: It is about people and what is in their hearts: love, friendship, motives, a child's mind. For a clean floor or clean hands the everyday word is 干净, not 纯洁.
column4: 他们的友谊很纯洁。
column5: 他們的友誼很純潔。
column6: Tāmen de yǒuyì hěn chúnjié.
column7: Their friendship is very pure.
column9: It is about people and what is in their hearts: love, friendship, motives, a child's mind. For a clean floor or clean hands the everyday word is 乾淨, not 純潔.

column3: Mostly a modifier in front of a noun: 慈善机构 (a charity), 慈善家, 慈善晚会, 慈善捐款. For a kind person you would say 善良 or 慈祥 instead.
column4: 她把钱捐给了慈善机构。
column5: 她把錢捐給了慈善機構。
column6: Tā bǎ qián juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
column7: She donated the money to a charity.
column9: Mostly a modifier in front of a noun: 慈善機構 (a charity), 慈善家, 慈善晚會, 慈善捐款. For a kind person you would say 善良 or 慈祥 instead.

column3: Describes how an older person looks and acts toward others: a 慈祥 face, smile or voice, most often grandparents or elderly teachers. It is not used for a young person or for a child.
column4: 奶奶有一张慈祥的脸。
column5: 奶奶有一張慈祥的臉。
column6: Nǎinai yǒu yī zhāng cíxiáng de liǎn.
column7: Grandma has a kindly face.
column9: Describes how an older person looks and acts toward others: a 慈祥 face, smile or voice, most often grandparents or elderly teachers. It is not used for a young person or for a child.

column3: Mostly cassette tapes (录音磁带) these days, so it sounds old-fashioned; the measure word is 盘. The 磁 is the same one as in 磁铁 (a magnet) and 磁场 (a magnetic field).
column4: 这盘磁带是爸爸年轻时买的。
column5: 這盤磁帶是爸爸年輕時買的。
column6: Zhè pán cídài shì bàba niánqīng shí mǎi de.
column7: Dad bought this cassette tape when he was young.
column9: Mostly cassette tapes (錄音磁帶) these days, so it sounds old-fashioned; the measure word is 盤. The 磁 is the same one as in 磁鐵 (a magnet) and 磁場 (a magnetic field).

column3: Used for animals and plants (雌雄同体 for a creature that is both). It also has a figurative sense: 决一雌雄 means to fight it out to see who wins. Taiwan reads the first syllable cī.
column4: 这种鸟的雌雄很难分辨。
column5: 這種鳥的雌雄很難分辨。
column6: Zhè zhǒng niǎo de cíxióng hěn nán fēnbiàn.
column7: It is hard to tell the male and female of this bird apart.
column9: Used for animals and plants (雌雄同體 for a creature that is both). It also has a figurative sense: 決一雌雄 means to fight it out to see who wins. Taiwan reads the first syllable cī.

column3: A product from a factory or shop that fails quality control, often sold at a discount. Its opposite is 正品 (a genuine, first-grade item); 次货 is the same idea in everyday speech.
column4: 这批货里有不少次品。
column5: 這批貨裡有不少次品。
column6: Zhè pī huò lǐ yǒu bù shǎo cìpǐn.
column7: There are quite a few defective items in this batch of goods.
column9: A product from a factory or shop that fails quality control, often sold at a discount. Its opposite is 正品 (a genuine, first-grade item); 次貨 is the same idea in everyday speech.

column3: The order in which people or things are lined up or taken: 按次序 (in order), 打乱次序 (mix up the order). 顺序 is a near synonym and works for steps and procedures too.
column4: 请按次序排队。
column5: 請按次序排隊。
column6: Qǐng àn cìxù páiduì.
column7: Please line up in order.
column9: The order in which people or things are lined up or taken: 按次序 (in order), 打亂次序 (mix up the order). 順序 is a near synonym and works for steps and procedures too.

column3: Waiting on someone and looking after their needs, as a servant would. Today it is used for caring for a sick relative, or jokingly for pampering someone; 难伺候 describes a picky person who is hard to please.
column4: 他每天都要伺候生病的母亲。
column5: 他每天都要伺候生病的母親。
column6: Tā měitiān dōu yào cìhou shēngbìng de mǔqin.
column7: He has to look after his sick mother every day.
column9: Waiting on someone and looking after their needs, as a servant would. Today it is used for caring for a sick relative, or jokingly for pampering someone; 難伺候 describes a picky person who is hard to please.

column3: A compliment for staying calm and not rushing under pressure, as in 从容不迫. It describes people and their manner, such as how someone answers questions or walks on stage. Taiwan reads the first syllable cōng.
column4: 她面对记者，从容地回答了每个问题。
column5: 她面對記者，從容地回答了每個問題。
column6: Tā miànduì jìzhě, cóngróng de huídá le měi gè wèntí.
column7: Facing the reporters, she answered every question calmly.
column9: A compliment for staying calm and not rushing under pressure, as in 從容不迫. It describes people and their manner, such as how someone answers questions or walks on stage. Taiwan reads the first syllable cōng.

column3: Mostly met inside words: 草丛 (a patch of grass), 树丛 (a clump of trees), 丛林 (a jungle), 丛书 (a book series). It is also a measure word for clumps: 一丛竹子 (a clump of bamboo).
column4: 他们走进了丛林。
column5: 他們走進了叢林。
column6: Tāmen zǒujìn le cóng lín.
column7: They walked into the jungle.
column9: Mostly met inside words: 草叢 (a patch of grass), 樹叢 (a clump of trees), 叢林 (a jungle), 叢書 (a book series). It is also a measure word for clumps: 一叢竹子 (a clump of bamboo).

column3: Casual and spoken. Often 凑合着 plus a verb (凑合着用, make do with it), and 还凑合 is a lukewarm answer to how something is, like "it's okay". The 凑 is also in 凑钱 (chip in) and 凑热闹 (join the fun).
column4: 这台旧电脑凑合能用。
column5: 這台舊電腦湊合能用。
column6: Zhè tái jiù diànnǎo còuhe néng yòng.
column7: This old computer is good enough to use.
column9: Casual and spoken. Often 湊合著 plus a verb (湊合著用, make do with it), and 還湊合 is a lukewarm answer to how something is, like "it's okay". The 湊 is also in 湊錢 (chip in) and 湊熱鬧 (join the fun).

column3: A criticism of someone's manner: how they speak, move or treat others (说话粗鲁, 动作粗鲁). It is stronger than just impolite; it suggests rough, uncouth behavior.
column4: 他说话很粗鲁，大家都不喜欢他。
column5: 他說話很粗魯，大家都不喜歡他。
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn cūlǔ, dàjiā dōu bù xǐhuan tā.
column7: He speaks very rudely, and nobody likes him.
column9: A criticism of someone's manner: how they speak, move or treat others (說話粗魯, 動作粗魯). It is stronger than just impolite; it suggests rough, uncouth behavior.

column3: Describes darting around in panic or without aim, said of animals or people: 乱窜 (run about wildly), 逃窜 (flee), 抱头鼠窜 (flee with head in hands). In 窜改 it means to tamper with a text or figures.
column4: 一只老鼠从厨房窜了出去。
column5: 一隻老鼠從廚房竄了出去。
column6: Yī zhī lǎoshǔ cóng chúfáng cuàn le chūqù.
column7: A mouse scurried out of the kitchen.
column9: Describes darting around in panic or without aim, said of animals or people: 亂竄 (run about wildly), 逃竄 (flee), 抱頭鼠竄 (flee with head in hands). In 竄改 it means to tamper with a text or figures.

column3: Always harmful. It goes with things that can be worn down by abuse or hardship: 身体, 健康, 精神, 花朵, or the young. A common pattern is 受到摧残 (suffer damage).
column4: 长期熬夜会摧残你的身体。
column5: 長期熬夜會摧殘你的身體。
column6: Chángqī áoyè huì cuīcán nǐ de shēntǐ.
column7: Staying up late for a long time will ruin your health.
column9: Always harmful. It goes with things that can be worn down by abuse or hardship: 身體, 健康, 精神, 花朵, or the young. A common pattern is 受到摧殘 (suffer damage).

column3: Said of what can easily be hurt or broken: feelings, health, a relationship, an economy, an ecosystem. A cracker or a glass is 脆 alone, not 脆弱; 脆弱 is more about weakness than crispness.
column4: 孩子的心很脆弱，需要多鼓励。
column5: 孩子的心很脆弱，需要多鼓勵。
column6: Háizi de xīn hěn cuìruò, xūyào duō gǔlì.
column7: A child's heart is fragile and needs a lot of encouragement.
column9: Said of what can easily be hurt or broken: feelings, health, a relationship, an economy, an ecosystem. A cracker or a glass is 脆 alone, not 脆弱; 脆弱 is more about weakness than crispness.

column3: A formal word for talks between parties such as governments, companies or unions, typically 进行磋商 or 与…磋商. It turns up in news reports and business writing, not in casual chat. 磋 on its own is an old word for polishing bone, horn or ivory into tools, and it is also a bound form meaning to deliberate.
column4: 双方将就价格问题进行磋商。
column5: 雙方將就價格問題進行磋商。
column6: Shuāngfāng jiāng jiù jiàgé wèntí jìnxíng cuōshāng.
column7: The two sides will hold talks on the price.
column9: A formal word for talks between parties such as governments, companies or unions, typically 進行磋商 or 與…磋商. It turns up in news reports and business writing, not in casual chat. 磋 on its own is an old word for polishing bone, horn or ivory into tools, and it is also a bound form meaning to deliberate.

column3: Students mostly meet it as 论文答辩, the oral defense of a thesis before a committee. In law it is the defendant's reply in court. The 辩 is the one in 辩论 (debate) and 辩护 (to defend in court).
column4: 她下周要参加论文答辩。
column5: 她下週要參加論文答辯。
column6: Tā xià zhōu yào cānjiā lùnwén dábiàn.
column7: She will defend her thesis next week.
column9: Students mostly meet it as 論文答辯, the oral defense of a thesis before a committee. In law it is the defendant's reply in court. The 辯 is the one in 辯論 (debate) and 辯護 (to defend in court).

column3: The object is usually a person (or a place, as in 打量四周), and the look is curious or wary, as in 上下打量 (look someone up and down). It is a different word from 测量, to measure. In speech it can also mean to suppose, as in 你打量我不知道吗.
column4: 他上下打量了我一番。
column5: 他上下打量了我一番。
column6: Tā shàngxià dǎliang le wǒ yī fān.
column7: He looked me up and down.
column9: The object is usually a person (or a place, as in 打量四周), and the look is curious or wary, as in 上下打量 (look someone up and down). It is a different word from 測量, to measure. In speech it can also mean to suppose, as in 你打量我不知道嗎.

column3: A verb plus its object, so other words can slip in between: 打了一天猎 (hunted all day). This 打 is the light "do" verb, as in 打球 and 打电话.
column4: 爷爷年轻时常去山里打猎。
column5: 爺爺年輕時常去山裡打獵。
column6: Yéye niánqīng shí cháng qù shān lǐ dǎliè.
column7: When Grandpa was young, he often went hunting in the mountains.
column9: A verb plus its object, so other words can slip in between: 打了一天獵 (hunted all day). This 打 is the light "do" verb, as in 打球 and 打電話.

column3: Two uses. As an adverb it is a shrug: 大不了重来 (at worst, start over). Negated, 没什么大不了 means it is no big deal. Here 不了 is the "can't" pattern, as in 受不了, used after 大.
column4: 大不了明天再试一次。
column5: 大不了明天再試一次。
column6: Dàbuliǎo míngtiān zài shì yī cì.
column7: At worst, we'll try again tomorrow.
column9: Two uses. As an adverb it is a shrug: 大不了重來 (at worst, start over). Negated, 沒什麼大不了 means it is no big deal. Here 不了 is the "can't" pattern, as in 受不了, used after 大.

column3: The minister of a monarchy: it fits imperial courts, historical dramas and countries with a king or emperor. A minister of today's Chinese government is a 部长.
column4: 皇帝听取了大臣的意见。
column5: 皇帝聽取了大臣的意見。
column6: Huángdì tīngqǔ le dàchén de yìjiàn.
column7: The emperor listened to his minister's opinion.
column9: The minister of a monarchy: it fits imperial courts, historical dramas and countries with a king or emperor. A minister of today's Chinese government is a 部長.

column3: A disapproving adverb in front of a verb: 大肆宣扬, 大肆破坏, 大肆挥霍. It is for bad or shameless acts, so you would not use it to praise someone. The 肆 also appears in 放肆 and 肆无忌惮.
column4: 有人大肆宣传这种假药。
column5: 有人大肆宣傳這種假藥。
column6: Yǒu rén dàsì xuānchuán zhè zhǒng jiǎyào.
column7: Some people are heavily promoting this fake medicine.
column9: A disapproving adverb in front of a verb: 大肆宣揚, 大肆破壞, 大肆揮霍. It is for bad or shameless acts, so you would not use it to praise someone. The 肆 also appears in 放肆 and 肆無忌憚.

column3: Usually 大体上, in front of a verb or adjective to sum up: 大体相同, 大体完成, 大体同意. It is also a noun for the big picture, in the phrase 识大体 (to see the big picture and be sensible).
column4: 这两份报告的内容大体相同。
column5: 這兩份報告的內容大體相同。
column6: Zhè liǎng fèn bàogào de nèiróng dàtǐ xiāngtóng.
column7: The content of these two reports is broadly the same.
column9: Usually 大體上, in front of a verb or adjective to sum up: 大體相同, 大體完成, 大體同意. It is also a noun for the big picture, in the phrase 識大體 (to see the big picture and be sensible).

column3: The word of news reports and police statements for violent criminals such as robbers and attackers (持刀歹徒, an armed thug). In everyday talk people say 坏人 instead.
column4: 歹徒持刀抢劫了一家银行。
column5: 歹徒持刀搶劫了一家銀行。
column6: Dǎitú chí dāo qiǎngjié le yī jiā yínháng.
column7: A thug with a knife robbed a bank.
column9: The word of news reports and police statements for violent criminals such as robbers and attackers (持刀歹徒, an armed thug). In everyday talk people say 壞人 instead.

column3: Two uses: neglecting one's duty (不敢怠慢, would not dare slack off), and a polite apology from a host, 怠慢了, for not looking after a guest well enough. A guest would not say it of themselves.
column4: 对不起，怠慢您了。
column5: 對不起，怠慢您了。
column6: Duìbuqǐ, dàimàn nín le.
column7: Sorry, I haven't looked after you properly.
column9: Two uses: neglecting one's duty (不敢怠慢, would not dare slack off), and a polite apology from a host, 怠慢了, for not looking after a guest well enough. A guest would not say it of themselves.

column3: A formal word from police reports and legal news: the police 逮捕 a suspect, who is then 被逮捕. In everyday speech people say 抓 or 抓住.
column4: 警察昨天逮捕了一名嫌疑人。
column5: 警察昨天逮捕了一名嫌疑人。
column6: Jǐngchá zuótiān dàibǔ le yī míng xiányírén.
column7: The police arrested a suspect yesterday.
column9: A formal word from police reports and legal news: the police 逮捕 a suspect, who is then 被逮捕. In everyday speech people say 抓 or 抓住.

column3: It describes a moment of nerves in front of something, often in advice like 别胆怯 or 不要胆怯. For a timid personality in general, 胆小 is the usual word. Taiwan reads the second syllable què.
column4: 他站在台上，一点也不胆怯。
column5: 他站在臺上，一點也不膽怯。
column6: Tā zhàn zài tái shàng, yīdiǎn yě bù dǎnqiè.
column7: He stood on the stage without a trace of fear.
column9: It describes a moment of nerves in front of something, often in advice like 別膽怯 or 不要膽怯. For a timid personality in general, 膽小 is the usual word. Taiwan reads the second syllable què.

column3: A formal, respectful word for the birthday of a revered person, especially in anniversaries like 诞辰一百周年. For your own or a friend's birthday, say 生日.
column4: 全国各地举行活动，纪念孔子诞辰。
column5: 全國各地舉行活動，紀念孔子誕辰。
column6: Quánguó gèdì jǔxíng huódòng, jìniàn Kǒngzǐ dànchén.
column7: Events were held across the country to mark the birthday of Confucius.
column9: A formal, respectful word for the birthday of a revered person, especially in anniversaries like 誕辰一百週年. For your own or a friend's birthday, say 生日.

column3: The opposite of 旺季. It is used for travel, hotels, shops and anything else with a slow season, and prices are often lower then. The same 季 appears in 雨季 and 旺季.
column4: 淡季的时候，机票和住宿都便宜很多。
column5: 淡季的時候，機票和住宿都便宜很多。
column6: Dànjì de shíhou, jīpiào hé zhùsù dōu piányi hěn duō.
column7: In the off season, flights and lodging are much cheaper.
column9: The opposite of 旺季. It is used for travel, hotels, shops and anything else with a slow season, and prices are often lower then. The same 季 appears in 雨季 and 旺季.

column3: Used in law, where it means the parties to a case (a lawyer's 当事人 is the client), and in everyday disputes for the person directly involved, as opposed to 旁观者, a bystander.
column4: 这件事要先听听当事人怎么说。
column5: 這件事要先聽聽當事人怎麼說。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yào xiān tīngtīng dāngshìrén zěnme shuō.
column7: First we should hear what the people involved have to say about it.
column9: Used in law, where it means the parties to a case (a lawyer's 當事人 is the client), and in everyday disputes for the person directly involved, as opposed to 旁觀者, a bystander.

column3: A set phrase of news and speeches, mostly in the pattern 当务之急是…: first comes the thing that cannot wait, then what to do about it. It can also follow a subject, as in 解决问题成了当务之急. The 之 in the middle is the literary equivalent of 的.
column4: 当务之急是先把受伤的人送到医院。
column5: 當務之急是先把受傷的人送到醫院。
column6: Dāngwùzhījí shì xiān bǎ shòushāng de rén sòng dào yīyuàn.
column7: The most urgent thing is to get the injured to the hospital first.
column9: A set phrase of news and speeches, mostly in the pattern 當務之急是…: first comes the thing that cannot wait, then what to do about it. It can also follow a subject, as in 解決問題成了當務之急. The 之 in the middle is the literary equivalent of 的.

column3: It goes with 高, 中 and 低 (高档 is high-end), and 有档次 or 提高档次 praise or raise the quality of a product, hotel, restaurant or even a person's taste. Taiwan reads 档 dǎng.
column4: 这家餐厅很有档次，价格也不便宜。
column5: 這家餐廳很有檔次，價格也不便宜。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn yǒu dàngcì, jiàgé yě bù piányi.
column7: This restaurant is classy, and the prices are not cheap either.
column9: It goes with 高, 中 and 低 (高檔 is high-end), and 有檔次 or 提高檔次 praise or raise the quality of a product, hotel, restaurant or even a person's taste. Taiwan reads 檔 dǎng.

column3: The usual verbs are 发射 (launch) and 拦截 (intercept). 弹 here is the shell or bullet, as in 子弹 and 炸弹. In Taiwan 飞弹 is the common word.
column4: 军队试射了一枚新型导弹。
column5: 軍隊試射了一枚新型導彈。
column6: Jūnduì shìshè le yī méi xīnxíng dǎodàn.
column7: The army test-fired a new type of missile.
column9: The usual verbs are 發射 (launch) and 攔截 (intercept). 彈 here is the shell or bullet, as in 子彈 and 炸彈. In Taiwan 飛彈 is the common word.

column3: In daily life it is mostly the navigation app in a phone or car: 开导航, 用导航. On websites 导航栏 is the navigation bar. The 航 is the same as in 航班 and 航空, where it means traveling by ship or plane.
column4: 开着导航走，不会迷路。
column5: 開著導航走，不會迷路。
column6: Kāizhe dǎoháng zǒu, bù huì mílù.
column7: If you go with the navigation on, you will not get lost.
column9: In daily life it is mostly the navigation app in a phone or car: 開導航, 用導航. On websites 導航欄 is the navigation bar. The 航 is the same as in 航班 and 航空, where it means traveling by ship or plane.

column3: Formal and often abstract. After a noun it makes an 'X-oriented' phrase, as in 市场导向 and 结果导向; as a verb it means steering things toward some outcome, as in 导向成功.
column4: 公司的政策以市场为导向。
column5: 公司的政策以市場為導向。
column6: Gōngsī de zhèngcè yǐ shìchǎng wéi dǎoxiàng.
column7: The company's policy is market-oriented.
column9: Formal and often abstract. After a noun it makes an 'X-oriented' phrase, as in 市場導向 and 結果導向; as a verb it means steering things toward some outcome, as in 導向成功.

column3: A verb with its object built in, so it can be split, as in 捣什么乱 and 捣了半天乱; 别捣乱 is the everyday warning. It suits children, pets and unwanted helpers who get in the way, on purpose or not; it is milder than 破坏 (to wreck).
column4: 孩子们在教室里捣乱，老师很生气。
column5: 孩子們在教室裡搗亂，老師很生氣。
column6: Háizimen zài jiàoshì lǐ dǎoluàn, lǎoshī hěn shēngqì.
column7: The children were causing trouble in the classroom, and the teacher was angry.
column9: A verb with its object built in, so it can be split, as in 搗什麼亂 and 搗了半天亂; 別搗亂 is the everyday warning. It suits children, pets and unwanted helpers who get in the way, on purpose or not; it is milder than 破壞 (to wreck).

column3: A formal word from law and crime reports: 盗窃罪 is the crime of theft and 盗窃案 a theft case. In everyday speech people say 偷.
column4: 他因盗窃被判了两年。
column5: 他因盜竊被判了兩年。
column6: Tā yīn dàoqiè bèi pàn le liǎng nián.
column7: He was sentenced to two years for theft.
column9: A formal word from law and crime reports: 盜竊罪 is the crime of theft and 盜竊案 a theft case. In everyday speech people say 偷.

column3: Once the husks are removed, the rice is 大米. The rice plant itself is 水稻, and harvested grain in general is 谷物.
column4: 农民把刚收割的稻谷晒在院子里。
column5: 農民把剛收割的稻穀曬在院子裡。
column6: Nóngmín bǎ gāng shōugē de dàogǔ shài zài yuànzi lǐ.
column7: The farmers spread the freshly harvested rice to dry in the yard.
column9: Once the husks are removed, the rice is 大米. The rice plant itself is 水稻, and harvested grain in general is 穀物.

column3: Mostly a verdict or warning at the end of a sentence: 为了…而…，那就得不偿失了. It is said of a choice that looks like a saving or a win but costs more than it gains, in speech and in writing.
column4: 为了省钱买了便宜货，结果两天就坏了，真是得不偿失。
column5: 為了省錢買了便宜貨，結果兩天就壞了，真是得不償失。
column6: Wèile shěng qián mǎi le piányi huò, jiéguǒ liǎng tiān jiù huài le, zhēn shì débùchángshī.
column7: I bought a cheap one to save money, and it broke in two days. It was not worth it.
column9: Mostly a verdict or warning at the end of a sentence: 為了…而…，那就得不償失了. It is said of a choice that looks like a saving or a win but costs more than it gains, in speech and in writing.

column3: It usually describes the people who do your work well, mainly in 得力助手 (right-hand man) and 得力干将. For measures and management, 得力 can also say they work well, as in 措施得力.
column4: 他是老板最得力的助手。
column5: 他是老闆最得力的助手。
column6: Tā shì lǎobǎn zuì délì de zhùshǒu.
column7: He is the boss's most capable assistant.
column9: It usually describes the people who do your work well, mainly in 得力助手 (right-hand man) and 得力幹將. For measures and management, 得力 can also say they work well, as in 措施得力.

column3: Always praise, for a place's natural conditions or a person's gifts and background: 得天独厚的自然条件, or after a subject, 地理位置得天独厚. It reads as heaven alone being generous to it, not as plain luck.
column4: 这个地方气候温和，土壤肥沃，自然条件得天独厚。
column5: 這個地方氣候溫和，土壤肥沃，自然條件得天獨厚。
column6: Zhège dìfang qìhòu wēnhé, tǔrǎng féiwò, zìrán tiáojiàn détiāndúhòu.
column7: This place has a mild climate and rich soil: nature has been exceptionally kind to it.
column9: Always praise, for a place's natural conditions or a person's gifts and background: 得天獨厚的自然條件, or after a subject, 地理位置得天獨厚. It reads as heaven alone being generous to it, not as plain luck.

column3: Red lanterns are hung for the Spring Festival, and lantern displays are the heart of the Lantern Festival; the verbs are 挂 (hang) and 提 (carry). The 笼 is the same as in 鸟笼 and 蒸笼: a frame that wraps around what is inside.
column4: 过年的时候，家家户户都挂起了红灯笼。
column5: 過年的時候，家家戶戶都掛起了紅燈籠。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, jiājiāhùhù dōu guà qǐ le hóng dēnglóng.
column7: At New Year, every household hangs up red lanterns.
column9: Red lanterns are hung for the Spring Festival, and lantern displays are the heart of the Lantern Festival; the verbs are 掛 (hang) and 提 (carry). The 籠 is the same as in 鳥籠 and 蒸籠: a frame that wraps around what is inside.

column3: Typhoons and troops 登陆 on a coast, and a product or app can 登陆 a new market. For logging in to an account the standard word is 登录 (in Taiwan, 登入), though 登陆 is often seen online.
column4: 台风今天下午将在福建沿海登陆。
column5: 颱風今天下午將在福建沿海登陸。
column6: Táifēng jīntiān xiàwǔ jiāng zài Fújiàn yánhǎi dēnglù.
column7: The typhoon will make landfall on the Fujian coast this afternoon.
column9: Typhoons and troops 登陸 on a coast, and a product or app can 登陸 a new market. For logging in to an account the standard word is 登錄 (in Taiwan, 登入), though 登陸 is often seen online.

column3: It is the foot pushing hard against something: pedaling (蹬自行车), kicking off the covers (蹬被子), or pushing off a wall. Taiwan reads it dèng.
column4: 他蹬着自行车往前冲。
column5: 他蹬著自行車往前衝。
column6: Tā dēng zhe zìxíngchē wǎng qián chōng.
column7: He pedaled his bicycle and shot forward.
column9: It is the foot pushing hard against something: pedaling (蹬自行車), kicking off the covers (蹬被子), or pushing off a wall. Taiwan reads it dèng.

column3: Two common uses: 瞪大眼睛 (open the eyes wide, in surprise) and 瞪+person+一眼 (glare at someone briefly, in anger or warning).
column4: 她瞪了我一眼，什么也没说。
column5: 她瞪了我一眼，什麼也沒說。
column6: Tā dèng le wǒ yī yǎn, shénme yě méi shuō.
column7: She glared at me and said nothing.
column9: Two common uses: 瞪大眼睛 (open the eyes wide, in surprise) and 瞪+person+一眼 (glare at someone briefly, in anger or warning).

column3: A collective word for flood-control works. 堤 runs along the bank to keep a river in, while 坝 blocks the river itself, as in 水坝. The common verbs are 修建 and 加固. Taiwan reads 堤 as tí, so the word is tíbà there.
column4: 暴雨过后，工人们加固了河边的堤坝。
column5: 暴雨過後，工人們加固了河邊的堤壩。
column6: Bàoyǔ guòhòu, gōngrénmen jiāgù le hébiān de dībà.
column7: After the heavy rain, workers reinforced the dikes and dams by the river.
column9: A collective word for flood-control works. 堤 runs along the bank to keep a river in, while 壩 blocks the river itself, as in 水壩. The common verbs are 修建 and 加固. Taiwan reads 堤 as tí, so the word is tíbà there.

column3: It takes a person, group or country as its object, or works in 互相敌视 and 敌视的目光. It is a serious, negative word for open hostility, far stronger than just not liking someone.
column4: 他们两家互相敌视了很多年。
column5: 他們兩家互相敵視了很多年。
column6: Tāmen liǎng jiā hùxiāng díshì le hěn duō nián.
column7: The two families were hostile to each other for many years.
column9: It takes a person, group or country as its object, or works in 互相敵視 and 敵視的目光. It is a serious, negative word for open hostility, far stronger than just not liking someone.

column3: It covers boycotts of products or countries (抵制日货), and also resisting things seen as bad, as in 抵制诱惑 (resist temptation) and 抵制不良风气. The object is usually something harmful or unwelcome.
column4: 许多消费者抵制这个品牌的产品。
column5: 許多消費者抵制這個品牌的產品。
column6: Xǔduō xiāofèizhě dǐzhì zhège pǐnpái de chǎnpǐn.
column7: Many consumers are boycotting this brand's products.
column9: It covers boycotts of products or countries (抵制日貨), and also resisting things seen as bad, as in 抵制誘惑 (resist temptation) and 抵制不良風氣. The object is usually something harmful or unwelcome.

column3: It almost always sits in 到了…的地步 or 落到这个地步, for the degree something has reached, usually a bad one. Even a good outcome gets the pattern when it is surprisingly far: 好到这种地步.
column4: 事情已经到了无法挽回的地步。
column5: 事情已經到了無法挽回的地步。
column6: Shìqing yǐjīng dào le wúfǎ wǎnhuí de dìbù.
column7: Things have reached the point where they cannot be undone.
column9: It almost always sits in 到了…的地步 or 落到這個地步, for the degree something has reached, usually a bad one. Even a good outcome gets the pattern when it is surprisingly far: 好到這種地步.

column3: It is followed by a description of how the ground lies: 地势平坦 (flat), 地势险要 (rugged and strategic) or 地势低洼 (low-lying, so floods are a risk). The word is about height and slope, not the place itself.
column4: 这里地势平坦，适合种水稻。
column5: 這裡地勢平坦，適合種水稻。
column6: Zhèlǐ dìshì píngtǎn, shìhé zhòng shuǐdào.
column7: The land here is flat and suits rice growing.
column9: It is followed by a description of how the ground lies: 地勢平坦 (flat), 地勢險要 (rugged and strategic) or 地勢低窪 (low-lying, so floods are a risk). The word is about height and slope, not the place itself.

column3: A technical word for what the ground and rock under a place are like. It comes up in 地质条件 (the ground conditions), 地质灾害 (landslides and the like) and 地质学 (the science).
column4: 这个地区的地质条件很复杂。
column5: 這個地區的地質條件很複雜。
column6: Zhège dìqū de dìzhì tiáojiàn hěn fùzá.
column7: The ground conditions in this area are very complicated.
column9: A technical word for what the ground and rock under a place are like. It comes up in 地質條件 (the ground conditions), 地質災害 (landslides and the like) and 地質學 (the science).

column3: Used for figures that go up step by step in a regular way, often with 逐年 or 逐月 before it, or in 递增数列 (an increasing sequence). Its opposite is 递减.
column4: 公司的利润逐年递增。
column5: 公司的利潤逐年遞增。
column6: Gōngsī de lìrùn zhúnián dìzēng.
column7: The company's profits grow year after year.
column9: Used for figures that go up step by step in a regular way, often with 逐年 or 逐月 before it, or in 遞增數列 (an increasing sequence). Its opposite is 遞減.

column3: The one being shaken is the vehicle, boat, plane or its passengers: 车子颠簸, 颠簸了一路. Said of a hard life, it means one full of ups and downs. On its own, 簸 means to toss something up and down, as in winnowing grain.
column4: 山路很不平，车子颠簸得很厉害。
column5: 山路很不平，車子顛簸得很厲害。
column6: Shānlù hěn bùpíng, chēzi diānbǒ de hěn lìhai.
column7: The mountain road is very uneven, and the car bounced around a lot.
column9: The one being shaken is the vehicle, boat, plane or its passengers: 車子顛簸, 顛簸了一路. Said of a hard life, it means one full of ups and downs. On its own, 簸 means to toss something up and down, as in winnowing grain.

column3: Used for flipping something over or reversing an order: 上下颠倒, 颠倒顺序. In set phrases it describes a confused mind: 颠倒是非 (to twist right and wrong), 神魂颠倒 (to be head over heels).
column4: 这幅画挂颠倒了。
column5: 這幅畫掛顛倒了。
column6: Zhè fú huà guà diāndǎo le.
column7: This painting is hung upside down.
column9: Used for flipping something over or reversing an order: 上下顛倒, 顛倒順序. In set phrases it describes a confused mind: 顛倒是非 (to twist right and wrong), 神魂顛倒 (to be head over heels).

column3: Small touches added here and there to a plainer background: 湖边点缀着几座小亭子. It also describes something that is there only for show: 只是个点缀.
column4: 湖边点缀着几座小亭子。
column5: 湖邊點綴著幾座小亭子。
column6: Húbiān diǎnzhuì zhe jǐ zuò xiǎo tíngzi.
column7: A few small pavilions dot the lakeside.
column9: Small touches added here and there to a plainer background: 湖邊點綴著幾座小亭子. It also describes something that is there only for show: 只是個點綴.

column3: A warm, everyday word, usually as 惦记着: a person who is away or a matter left unfinished stays on your mind. It can also mean having your eye on something that is someone else's: 惦记别人的东西.
column4: 出门在外，我总惦记着家里的父母。
column5: 出門在外，我總惦記著家裡的父母。
column6: Chūmén zàiwài, wǒ zǒng diànjì zhe jiālǐ de fùmǔ.
column7: Away from home, I am always thinking of my parents.
column9: A warm, everyday word, usually as 惦記著: a person who is away or a matter left unfinished stays on your mind. It can also mean having your eye on something that is someone else's: 惦記別人的東西.

column3: A written, formal word with an abstract object, nearly always 基础 (a foundation): 奠定基础, 奠定地位. The subject is what gets the credit: a study, a victory or a reform that laid the groundwork for what followed.
column4: 他的研究为这门学科奠定了基础。
column5: 他的研究為這門學科奠定了基礎。
column6: Tā de yánjiū wèi zhè mén xuékē diàndìng le jīchǔ.
column7: His research laid the foundation for this field.
column9: A written, formal word with an abstract object, nearly always 基礎 (a foundation): 奠定基礎, 奠定地位. The subject is what gets the credit: a study, a victory or a reform that laid the groundwork for what followed.

column3: Usually 叼着: holding something in the mouth without chewing it, such as a cigarette, a pen, or a cat carrying a mouse. If you bite into it, say 咬.
column4: 小狗叼着一根骨头跑了。
column5: 小狗叼著一根骨頭跑了。
column6: Xiǎogǒu diāo zhe yī gēn gǔtou pǎo le.
column7: The puppy ran off with a bone in its mouth.
column9: Usually 叼著: holding something in the mouth without chewing it, such as a cigarette, a pen, or a cat carrying a mouse. If you bite into it, say 咬.

column3: Covers both carved and modeled works, whether it is a statue in a square or the art as a whole. The same 塑 turns up in 塑料 (plastic) and 塑造 (to shape a character or an image).
column4: 广场中央有一座巨大的雕塑。
column5: 廣場中央有一座巨大的雕塑。
column6: Guǎngchǎng zhōngyāng yǒu yī zuò jùdà de diāosù.
column7: In the middle of the square stands a huge sculpture.
column9: Covers both carved and modeled works, whether it is a statue in a square or the art as a whole. The same 塑 turns up in 塑料 (plastic) and 塑造 (to shape a character or an image).

column3: Said by someone who cares or has authority, such as a parent, a teacher or a doctor, usually before the listener goes off to do something. It is followed by what to do or avoid: 叮嘱他路上小心. On its own, 叮 also means to sting or bite, as a mosquito does.
column4: 临走前，妈妈再三叮嘱我路上要小心。
column5: 臨走前，媽媽再三叮囑我路上要小心。
column6: Línzǒu qián, māma zàisān dīngzhǔ wǒ lùshang yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Before I left, Mom told me again and again to be careful on the road.
column9: Said by someone who cares or has authority, such as a parent, a teacher or a doctor, usually before the listener goes off to do something. It is followed by what to do or avoid: 叮囑他路上小心. On its own, 叮 also means to sting or bite, as a mosquito does.

column3: As a noun it goes with 下: 下定义 means to give a definition. As a verb it takes an object, often with 为 or 成: 把它定义为…….
column4: 每个人对成功的定义都不一样。
column5: 每個人對成功的定義都不一樣。
column6: Měi gè rén duì chénggōng de dìngyì dōu bù yīyàng.
column7: Everyone defines success differently.
column9: As a noun it goes with 下: 下定義 means to give a definition. As a verb it takes an object, often with 為 or 成: 把它定義為…….

column3: Said about a person, usually as mild criticism or teasing, for someone who keeps losing things or forgetting them. The 三 and 四 are not counts: they just mean one thing after another. Here 落 is read là, meaning to leave something behind, not luò as in falling.
column4: 他总是丢三落四，出门老忘带钥匙。
column5: 他總是丟三落四，出門老忘帶鑰匙。
column6: Tā zǒngshì diūsānlàsì, chūmén lǎo wàng dài yàoshi.
column7: He is always forgetting things and keeps leaving his keys at home.
column9: Said about a person, usually as mild criticism or teasing, for someone who keeps losing things or forgetting them. The 三 and 四 are not counts: they just mean one thing after another. Here 落 is read là, meaning to leave something behind, not luò as in falling.

column3: Both for a person who treats guests and for a country or city hosting a big event: 东道主国家, 东道主队. On its own 东 can mean host, as in 做东 (to treat) and 房东 (landlord).
column4: 作为东道主，我们一定会好好招待各位客人。
column5: 作為東道主，我們一定會好好招待各位客人。
column6: Zuòwéi dōngdàozhǔ, wǒmen yīdìng huì hǎohāo zhāodài gèwèi kèrén.
column7: As the host, we will certainly take good care of all our guests.
column9: Both for a person who treats guests and for a country or city hosting a big event: 東道主國家, 東道主隊. On its own 東 can mean host, as in 做東 (to treat) and 房東 (landlord).

column3: Describes looking around, often idly or with a wandering mind: a pupil in class, a child in a crowd, someone nervous or lost. Said to a person who should be paying attention, it is a mild reproach.
column4: 上课的时候不要东张西望。
column5: 上課的時候不要東張西望。
column6: Shàngkè de shíhou bùyào dōngzhāngxīwàng.
column7: Don't look around during class.
column9: Describes looking around, often idly or with a wandering mind: a pupil in class, a child in a crowd, someone nervous or lost. Said to a person who should be paying attention, it is a mild reproach.

column3: The head of the 董事会 (board). The 总经理 runs the daily business, so the two are not the same job. People often call the chairman by surname plus 董, as in 王董.
column4: 董事长在会上宣布了新的计划。
column5: 董事長在會上宣布了新的計畫。
column6: Dǒngshìzhǎng zài huì shàng xuānbù le xīn de jìhuà.
column7: The chairman announced a new plan at the meeting.
column9: The head of the 董事會 (board). The 總經理 runs the daily business, so the two are not the same job. People often call the chairman by surname plus 董, as in 王董.

column3: Said of something that should be steady but is not: a society, a region, a market, an era (动荡的年代), often with 不安. For a bumpy ride, say 颠簸.
column4: 那是一个社会动荡的年代。
column5: 那是一個社會動盪的年代。
column6: Nà shì yī gè shèhuì dòngdàng de niándài.
column7: That was an age of social turmoil.
column9: Said of something that should be steady but is not: a society, a region, a market, an era (動盪的年代), often with 不安. For a bumpy ride, say 顛簸.

column3: Mostly the smallest sign that something is going on, a sound or a stir, and usually heard in the negative: 一点动静也没有. 听到动静 means to hear something happening.
column4: 屋里一点动静也没有。
column5: 屋裡一點動靜也沒有。
column6: Wūlǐ yīdiǎn dòngjìng yě méiyǒu.
column7: There isn't a sound from inside the room.
column9: Mostly the smallest sign that something is going on, a sound or a stir, and usually heard in the negative: 一點動靜也沒有. 聽到動靜 means to hear something happening.

column3: Pairs with 静脉 (vein). It is also figurative: a main road, railway or river is called a 大动脉, the artery of a region's transport.
column4: 医生说他的动脉有点硬化。
column5: 醫生說他的動脈有點硬化。
column6: Yīshēng shuō tā de dòngmài yǒudiǎn yìnghuà.
column7: The doctor says his arteries have hardened a little.
column9: Pairs with 靜脈 (vein). It is also figurative: a main road, railway or river is called a 大動脈, the artery of a region's transport.

column3: Used of water or a river that freezes over, but mostly figuratively, in news and banking: 冻结账户, 冻结资产, 冻结工资, 冻结招聘. What is frozen stays as it is and cannot be touched.
column4: 银行已经冻结了他的账户。
column5: 銀行已經凍結了他的帳戶。
column6: Yínháng yǐjīng dòngjié le tā de zhànghù.
column7: The bank has already frozen his account.
column9: Used of water or a river that freezes over, but mostly figuratively, in news and banking: 凍結帳戶, 凍結資產, 凍結工資, 凍結招聘. What is frozen stays as it is and cannot be touched.

column3: A busy little word. 兜圈子 is to go in circles or to talk around the point, 兜风 is to go for a spin, and 衣兜 and 裤兜 are pockets, a colloquial word beside 口袋.
column4: 别兜圈子了，有话直说吧。
column5: 別兜圈子了，有話直說吧。
column6: Bié dōu quānzi le, yǒu huà zhí shuō ba.
column7: Stop beating around the bush and just say it.
column9: A busy little word. 兜圈子 is to go in circles or to talk around the point, 兜風 is to go for a spin, and 衣兜 and 褲兜 are pockets, a colloquial word beside 口袋.

column3: Seen from the climber's side: a slope, cliff, mountain path or flight of stairs that is hard to go up. 陡 alone also means suddenly, as in 陡然.
column4: 这条山路非常陡峭，走起来很费力。
column5: 這條山路非常陡峭，走起來很費力。
column6: Zhè tiáo shānlù fēicháng dǒuqiào, zǒu qǐlái hěn fèilì.
column7: This mountain path is very steep and hard going.
column9: Seen from the climber's side: a slope, cliff, mountain path or flight of stairs that is hard to go up. 陡 alone also means suddenly, as in 陡然.

column3: A person with authority or a stake keeps pushing someone to do or finish a task. The one urged is the object, and the task follows: 督促孩子写作业. Officials also use it for institutions: 督促企业整改.
column4: 妈妈每天督促孩子按时完成作业。
column5: 媽媽每天督促孩子按時完成作業。
column6: Māma měitiān dūcù háizi ànshí wánchéng zuòyè.
column7: Every day Mom makes sure her child finishes the homework on time.
column9: A person with authority or a stake keeps pushing someone to do or finish a task. The one urged is the object, and the task follows: 督促孩子寫作業. Officials also use it for institutions: 督促企業整改.

column3: A political word with a negative tone: 独裁者, 独裁政权, with 民主 as its opposite. It can also describe a boss or parent who decides everything alone: 他很独裁. The 裁 that means decide is the one in 裁判 (referee) and 裁决 (ruling).
column4: 这个国家长期处于独裁统治之下。
column5: 這個國家長期處於獨裁統治之下。
column6: Zhège guójiā chángqī chǔyú dúcái tǒngzhì zhī xià.
column7: The country lived under a dictatorship for a long time.
column9: A political word with a negative tone: 獨裁者, 獨裁政權, with 民主 as its opposite. It can also describe a boss or parent who decides everything alone: 他很獨裁. The 裁 that means decide is the one in 裁判 (referee) and 裁決 (ruling).

column3: A written word for a blockage in a road, pipe or blood vessel: 交通堵塞, 血管堵塞. In speech a traffic jam is 堵车 on the mainland and 塞车 in Taiwan. It also appears in 堵塞漏洞, to close a loophole. In this word 塞 is read sè, but it is sāi when it means to stuff something in.
column4: 因为下雨，市中心的交通严重堵塞。
column5: 因為下雨，市中心的交通嚴重堵塞。
column6: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, shì zhōngxīn de jiāotōng yánzhòng dǔsè.
column7: Because of the rain, traffic in the city center is badly jammed.
column9: A written word for a blockage in a road, pipe or blood vessel: 交通堵塞, 血管堵塞. In speech a traffic jam is 堵車 on the mainland and 塞車 in Taiwan. It also appears in 堵塞漏洞, to close a loophole. In this word 塞 is read sè, but it is sāi when it means to stuff something in.

column3: Formal, for slogans, policies and rules. The object is always something bad, such as waste, cheating or fake goods, and the aim is to stop it for good: 杜绝浪费, 杜绝后患.
column4: 学校采取措施，杜绝考试作弊。
column5: 學校採取措施，杜絕考試作弊。
column6: Xuéxiào cǎiqǔ cuòshī, dùjué kǎoshì zuòbì.
column7: The school is taking measures to stamp out cheating on exams.
column9: Formal, for slogans, policies and rules. The object is always something bad, such as waste, cheating or fake goods, and the aim is to stop it for good: 杜絕浪費, 杜絕後患.

column3: It describes looks, posture and character alike: 五官端正 for regular features, 坐姿端正 for sitting up straight, 品行端正 for good conduct. As a verb it means to straighten out, as in 端正态度 (to fix one's attitude).
column4: 他坐得很端正。
column5: 他坐得很端正。
column6: Tā zuò de hěn duānzhèng.
column7: He sits very straight.
column9: It describes looks, posture and character alike: 五官端正 for regular features, 坐姿端正 for sitting up straight, 品行端正 for good conduct. As a verb it means to straighten out, as in 端正態度 (to fix one's attitude).

column3: It describes things that are brief and sharp, with a rushed or abrupt feel: 呼吸短促 (short, gasping breaths), 短促的铃声 (a quick ring), 时间短促 (not enough time). It is not used for a short object or a short person.
column4: 他跑了很远，呼吸变得很短促。
column5: 他跑了很遠，呼吸變得很短促。
column6: Tā pǎo le hěn yuǎn, hūxī biàn de hěn duǎncù.
column7: He ran a long way, and his breathing became short and quick.
column9: It describes things that are brief and sharp, with a rushed or abrupt feel: 呼吸短促 (short, gasping breaths), 短促的鈴聲 (a quick ring), 時間短促 (not enough time). It is not used for a short object or a short person.

column3: A firm conclusion drawn from evidence or reasoning, stronger than 认为 (to think). It is very often negated, as in 无法断定 or 不能断定, to say that something cannot be known for sure yet. 断 is built from a part meaning to cut and an axe 斤.
column4: 现在还不能断定他是不是说谎。
column5: 現在還不能斷定他是不是說謊。
column6: Xiànzài hái bù néng duàndìng tā shì bù shì shuōhuǎng.
column7: We can't yet say for sure whether he is lying.
column9: A firm conclusion drawn from evidence or reasoning, stronger than 認為 (to think). It is very often negated, as in 無法斷定 or 不能斷定, to say that something cannot be known for sure yet. 斷 is built from a part meaning to cut and an axe 斤.

column3: Mostly for cutting off relationships or supplies, not for snapping a physical thing: 断绝关系 (to cut ties), 断绝来往, 断绝经济来源, 水电被断绝. For a rope or a line, say 断 or 剪断. 绝 began as a knife cutting silk threads.
column4: 他和家里断绝了关系。
column5: 他和家裡斷絕了關係。
column6: Tā hé jiālǐ duànjué le guānxì.
column7: He cut off all ties with his family.
column9: Mostly for cutting off relationships or supplies, not for snapping a physical thing: 斷絕關係 (to cut ties), 斷絕來往, 斷絕經濟來源, 水電被斷絕. For a rope or a line, say 斷 or 剪斷. 絕 began as a knife cutting silk threads.

column3: It suits things that build up gradually, often unwanted: 垃圾, 灰尘, 积雪, 工作 or 问题 堆积. Unlike 堆, which is also the plain verb for stacking something yourself, 堆积 is about the result of buildup. It also works as a noun, and 堆积如山 means piled up like a mountain.
column4: 路边堆积着很多垃圾。
column5: 路邊堆積著很多垃圾。
column6: Lùbiān duījī zhe hěn duō lājī.
column7: A lot of garbage has piled up by the road.
column9: It suits things that build up gradually, often unwanted: 垃圾, 灰塵, 積雪, 工作 or 問題 堆積. Unlike 堆, which is also the plain verb for stacking something yourself, 堆積 is about the result of buildup. It also works as a noun, and 堆積如山 means piled up like a mountain.

column3: It works as an adjective or a noun: 左右对称 is left-right symmetry, 轴对称 is symmetry about an axis. The opposite is 不对称, which also turns up figuratively in 信息不对称, where one side knows more than the other. Taiwan reads 称 chèng in this word, not chèn.
column4: 人的身体是左右对称的。
column5: 人的身體是左右對稱的。
column6: Rén de shēntǐ shì zuǒyòu duìchèn de.
column7: The human body is left-right symmetrical.
column9: It works as an adjective or a noun: 左右對稱 is left-right symmetry, 軸對稱 is symmetry about an axis. The opposite is 不對稱, which also turns up figuratively in 信息不對稱, where one side knows more than the other. Taiwan reads 稱 chèng in this word, not chèn.

column3: Couplets are hung on both sides of a door or gate, most famously in black or gold on red paper at Chinese New Year (the New Year kind is called 春联). The two lines match word for word, with the same length and each word paired with one of the same kind.
column4: 过年的时候，家家户户都贴对联。
column5: 過年的時候，家家戶戶都貼對聯。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, jiājiā hùhù dōu tiē duìlián.
column7: At New Year, every household puts up couplets.
column9: Couplets are hung on both sides of a door or gate, most famously in black or gold on red paper at Chinese New Year (the New Year kind is called 春聯). The two lines match word for word, with the same length and each word paired with one of the same kind.

column3: It has two common uses: laying two things side by side to check or compare, as in 中英对照 (Chinese and English side by side) and 对照原文 (check against the original), and a contrast that makes a difference stand out, as in 形成鲜明对照.
column4: 请把名单和身份证对照一下。
column5: 請把名單和身分證對照一下。
column6: Qǐng bǎ míngdān hé shēnfènzhèng duìzhào yīxià.
column7: Please check the list against the ID.
column9: It has two common uses: laying two things side by side to check or compare, as in 中英對照 (Chinese and English side by side) and 對照原文 (check against the original), and a contrast that makes a difference stand out, as in 形成鮮明對照.

column3: Today it is used mostly in the figurative sense: a promise, pledge or prize is "paid out" as 兑现承诺, 兑现诺言, 兑现奖金. A broken promise is 不兑现 or 无法兑现, and cashing a check is the literal use.
column4: 公司承诺的奖金一直没有兑现。
column5: 公司承諾的獎金一直沒有兌現。
column6: Gōngsī chéngnuò de jiǎngjīn yīzhí méiyǒu duìxiàn.
column7: The bonus the company promised has never been paid.
column9: Today it is used mostly in the figurative sense: a promise, pledge or prize is "paid out" as 兌現承諾, 兌現諾言, 兌現獎金. A broken promise is 不兌現 or 無法兌現, and cashing a check is the literal use.

column3: A narrative adverb for a reaction or change that happens in an instant: 顿时安静了, 顿时明白了. Because it reports what happened, it can't go in a request or command, where you would use 马上 or 立刻.
column4: 听到这个消息，大家顿时安静了下来。
column5: 聽到這個消息，大家頓時安靜了下來。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā dùnshí ānjìng le xiàlai.
column7: On hearing the news, everyone instantly fell silent.
column9: A narrative adverb for a reaction or change that happens in an instant: 頓時安靜了, 頓時明白了. Because it reports what happened, it can't go in a request or command, where you would use 馬上 or 立刻.

column3: Common in news and business for society, culture, the economy or a market: 经济多元化, 文化多元化, 多元化经营 (a diversified business). It works as a verb or an adjective, and it sounds positive, like a society open to many views.
column4: 这座城市的文化越来越多元化。
column5: 這座城市的文化越來越多元化。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì de wénhuà yuè lái yuè duōyuánhuà.
column7: This city's culture is becoming more and more diverse.
column9: Common in news and business for society, culture, the economy or a market: 經濟多元化, 文化多元化, 多元化經營 (a diversified business). It works as a verb or an adjective, and it sounds positive, like a society open to many views.

column3: A spoken word, usually with 打: 打哆嗦 or 打了个哆嗦 for a shiver from cold, fear or nerves. 哆哆嗦嗦 describes shaking that keeps going, as of a trembling voice or hands.
column4: 天太冷了，他冻得直打哆嗦。
column5: 天太冷了，他凍得直打哆嗦。
column6: Tiān tài lěng le, tā dòng de zhí dǎ duōsuo.
column7: It was so cold that he kept shivering.
column9: A spoken word, usually with 打: 打哆嗦 or 打了個哆嗦 for a shiver from cold, fear or nerves. 哆哆嗦嗦 describes shaking that keeps going, as of a trembling voice or hands.

column3: Moral or personal decline, such as sliding into gambling, drugs or a wasted life: 自甘堕落 (to sink willingly), 堕落的生活. It is not used for a literal fall; for a plane or an object coming down, use 坠落.
column4: 他整天赌博，越来越堕落。
column5: 他整天賭博，越來越墮落。
column6: Tā zhěngtiān dǔbó, yuè lái yuè duòluò.
column7: He gambles all day and sinks lower and lower.
column9: Moral or personal decline, such as sliding into gambling, drugs or a wasted life: 自甘墮落 (to sink willingly), 墮落的生活. It is not used for a literal fall; for a plane or an object coming down, use 墜落.

column3: Extra in the sense of beyond what was set or agreed: 额外费用 is a charge not in the price, 额外收入 is side income. It goes before a noun (usually with 的) or before a verb, as in 额外付费.
column4: 这次旅行没有额外费用。
column5: 這次旅行沒有額外費用。
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng méiyǒu éwài fèiyòng.
column7: This trip has no extra charges.
column9: Extra in the sense of beyond what was set or agreed: 額外費用 is a charge not in the price, 額外收入 is side income. It goes before a noun (usually with 的) or before a verb, as in 額外付費.

column3: Used for conditions getting worse: 病情恶化 (an illness), 关系恶化, 环境恶化, 局势恶化. The opposite is 好转. It can also take an object, as in 恶化了两国关系. 恶 is also read wù when it means to hate.
column4: 他的病情突然恶化了。
column5: 他的病情突然惡化了。
column6: Tā de bìngqíng tūrán èhuà le.
column7: His condition suddenly got worse.
column9: Used for conditions getting worse: 病情惡化 (an illness), 關係惡化, 環境惡化, 局勢惡化. The opposite is 好轉. It can also take an object, as in 惡化了兩國關係. 惡 is also read wù when it means to hate.

column3: A formal, news-style verb for holding something harmful in check before it grows: 遏制通货膨胀, 遏制疫情蔓延, 遏制污染. Its objects are usually bad things, and it is mostly written, as in reports and speeches.
column4: 政府采取措施遏制房价上涨。
column5: 政府採取措施遏制房價上漲。
column6: Zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ cuòshī èzhì fángjià shàngzhǎng.
column7: The government is taking measures to curb rising housing prices.
column9: A formal, news-style verb for holding something harmful in check before it grows: 遏制通貨膨脹, 遏制疫情蔓延, 遏制污染. Its objects are usually bad things, and it is mostly written, as in reports and speeches.

column3: Two opposites joined into one word for the history of favors and grudges between people or groups: 个人恩怨 (a personal feud), 恩怨情仇 (a stock phrase of dramas and martial-arts novels), 了结恩怨. 恩怨分明 describes someone who keeps track of both and repays each.
column4: 他们之间的恩怨已经持续了很多年。
column5: 他們之間的恩怨已經持續了很多年。
column6: Tāmen zhījiān de ēnyuàn yǐjīng chíxù le hěn duō nián.
column7: The bad blood between them has lasted for many years.
column9: Two opposites joined into one word for the history of favors and grudges between people or groups: 個人恩怨 (a personal feud), 恩怨情仇 (a stock phrase of dramas and martial-arts novels), 了結恩怨. 恩怨分明 describes someone who keeps track of both and repays each.

column3: Oxides are named in one pattern: a number, then 氧化 (oxide), then the element. So 一氧化碳 is carbon monoxide and 二氧化硫 is sulfur dioxide. In the news it comes up in 二氧化碳排放 (emissions). 氧 was standardized in the 19th century from 养 (to nourish), for oxygen's role in sustaining life.
column4: 汽车排放大量二氧化碳。
column5: 汽車排放大量二氧化碳。
column6: Qìchē páifàng dàliàng èryǎnghuàtàn.
column7: Cars give off a large amount of carbon dioxide.
column9: Oxides are named in one pattern: a number, then 氧化 (oxide), then the element. So 一氧化碳 is carbon monoxide and 二氧化硫 is sulfur dioxide. In the news it comes up in 二氧化碳排放 (emissions). 氧 was standardized in the 19th century from 養 (to nourish), for oxygen's role in sustaining life.

column3: It means staring into space with your mind elsewhere, and says nothing about being stupid: the person is usually just daydreaming, tired or lost in thought. 发什么呆? is the everyday "what are you spacing out for?".
column4: 她坐在窗边发呆。
column5: 她坐在窗邊發呆。
column6: Tā zuò zài chuāngbiān fādāi.
column7: She sits by the window, staring into space.
column9: It means staring into space with your mind elsewhere, and says nothing about being stupid: the person is usually just daydreaming, tired or lost in thought. 發什麼呆? is the everyday "what are you spacing out for?".

column3: The promised thing comes right after: 发誓再也不喝酒 (I swear never to drink again). It can be solemn (对天发誓) or casual (我发誓, "I swear"), and it splits like a verb plus object: 发了誓, 发过誓.
column4: 他发誓再也不迟到了。
column5: 他發誓再也不遲到了。
column6: Tā fāshì zài yě bù chídào le.
column7: He swore never to be late again.
column9: The promised thing comes right after: 發誓再也不喝酒 (I swear never to drink again). It can be solemn (對天發誓) or casual (我發誓, "I swear"), and it splits like a verb plus object: 發了誓, 發過誓.

column3: Mainly for the physical growth of children, animals and plants: 发育期 (the growth years), 发育良好, 发育不良. For an economy or a project, say 发展 instead.
column4: 青少年的发育需要充足的睡眠。
column5: 青少年的發育需要充足的睡眠。
column6: Qīngshàonián de fāyù xūyào chōngzú de shuìmián.
column7: Teenagers need plenty of sleep to grow properly.
column9: Mainly for the physical growth of children, animals and plants: 發育期 (the growth years), 發育良好, 發育不良. For an economy or a project, say 發展 instead.

column3: A company or school treated as a "person" in law, able to own property. The contrast is 自然人, an actual human. On the mainland it also often means the one person who signs for the company (法人代表). An old form of 法 contained 廌, a mythical creature that can distinguish right from wrong.
column4: 公司是法人，可以拥有自己的财产。
column5: 公司是法人，可以擁有自己的財產。
column6: Gōngsī shì fǎrén, kěyǐ yōngyǒu zìjǐ de cáichǎn.
column7: A company is a legal person and can own property.
column9: A company or school treated as a "person" in law, able to own property. The contrast is 自然人, an actual human. On the mainland it also often means the one person who signs for the company (法人代表). An old form of 法 contained 廌, a mythical creature that can distinguish right from wrong.

column3: It describes a place that is busy and prosperous, full of shops, traffic and money: 繁华的市中心, 繁华地段. A lively but modest street market is 热闹, not 繁华. 华 was the original form of 花, flower.
column4: 这条街是城里最繁华的地段。
column5: 這條街是城裡最繁華的地段。
column6: Zhè tiáo jiē shì chéng lǐ zuì fánhuá de dìduàn.
column7: This street is the busiest and most prosperous part of the city.
column9: It describes a place that is busy and prosperous, full of shops, traffic and money: 繁華的市中心, 繁華地段. A lively but modest street market is 熱鬧, not 繁華. 華 was the original form of 花, flower.

column3: The counterpart of 简体字 (simplified characters). It is often shortened to 繁体, as in 繁体中文. Taiwan and Hong Kong write in this script; the mainland and Singapore use simplified. Taiwan's official name for them is 正体字, "standard characters", though 繁体字 is common there too.
column4: 台湾和香港使用繁体字。
column5: 台灣和香港使用繁體字。
column6: Táiwān hé Xiānggǎng shǐyòng fántǐzì.
column7: Taiwan and Hong Kong use traditional characters.
column9: The counterpart of 簡體字 (simplified characters). It is often shortened to 繁體, as in 繁體中文. Taiwan and Hong Kong write in this script; the mainland and Singapore use simplified. Taiwan's official name for them is 正體字, "standard characters", though 繁體字 is common there too.

column3: To answer a claim or accusation with a counter-argument: 反驳对方的观点, 无力反驳, 他反驳说. You bring reasons, so it is more than 不同意 (to disagree). The thing refuted is usually a view, not a person.
column4: 他用事实反驳了对方的说法。
column5: 他用事實反駁了對方的說法。
column6: Tā yòng shìshí fǎnbó le duìfāng de shuōfǎ.
column7: He used facts to refute the other side's claim.
column9: To answer a claim or accusation with a counter-argument: 反駁對方的觀點, 無力反駁, 他反駁說. You bring reasons, so it is more than 不同意 (to disagree). The thing refuted is usually a view, not a person.

column3: It describes behavior, weather or results that depart from the usual, as in 天气反常 or 反常的行为, and usually hints that something is off.
column4: 今年冬天的天气很反常。
column5: 今年冬天的天氣很反常。
column6: Jīnnián dōngtiān de tiānqì hěn fǎncháng.
column7: The weather this winter is very unusual.
column9: It describes behavior, weather or results that depart from the usual, as in 天氣反常 or 反常的行為, and usually hints that something is off.

column3: The pattern is 对 + person or thing + 很反感, or 引起反感 for causing resentment. It is a definite but not violent dislike, usually of someone's manner, tone or behavior.
column4: 我对他说话的态度很反感。
column5: 我對他說話的態度很反感。
column6: Wǒ duì tā shuōhuà de tàidù hěn fǎngǎn.
column7: I really dislike the way he talks.
column9: The pattern is 對 + person or thing + 很反感, or 引起反感 for causing resentment. It is a definite but not violent dislike, usually of someone's manner, tone or behavior.

column3: It covers both the feedback itself (用户反馈, 反馈意见) and the act of passing it back, as in 反馈给我们. It is also a technical term in electronics and control systems.
column4: 请把您的意见反馈给我们。
column5: 請把您的意見反饋給我們。
column6: Qǐng bǎ nín de yìjiàn fǎnkuì gěi wǒmen.
column7: Please give us your feedback.
column9: It covers both the feedback itself (用戶反饋, 反饋意見) and the act of passing it back, as in 反饋給我們. It is also a technical term in electronics and control systems.

column3: It covers light, sound and heat bouncing back, and the body's automatic reactions, as in 条件反射 for a conditioned reflex. Compare 放射, sending out from a center, and 辐射, radiating; all are built on 射, to shoot. 射 began as a bow and an arrow, to shoot a bow.
column4: 镜子反射出明亮的阳光。
column5: 鏡子反射出明亮的陽光。
column6: Jìngzi fǎnshè chū míngliàng de yángguāng.
column7: The mirror reflects the bright sunlight.
column9: It covers light, sound and heat bouncing back, and the body's automatic reactions, as in 條件反射 for a conditioned reflex. Compare 放射, sending out from a center, and 輻射, radiating; all are built on 射, to shoot. 射 began as a bow and an arrow, to shoot a bow.

column3: A serious look back at your own actions or a past event in order to learn from it: 反思自己, 深刻反思. It fits essays and news as well as personal talk.
column4: 失败以后，他开始反思自己的做法。
column5: 失敗以後，他開始反思自己的做法。
column6: Shībài yǐhòu, tā kāishǐ fǎnsī zìjǐ de zuòfǎ.
column7: After failing, he began to reflect on his own approach.
column9: A serious look back at your own actions or a past event in order to learn from it: 反思自己, 深刻反思. It fits essays and news as well as personal talk.

column3: A written connector that turns an argument around: if A is true then B, 反之 not B. It comes at the start of a clause, usually after a comma or full stop, often with 则 right after it.
column4: 多运动对身体有好处，反之则容易生病。
column5: 多運動對身體有好處，反之則容易生病。
column6: Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒu hǎochù, fǎnzhī zé róngyì shēngbìng.
column7: Exercise is good for you; otherwise you get sick more easily.
column9: A written connector that turns an argument around: if A is true then B, 反之 not B. It comes at the start of a clause, usually after a comma or full stop, often with 則 right after it.

column3: It is said of rivers, but even more often of something bad or unwanted that spreads without control: 假货泛滥, 垃圾信息泛滥. The tone is always negative.
column4: 市场上假货泛滥，消费者要小心。
column5: 市場上假貨泛濫，消費者要小心。
column6: Shìchǎng shàng jiǎhuò fànlàn, xiāofèizhě yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Fake goods are everywhere on the market, so consumers should be careful.
column9: It is said of rivers, but even more often of something bad or unwanted that spreads without control: 假貨泛濫, 垃圾信息泛濫. The tone is always negative.
