column3: A formal word from philosophy and academic writing for a broad class of things. It is common in 属于…范畴 and 超出…的范畴, meaning inside or outside the scope of a topic or field.
column4: 这个问题不属于我们讨论的范畴。
column5: 這個問題不屬於我們討論的範疇。
column6: Zhège wèntí bù shǔyú wǒmen tǎolùn de fànchóu.
column7: This question is outside what we are discussing.
column9: A formal word from philosophy and academic writing for a broad class of things. It is common in 屬於…範疇 and 超出…的範疇, meaning inside or outside the scope of a topic or field.

column3: It suggests selling goods as a dealer or peddler, often something illegal or disapproved of: 贩卖毒品, 贩卖人口. For an ordinary shop selling things, plain 卖 is the everyday word. It can also be neutral, as in 自动贩卖机, a vending machine.
column4: 他因为贩卖假药被警察抓了。
column5: 他因為販賣假藥被警察抓了。
column6: Tā yīnwèi fànmài jiǎyào bèi jǐngchá zhuā le.
column7: He was arrested by the police for selling fake medicine.
column9: It suggests selling goods as a dealer or peddler, often something illegal or disapproved of: 販賣毒品, 販賣人口. For an ordinary shop selling things, plain 賣 is the everyday word. It can also be neutral, as in 自動販賣機, a vending machine.

column3: Where something lies relative to you or a landmark, in terms like 东南西北 and 上下前后: 辨别方位, 分不清方位. 方位词 is the grammar term for such words of direction and position.
column4: 我在森林里迷路了，分不清方位。
column5: 我在森林裡迷路了，分不清方位。
column6: Wǒ zài sēnlín lǐ mílù le, fēn bù qīng fāngwèi.
column7: I got lost in the forest and couldn't tell which direction was which.
column9: Where something lies relative to you or a landmark, in terms like 東南西北 and 上下前後: 辨別方位, 分不清方位. 方位詞 is the grammar term for such words of direction and position.

column3: A regional variety such as Cantonese, Shanghainese or Hokkien, which differ from the standard language so much that speakers often can't understand each other. People usually name them with 话 instead: 广东话, 上海话.
column4: 他们在家里说方言，我一句也听不懂。
column5: 他們在家裡說方言，我一句也聽不懂。
column6: Tāmen zài jiā lǐ shuō fāngyán, wǒ yī jù yě tīng bù dǒng.
column7: They speak a dialect at home, and I can't understand a word.
column9: A regional variety such as Cantonese, Shanghainese or Hokkien, which differ from the standard language so much that speakers often can't understand each other. People usually name them with 話 instead: 廣東話, 上海話.

column3: Almost always followed by a distance, to say how far the area around a place reaches: 方圆十里, 方圆五公里内. It is a little bookish, at home in news and stories; in talk, 附近 is more usual.
column4: 方圆五公里内没有一家商店。
column5: 方圓五公里內沒有一家商店。
column6: Fāngyuán wǔ gōnglǐ nèi méiyǒu yī jiā shāngdiàn.
column7: There isn't a single shop within five kilometers.
column9: Almost always followed by a distance, to say how far the area around a place reaches: 方圓十里, 方圓五公里內. It is a little bookish, at home in news and stories; in talk, 附近 is more usual.

column3: A more formal word for defense, used for military works, security systems and the body's own defenses: 防御系统, 防御工事. In sports, 防守 is the usual word. Its opposite is 进攻.
column4: 这座城市的防御系统非常完善。
column5: 這座城市的防禦系統非常完善。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì de fángyù xìtǒng fēicháng wánshàn.
column7: This city's defense system is very thorough.
column9: A more formal word for defense, used for military works, security systems and the body's own defenses: 防禦系統, 防禦工事. In sports, 防守 is the usual word. Its opposite is 進攻.

column3: 纺织业, 纺织厂 and 纺织品 are the textile trade, its factories and its goods. Today it is mostly the industry word; in talk about the past it is also the spinning and weaving women did at home.
column4: 这家工厂主要生产纺织品。
column5: 這家工廠主要生產紡織品。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng zhǔyào shēngchǎn fǎngzhī pǐn.
column7: This factory mainly makes textiles.
column9: 紡織業, 紡織廠 and 紡織品 are the textile trade, its factories and its goods. Today it is mostly the industry word; in talk about the past it is also the spinning and weaving women did at home.

column3: Light, heat or rays going out from a center, as in 放射性 (radioactive) and 放射治疗 (radiation therapy); also figurative, as in 放射出光芒. Compare 反射, which sends them back.
column4: 太阳向四面八方放射光和热。
column5: 太陽向四面八方放射光和熱。
column6: Tàiyáng xiàng sìmiàn bāfāng fàngshè guāng hé rè.
column7: The sun sends out light and heat in all directions.
column9: Light, heat or rays going out from a center, as in 放射性 (radioactive) and 放射治療 (radiation therapy); also figurative, as in 放射出光芒. Compare 反射, which sends them back.

column3: A set phrase for the animal kingdom, in which 飞 and 走 give the way the two groups move. It turns up in descriptions of nature, zoos and forests, usually as 各种飞禽走兽 or 飞禽走兽都有.
column4: 这片森林里有各种飞禽走兽。
column5: 這片森林裡有各種飛禽走獸。
column6: Zhè piàn sēnlín lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng fēiqínzǒushòu.
column7: This forest has all kinds of birds and beasts.
column9: A set phrase for the animal kingdom, in which 飛 and 走 give the way the two groups move. It turns up in descriptions of nature, zoos and forests, usually as 各種飛禽走獸 or 飛禽走獸都有.

column3: A poetic word for flying: birds, planes, or dreams and imagination, as in 自由飞翔, 展翅飞翔 and 飞翔的梦想. For ordinary flying, such as a plane to Beijing, use 飞.
column4: 一只老鹰在蓝天上自由地飞翔。
column5: 一隻老鷹在藍天上自由地飛翔。
column6: Yī zhī lǎoyīng zài lántiān shàng zìyóu de fēixiáng.
column7: An eagle soars freely in the blue sky.
column9: A poetic word for flying: birds, planes, or dreams and imagination, as in 自由飛翔, 展翅飛翔 and 飛翔的夢想. For ordinary flying, such as a plane to Beijing, use 飛.

column3: Mostly figurative: a big jump forward in progress, as in 飞跃发展 and 实现飞跃, said of an economy, technology or a company's results. Leaping through the air is the rarer, literal use.
column4: 这几年我们公司的业绩有了飞跃。
column5: 這幾年我們公司的業績有了飛躍。
column6: Zhè jǐ nián wǒmen gōngsī de yèjī yǒu le fēiyuè.
column7: In these years our company's results have taken a big leap.
column9: Mostly figurative: a big jump forward in progress, as in 飛躍發展 and 實現飛躍, said of an economy, technology or a company's results. Leaping through the air is the rarer, literal use.

column3: Only for soil and land, as in 肥沃的土地 and 土壤肥沃. A fat person is 胖 and a fat animal 肥, never 肥沃.
column4: 这里的土地非常肥沃，适合种水稻。
column5: 這裡的土地非常肥沃，適合種水稻。
column6: Zhèlǐ de tǔdì fēicháng féiwò, shìhé zhòng shuǐdào.
column7: The land here is very fertile and good for growing rice.
column9: Only for soil and land, as in 肥沃的土地 and 土壤肥沃. A fat person is 胖 and a fat animal 肥, never 肥沃.

column3: It means saying false things that damage someone's reputation, and is also a legal term: 诽谤罪 is the offense of defamation. A common partner is 造谣, spreading rumors.
column4: 他到处造谣诽谤我，我要告他。
column5: 他到處造謠誹謗我，我要告他。
column6: Tā dàochù zàoyáo fěibàng wǒ, wǒ yào gào tā.
column7: He spreads rumors and slanders me everywhere; I'm going to sue him.
column9: It means saying false things that damage someone's reputation, and is also a legal term: 誹謗罪 is the offense of defamation. A common partner is 造謠, spreading rumors.

column3: For laws, systems, treaties and customs that are formally ended: 废除死刑, 废除不平等条约. For things you simply throw away, use 扔 or 丢掉.
column4: 这个国家已经废除了死刑。
column5: 這個國家已經廢除了死刑。
column6: Zhège guójiā yǐjīng fèichú le sǐxíng.
column7: This country has abolished the death penalty.
column9: For laws, systems, treaties and customs that are formally ended: 廢除死刑, 廢除不平等條約. For things you simply throw away, use 扔 or 丟掉.

column3: A praising idiom for being absorbed in study, work or a hobby. It is often used as 废寝忘食地 + verb, about students, researchers and craftspeople, and fits both writing and speech.
column4: 他为了准备考试，废寝忘食地复习。
column5: 他為了準備考試，廢寢忘食地複習。
column6: Tā wèile zhǔnbèi kǎoshì, fèiqǐnwàngshí de fùxí.
column7: To prepare for the exam, he studies day and night without rest.
column9: A praising idiom for being absorbed in study, work or a hobby. It is often used as 廢寢忘食地 + verb, about students, researchers and craftspeople, and fits both writing and speech.

column3: What is left of buildings or a city after war, an earthquake or a fire: 地震后的废墟, 战争的废墟. Ancient sites that people visit are called 遗址 instead.
column4: 地震过后，城市变成了一片废墟。
column5: 地震過後，城市變成了一片廢墟。
column6: Dìzhèn guòhòu, chéngshì biànchéng le yī piàn fèixū.
column7: After the earthquake, the city became a field of ruins.
column9: What is left of buildings or a city after war, an earthquake or a fire: 地震後的廢墟, 戰爭的廢墟. Ancient sites that people visit are called 遺址 instead.

column3: Water boiling, but just as often a crowd or feelings boiling over: 全场沸腾, 热血沸腾, 沸腾的生活. Usually excitement, but also anger, as in 民怨沸腾.
column4: 听到好消息，全场观众都沸腾了。
column5: 聽到好消息，全場觀眾都沸騰了。
column6: Tīngdào hǎo xiāoxi, quánchǎng guānzhòng dōu fèiténg le.
column7: On hearing the good news, the whole audience erupted.
column9: Water boiling, but just as often a crowd or feelings boiling over: 全場沸騰, 熱血沸騰, 沸騰的生活. Usually excitement, but also anger, as in 民怨沸騰.

column3: Telling apart things that look or sound alike, using your senses or judgment: 分辨真假, 分辨方向. It often takes 不出 or 得出: 分辨不出. The similar 辨别 is more formal.
column4: 我分辨不出这两种茶有什么不同。
column5: 我分辨不出這兩種茶有什麼不同。
column6: Wǒ fēnbiàn bù chū zhè liǎng zhǒng chá yǒu shénme bù tóng.
column7: I can't tell what the difference between these two teas is.
column9: Telling apart things that look or sound alike, using your senses or judgment: 分辨真假, 分辨方向. It often takes 不出 or 得出: 分辨不出. The similar 辨別 is more formal.

column3: Used for knowing how far to go in what you say or do: 有分寸 is tactful and well judged, 没分寸 is tactless. Both characters are small units of length. So the word is like measuring out exactly the right amount.
column4: 他说话很有分寸。
column5: 他說話很有分寸。
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn yǒu fēncun.
column7: He is careful about what he says.
column9: Used for knowing how far to go in what you say or do: 有分寸 is tactful and well judged, 沒分寸 is tactless. Both characters are small units of length. So the word is like measuring out exactly the right amount.

column3: A business word: a company shares part of its profit with shareholders, partners or employees, as in 股东分红 and 员工分红. Here 红 is not the color but its sense of a bonus.
column4: 公司每年都给股东分红。
column5: 公司每年都給股東分紅。
column6: Gōngsī měinián dōu gěi gǔdōng fēnhóng.
column7: The company pays its shareholders a dividend every year.
column9: A business word: a company shares part of its profit with shareholders, partners or employees, as in 股東分紅 and 員工分紅. Here 紅 is not the color but its sense of a bonus.

column3: A biology and medicine word: glands and cells release a substance such as saliva, hormones or sweat, and that substance is the object, as in 分泌激素.
column4: 身体会分泌激素。
column5: 身體會分泌激素。
column6: Shēntǐ huì fēnmì jīsù.
column7: The body secretes hormones.
column9: A biology and medicine word: glands and cells release a substance such as saliva, hormones or sweat, and that substance is the object, as in 分泌激素.

column3: Used for a difference in opinions, plans or positions, usually in a formal or news setting: 存在分歧, 意见分歧, 解决分歧.
column4: 双方在价格上存在分歧。
column5: 雙方在價格上存在分歧。
column6: Shuāngfāng zài jiàgé shàng cúnzài fēnqí.
column7: The two sides disagree on the price.
column9: Used for a difference in opinions, plans or positions, usually in a formal or news setting: 存在分歧, 意見分歧, 解決分歧.

column3: Also used figuratively: 婚姻是爱情的坟墓 calls marriage the grave of love.
column4: 村子后面有一座古老的坟墓。
column5: 村子後面有一座古老的墳墓。
column6: Cūnzi hòumiàn yǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de fénmù.
column7: Behind the village there is an old grave.
column9: Also used figuratively: 婚姻是愛情的墳墓 calls marriage the grave of love.

column3: Used for a dry substance ground fine, such as medicine, spice or chemicals; in compounds like 面粉 and 奶粉 the single 粉 is the usual form. Here 末 is in its sense of powder or dust.
column4: 他把药片磨成了粉末。
column5: 他把藥片磨成了粉末。
column6: Tā bǎ yàopiàn mó chéng le fěnmò.
column7: He ground the pill into powder.
column9: Used for a dry substance ground fine, such as medicine, spice or chemicals; in compounds like 麵粉 and 奶粉 the single 粉 is the usual form. Here 末 is in its sense of powder or dust.

column3: The everyday word for pink, used for clothes, flowers and the like; 粉红色 means the same. 粉 is thought to have first meant face powder, then the white of that powder, and later the color of a face made up with it: pink.
column4: 她穿了一条粉色的裙子。
column5: 她穿了一條粉色的裙子。
column6: Tā chuān le yī tiáo fěnsè de qúnzi.
column7: She wore a pink skirt.
column9: The everyday word for pink, used for clothes, flowers and the like; 粉紅色 means the same. 粉 is thought to have first meant face powder, then the white of that powder, and later the color of a face made up with it: pink.

column3: Often figurative, with a rumor, a plan, a hope or a plot as the thing smashed; for simply breaking a glass or a plate, 打碎 is more usual.
column4: 这个谣言很快就被粉碎了。
column5: 這個謠言很快就被粉碎了。
column6: Zhège yáoyán hěn kuài jiù bèi fěnsuì le.
column7: The rumor was quickly shot down.
column9: Often figurative, with a rumor, a plan, a hope or a plot as the thing smashed; for simply breaking a glass or a plate, 打碎 is more usual.

column3: Often figurative: 有分量 describes words, a person or a piece of work that carries weight, and 没分量 describes one that does not. Here 分 is the sense meaning a part or share.
column4: 他说的话很有分量。
column5: 他說的話很有分量。
column6: Tā shuō de huà hěn yǒu fènliang.
column7: His words carry a lot of weight.
column9: Often figurative: 有分量 describes words, a person or a piece of work that carries weight, and 沒分量 describes one that does not. Here 分 is the sense meaning a part or share.

column3: Usually a flattering word for a rounded, shapely figure or face, as in 身材丰满, and also for things fully developed, as in 羽毛丰满 (fully fledged).
column4: 理想很丰满，现实却很骨感。
column5: 理想很豐滿，現實卻很骨感。
column6: Lǐxiǎng hěn fēngmǎn, xiànshí què hěn gǔgǎn.
column7: The ideal is full, but reality is bare bones.
column9: Usually a flattering word for a rounded, shapely figure or face, as in 身材豐滿, and also for things fully developed, as in 羽毛豐滿 (fully fledged).

column3: Mostly describes a meal or feast, a table full of dishes: 丰盛的晚餐, 丰盛的午餐.
column4: 妈妈准备了一桌丰盛的晚餐。
column5: 媽媽準備了一桌豐盛的晚餐。
column6: Māma zhǔnbèi le yī zhuō fēngshèng de wǎncān.
column7: Mom prepared a lavish dinner.
column9: Mostly describes a meal or feast, a table full of dishes: 豐盛的晚餐, 豐盛的午餐.

column3: A set phrase of travel writing and talk about places: you get to know the 风土人情 of a region, meaning its landscape, customs and the way its people live. Alone, 人情 also means a favor you owe someone, as in 欠人情.
column4: 我们去旅行时喜欢了解当地的风土人情。
column5: 我們去旅行時喜歡了解當地的風土人情。
column6: Wǒmen qù lǚxíng shí xǐhuan liǎojiě dāngdì de fēngtǔrénqíng.
column7: When we travel, we like to learn about the local customs and way of life.
column9: A set phrase of travel writing and talk about places: you get to know the 風土人情 of a region, meaning its landscape, customs and the way its people live. Alone, 人情 also means a favor you owe someone, as in 欠人情.

column3: Mostly for the distinctive taste of a regional or traditional dish, as in 地方风味 and 家乡风味, and often seen on restaurant signs.
column4: 这家餐厅的菜有浓浓的四川风味。
column5: 這家餐廳的菜有濃濃的四川風味。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài yǒu nóngnóng de Sìchuān fēngwèi.
column7: The dishes at this restaurant have a strong Sichuan flavor.
column9: Mostly for the distinctive taste of a regional or traditional dish, as in 地方風味 and 家鄉風味, and often seen on restaurant signs.

column3: Used for sealing off a road, a port, a border or a crime scene, and also for keeping news from getting out: 封锁消息.
column4: 警方封锁了现场。
column5: 警方封鎖了現場。
column6: Jǐngfāng fēngsuǒ le xiànchǎng.
column7: The police sealed off the scene.
column9: Used for sealing off a road, a port, a border or a crime scene, and also for keeping news from getting out: 封鎖消息.

column3: Describes the edge of a knife, scissors or a sword, and figuratively sharp words or writing: 言辞锋利. 利 shows a knife 刀 reaping grain 禾, and it too means sharp.
column4: 这把刀非常锋利，小心别割到手。
column5: 這把刀非常鋒利，小心別割到手。
column6: Zhè bǎ dāo fēicháng fēnglì, xiǎoxīn bié gē dào shǒu.
column7: This knife is very sharp, so be careful not to cut your hand.
column9: Describes the edge of a knife, scissors or a sword, and figuratively sharp words or writing: 言辭鋒利. 利 shows a knife 刀 reaping grain 禾, and it too means sharp.

column3: A formal, news-style word for a committee, council or parliament voting down a proposal or plan; 一票否决 is a veto by a single vote.
column4: 委员会否决了这个提议。
column5: 委員會否決了這個提議。
column6: Wěiyuánhuì fǒujué le zhège tíyì.
column7: The committee voted down this proposal.
column9: A formal, news-style word for a committee, council or parliament voting down a proposal or plan; 一票否決 is a veto by a single vote.

column3: In everyday speech it means going through the motions or brushing someone off: 敷衍了事 is doing a job carelessly, and 别敷衍我 is "don't brush me off". Both characters mean to spread: 敷 is to lay out or apply something such as ointment, and 衍 is to spread out.
column4: 他只是敷衍了我几句，就走了。
column5: 他只是敷衍了我幾句，就走了。
column6: Tā zhǐshì fūyǎn le wǒ jǐ jù, jiù zǒu le.
column7: He just brushed me off with a few words and left.
column9: In everyday speech it means going through the motions or brushing someone off: 敷衍了事 is doing a job carelessly, and 別敷衍我 is "don't brush me off". Both characters mean to spread: 敷 is to lay out or apply something such as ointment, and 衍 is to spread out.

column3: Most often negated: 不服气 is to refuse to accept a loss, a judgment or someone's claim to be better, and to feel resentful about it.
column4: 他输了比赛，但是心里不服气。
column5: 他輸了比賽，但是心裡不服氣。
column6: Tā shū le bǐsài, dànshì xīnli bù fúqì.
column7: He lost the match, but deep down he wouldn't accept it.
column9: Most often negated: 不服氣 is to refuse to accept a loss, a judgment or someone's claim to be better, and to feel resentful about it.

column3: It is both the captive, as in 抓了很多俘虏, and the act of capturing, as in 被俘虏, to be taken prisoner. Figuratively, to win someone over completely: 俘虏了观众的心.
column4: 士兵们被敌人俘虏了。
column5: 士兵們被敵人俘虜了。
column6: Shìbīngmen bèi dírén fúlǔ le.
column7: The soldiers were taken prisoner by the enemy.
column9: It is both the captive, as in 抓了很多俘虜, and the act of capturing, as in 被俘虜, to be taken prisoner. Figuratively, to win someone over completely: 俘虜了觀眾的心.

column3: Picture a wheel's spokes shooting out from the hub: that is how heat, light or nuclear radiation spreads out, as in 核辐射 and 电磁辐射.
column4: 手机的辐射对人体有影响吗？
column5: 手機的輻射對人體有影響嗎？
column6: Shǒujī de fúshè duì réntǐ yǒu yǐngxiǎng ma?
column7: Does the radiation from cell phones affect the human body?
column9: Picture a wheel's spokes shooting out from the hub: that is how heat, light or nuclear radiation spreads out, as in 核輻射 and 電磁輻射.

column3: Said of someone who is blessed with an easy, happy life or good family: 有福气 is a compliment, often said to parents of good children.
column4: 你有这么孝顺的孩子，真有福气。
column5: 你有這麼孝順的孩子，真有福氣。
column6: Nǐ yǒu zhème xiàoshùn de háizi, zhēn yǒu fúqi.
column7: To have such a dutiful child, you are truly blessed.
column9: Said of someone who is blessed with an easy, happy life or good family: 有福氣 is a compliment, often said to parents of good children.

column3: Gentle, affectionate touching as the hand slides over something, such as a child's head, a pet or a cheek: 抚摸着孩子的头.
column4: 她轻轻地抚摸着小猫。
column5: 她輕輕地撫摸著小貓。
column6: Tā qīngqīng de fǔmō zhe xiǎomāo.
column7: She gently stroked the kitten.
column9: Gentle, affectionate touching as the hand slides over something, such as a child's head, a pet or a cheek: 撫摸著孩子的頭.

column3: A formal word for raising a child to adulthood, with a legal sense in 抚养费 (child support) and 抚养权 (custody); for casual raising, 养 alone is used, as in 养孩子.
column4: 她一个人把三个孩子抚养成人。
column5: 她一個人把三個孩子撫養成人。
column6: Tā yī gè rén bǎ sān gè háizi fǔyǎng chéngrén.
column7: She raised three children on her own.
column9: A formal word for raising a child to adulthood, with a legal sense in 撫養費 (child support) and 撫養權 (custody); for casual raising, 養 alone is used, as in 養孩子.

column3: Looking down from a height, such as from a tower or a plane; the opposite is 仰视, and 俯视图 is a top view in a drawing. In bronze inscriptions 俯 had a person bending over, 勹, in place of today's 亻.
column4: 站在山顶可以俯视整个城市。
column5: 站在山頂可以俯視整個城市。
column6: Zhàn zài shāndǐng kěyǐ fǔshì zhěnggè chéngshì.
column7: From the top of the mountain you can look down on the whole city.
column9: Looking down from a height, such as from a tower or a plane; the opposite is 仰視, and 俯視圖 is a top view in a drawing. In bronze inscriptions 俯 had a person bending over, 勹, in place of today's 亻.

column3: Common for fruit, vegetables, meat and plants that spoil and go soft, and figuratively for a corrupt system. 烂 also means soft or mushy, and well-cooked until soft.
column4: 冰箱里的水果都腐烂了。
column5: 冰箱裡的水果都腐爛了。
column6: Bīngxiāng li de shuǐguǒ dōu fǔlàn le.
column7: The fruit in the fridge has all rotted.
column9: Common for fruit, vegetables, meat and plants that spoil and go soft, and figuratively for a corrupt system. 爛 also means soft or mushy, and well-cooked until soft.

column3: Used for acid, rust and salt water attacking metal, and figuratively for bad influences that wear down people or values: 腐蚀干部 describes a corrupting influence on officials. 蚀 is the same word as 食, "to eat". Think of corrosion as metal being slowly eaten away.
column4: 酸会腐蚀金属。
column5: 酸會腐蝕金屬。
column6: Suān huì fǔshí jīnshǔ.
column7: Acid corrodes metal.
column9: Used for acid, rust and salt water attacking metal, and figuratively for bad influences that wear down people or values: 腐蝕幹部 describes a corrupting influence on officials. 蝕 is the same word as 食, "to eat". Think of corrosion as metal being slowly eaten away.

column3: Literally for wood and other material that has rotted away. Figuratively it is a stock word in political and social writing for a decadent system, idea or way of life, often in 腐朽没落.
column4: 这座桥的木头已经腐朽了。
column5: 這座橋的木頭已經腐朽了。
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo de mùtou yǐjīng fǔxiǔ le.
column7: The wood of this bridge has already rotted.
column9: Literally for wood and other material that has rotted away. Figuratively it is a stock word in political and social writing for a decadent system, idea or way of life, often in 腐朽沒落.

column3: Usually mildly critical: it suggests agreeing just to go along with others, with no opinion of one's own. Often in 随声附和, to echo whatever is said.
column4: 他没有主见，总是附和别人。
column5: 他沒有主見，總是附和別人。
column6: Tā méiyǒu zhǔjiàn, zǒngshì fùhè biérén.
column7: He has no views of his own and always just goes along with others.
column9: Usually mildly critical: it suggests agreeing just to go along with others, with no opinion of one's own. Often in 隨聲附和, to echo whatever is said.

column3: Describes an institution that belongs to a larger one: 附属医院 and 附属小学 are the hospital and school run by a university. It also works as a verb with 于: 这所医院附属于北京大学 (this hospital belongs to Peking University).
column4: 这是大学的附属医院。
column5: 這是大學的附屬醫院。
column6: Zhè shì dàxué de fùshǔ yīyuàn.
column7: This is the university's affiliated hospital.
column9: Describes an institution that belongs to a larger one: 附屬醫院 and 附屬小學 are the hospital and school run by a university. It also works as a verb with 於: 這所醫院附屬於北京大學 (this hospital belongs to Peking University).

column3: Used for resurrection (复活节 is Easter) and loosely for anything that comes back: a character in a game, a dead custom. 复 originally meant "going back", which fits life coming back.
column4: 游戏里的角色可以复活。
column5: 遊戲裡的角色可以復活。
column6: Yóuxì lǐ de juésè kěyǐ fùhuó.
column7: Characters in the game can come back to life.
column9: Used for resurrection (復活節 is Easter) and loosely for anything that comes back: a character in a game, a dead custom. 復 originally meant "going back", which fits life coming back.

column3: A big, formal word for nations, cultures and movements coming back to strength: 民族复兴, and 文艺复兴 for the Renaissance. It is not used for a person recovering.
column4: 他们希望复兴传统文化。
column5: 他們希望復興傳統文化。
column6: Tāmen xīwàng fùxīng chuántǒng wénhuà.
column7: They hope to revive traditional culture.
column9: A big, formal word for nations, cultures and movements coming back to strength: 民族復興, and 文藝復興 for the Renaissance. It is not used for a person recovering.

column3: Formal. What is given is almost always abstract: 赋予权利 (rights), 赋予意义 (meaning), 赋予使命 (a mission); you would not use it for handing someone an object. 予 is a literary "give"; in everyday speech the word is 给.
column4: 法律赋予公民言论自由。
column5: 法律賦予公民言論自由。
column6: Fǎlǜ fùyǔ gōngmín yánlùn zìyóu.
column7: The law grants citizens freedom of speech.
column9: Formal. What is given is almost always abstract: 賦予權利 (rights), 賦予意義 (meaning), 賦予使命 (a mission); you would not use it for handing someone an object. 予 is a literary "give"; in everyday speech the word is 給.

column3: The plain medical and news word for diarrhea; in casual speech people say 拉肚子. 拉稀 is blunter slang.
column4: 他吃坏了东西，一直腹泻。
column5: 他吃壞了東西，一直腹瀉。
column6: Tā chī huài le dōngxi, yīzhí fùxiè.
column7: He ate something bad and has had diarrhea ever since.
column9: The plain medical and news word for diarrhea; in casual speech people say 拉肚子. 拉稀 is blunter slang.

column3: Covers things spread over a surface, such as snow, clouds or plants, and also reach and coverage: 信号覆盖 (signal coverage), 覆盖率 (the share covered). The object follows directly, as in 覆盖地面.
column4: 大雪覆盖了整个城市。
column5: 大雪覆蓋了整個城市。
column6: Dàxuě fùgài le zhěnggè chéngshì.
column7: Heavy snow covered the whole city.
column9: Covers things spread over a surface, such as snow, clouds or plants, and also reach and coverage: 信號覆蓋 (signal coverage), 覆蓋率 (the share covered). The object follows directly, as in 覆蓋地面.

column3: Improving something that already exists by adjusting it: crops, soil, a design, a recipe. It does not suit improving one's own skills or situation (for that, 提高 or 改善).
column4: 这种水稻是科学家改良出来的。
column5: 這種水稻是科學家改良出來的。
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐdào shì kēxuéjiā gǎiliáng chūlái de.
column7: This rice is a variety improved by scientists.
column9: Improving something that already exists by adjusting it: crops, soil, a design, a recipe. It does not suit improving one's own skills or situation (for that, 提高 or 改善).

column3: In daily life it comes up in talk about bones and diet: 补钙 (take extra calcium) and 缺钙 (be low in it). A modern word, borrowed from New Latin calcium.
column4: 牛奶里有很多钙。
column5: 牛奶裡有很多鈣。
column6: Niúnǎi lǐ yǒu hěn duō gài.
column7: Milk has a lot of calcium.
column9: In daily life it comes up in talk about bones and diet: 補鈣 (take extra calcium) and 缺鈣 (be low in it). A modern word, borrowed from New Latin calcium.

column3: The stamp is a seal or "chop" pressed in red ink, which makes a document official, so 盖章 is often the final approval step. It often goes with 签字, signing.
column4: 请在这里盖章。
column5: 請在這裡蓋章。
column6: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ gàizhāng.
column7: Please stamp here.
column9: The stamp is a seal or "chop" pressed in red ink, which makes a document official, so 蓋章 is often the final approval step. It often goes with 簽字, signing.

column3: It names a drought (严重干旱) and dry land or climate (干旱地区); 旱灾 stresses the disaster and its damage.
column4: 今年夏天，这个地区发生了严重的干旱。
column5: 今年夏天，這個地區發生了嚴重的乾旱。
column6: Jīnnián xiàtiān, zhège dìqū fāshēng le yánzhòng de gānhàn.
column7: This summer there was a severe drought in this region.
column9: It names a drought (嚴重乾旱) and dry land or climate (乾旱地區); 旱災 stresses the disaster and its damage.

column3: Describes a situation or a person's feeling when things are awkward and embarrassing, and also being stuck in an awkward position: 感到尴尬 (feel awkward), 处境尴尬 (be in an awkward spot). It is not for shame over a wrong you did.
column4: 我在会议上叫错了他的名字，真尴尬。
column5: 我在會議上叫錯了他的名字，真尷尬。
column6: Wǒ zài huìyì shàng jiào cuò le tā de míngzi, zhēn gāngà.
column7: I called him by the wrong name in the meeting. How awkward.
column9: Describes a situation or a person's feeling when things are awkward and embarrassing, and also being stuck in an awkward position: 感到尷尬 (feel awkward), 處境尷尬 (be in an awkward spot). It is not for shame over a wrong you did.

column3: A feeling of sighing at how time has passed or things have changed, usually when looking back. Often 感慨万千 (a flood of feelings) or as a verb: 他感慨地说.
column4: 回到老家，他感慨万千。
column5: 回到老家，他感慨萬千。
column6: Huídào lǎojiā, tā gǎnkǎi wànqiān.
column7: Back in his hometown, he was filled with deep feelings.
column9: A feeling of sighing at how time has passed or things have changed, usually when looking back. Often 感慨萬千 (a flood of feelings) or as a verb: 他感慨地說.

column3: Positive, and spoken as much as written: the drive to get on with work or study. Typical phrases are 有干劲, 干劲十足 (full of drive) and 鼓足干劲 (summon one's energy).
column4: 新老板来了以后，大家都很有干劲。
column5: 新老闆來了以後，大家都很有幹勁。
column6: Xīn lǎobǎn lái le yǐhòu, dàjiā dōu hěn yǒu gànjìn.
column7: Since the new boss arrived, everyone has been full of drive.
column9: Positive, and spoken as much as written: the drive to get on with work or study. Typical phrases are 有幹勁, 幹勁十足 (full of drive) and 鼓足幹勁 (summon one's energy).

column3: A formal word for the founding or guiding program of a party or movement: 党的纲领, 行动纲领 (action program). Seen mainly in politics, news and history.
column4: 这个政党公布了新的纲领。
column5: 這個政黨公布了新的綱領。
column6: Zhège zhèngdǎng gōngbù le xīn de gānglǐng.
column7: This party announced a new program.
column9: A formal word for the founding or guiding program of a party or movement: 黨的綱領, 行動綱領 (action program). Seen mainly in politics, news and history.

column3: Literally a sheltered bay for ships. Most often figurative: 温暖的港湾, a safe haven, usually home or a family where one finds rest.
column4: 家是我们温暖的港湾。
column5: 家是我們溫暖的港灣。
column6: Jiā shì wǒmen wēnnuǎn de gǎngwān.
column7: Home is our warm harbor.
column9: Literally a sheltered bay for ships. Most often figurative: 溫暖的港灣, a safe haven, usually home or a family where one finds rest.

column3: The lever of physics class, and in finance "leverage": 加杠杆 means borrowing to invest or expand, 去杠杆 means cutting that debt. The financial sense is very common in the news.
column4: 用杠杆可以省力。
column5: 用槓桿可以省力。
column6: Yòng gànggǎn kěyǐ shěnglì.
column7: Using a lever saves effort.
column9: The lever of physics class, and in finance "leverage": 加槓桿 means borrowing to invest or expand, 去槓桿 means cutting that debt. The financial sense is very common in the news.

column3: Praises skill, craft or technique: 技艺高超, 本领高超, 医术高超. It is never used for height, goals or prices.
column4: 他的厨艺非常高超。
column5: 他的廚藝非常高超。
column6: Tā de chúyì fēicháng gāochāo.
column7: His cooking skill is outstanding.
column9: Praises skill, craft or technique: 技藝高超, 本領高超, 醫術高超. It is never used for height, goals or prices.

column3: Used for moods and activity running high, such as 热情高涨, 情绪高涨, 士气高涨 (morale), and also for prices and demand. Not for a person's height.
column4: 大家的热情非常高涨。
column5: 大家的熱情非常高漲。
column6: Dàjiā de rèqíng fēicháng gāozhǎng.
column7: Everyone's enthusiasm is running very high.
column9: Used for moods and activity running high, such as 熱情高漲, 情緒高漲, 士氣高漲 (morale), and also for prices and demand. Not for a person's height.

column3: The word for pieces of writing submitted to a newspaper, magazine or website, seen from the editor's side: 投稿 is to submit one, 审稿 to review it.
column4: 编辑部每天收到几百份稿件。
column5: 編輯部每天收到幾百份稿件。
column6: Biānjíbù měitiān shōudào jǐbǎi fèn gǎojiàn.
column7: The editorial office receives hundreds of submissions every day.
column9: The word for pieces of writing submitted to a newspaper, magazine or website, seen from the editor's side: 投稿 is to submit one, 審稿 to review it.

column3: Said by someone with standing over the listener, such as a teacher, doctor or parent, and the warning is meant to be heeded. Formal and mostly written; in speech people say 提醒 or 叮嘱; 警告 is a sterner warning.
column4: 老师告诫学生不要迟到。
column5: 老師告誡學生不要遲到。
column6: Lǎoshī gàojiè xuésheng bùyào chídào.
column7: The teacher warned the students not to be late.
column9: Said by someone with standing over the listener, such as a teacher, doctor or parent, and the warning is meant to be heeded. Formal and mostly written; in speech people say 提醒 or 叮囑; 警告 is a sterner warning.

column3: A lump on the skin or in food, such as a pimple, a bump, a knot or a clump of dough. 鸡皮疙瘩 is goosebumps, and 心里有疙瘩 means a knot of resentment that is still there.
column4: 听到这个故事，我起了一身鸡皮疙瘩。
column5: 聽到這個故事，我起了一身雞皮疙瘩。
column6: Tīngdào zhège gùshi, wǒ qǐ le yīshēn jīpí gēda.
column7: Hearing this story gave me goosebumps all over.
column9: A lump on the skin or in food, such as a pimple, a bump, a knot or a clump of dough. 雞皮疙瘩 is goosebumps, and 心裡有疙瘩 means a knot of resentment that is still there.

column3: Covers both pigeons and doves; a white dove as a symbol of peace is 和平鸽. 放鸽子 is spoken slang for standing someone up.
column4: 他又放我鸽子了。
column5: 他又放我鴿子了。
column6: Tā yòu fàng wǒ gēzi le.
column7: He stood me up again.
column9: Covers both pigeons and doves; a white dove as a symbol of peace is 和平鴿. 放鴿子 is spoken slang for standing someone up.

column3: A formal, written word, common in speeches, essays and news. Its object is a person, a deed or a value held up as admirable: 歌颂英雄, 歌颂友谊, 歌颂祖国.
column4: 这首诗歌颂了普通劳动者的辛勤付出。
column5: 這首詩歌頌了普通勞動者的辛勤付出。
column6: Zhè shǒu shī gēsòng le pǔtōng láodòngzhě de xīnqín fùchū.
column7: This poem praises the hard work of ordinary laborers.
column9: A formal, written word, common in speeches, essays and news. Its object is a person, a deed or a value held up as admirable: 歌頌英雄, 歌頌友誼, 歌頌祖國.

column3: Beyond a physical layout, it is used for the shape of a situation (国际格局, 市场格局) and for the breadth of a person's outlook: 有格局 or 大格局 is high praise for someone who sees the big picture.
column4: 他很有格局，不会为小事计较。
column5: 他很有格局，不會為小事計較。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu géjú, bù huì wèi xiǎoshì jìjiào.
column7: He has a broad outlook and doesn't fuss over small things.
column9: Beyond a physical layout, it is used for the shape of a situation (國際格局, 市場格局) and for the breadth of a person's outlook: 有格局 or 大格局 is high praise for someone who sees the big picture.

column3: The set form that a document, file or form has to follow: 文件格式, 简历格式, 格式不对. 格式化 means to format a disk or text.
column4: 请按这个格式填写表格。
column5: 請按這個格式填寫表格。
column6: Qǐng àn zhège géshì tiánxiě biǎogé.
column7: Please fill in the form in this format.
column9: The set form that a document, file or form has to follow: 文件格式, 簡歷格式, 格式不對. 格式化 means to format a disk or text.

column3: Describes a distance between people or groups that grows from misunderstanding or difference, not a physical gap. It usually goes with 有, 产生 or 消除: 消除隔阂 is to bridge it.
column4: 一次长谈消除了父子之间的隔阂。
column5: 一次長談消除了父子之間的隔閡。
column6: Yī cì chángtán xiāochú le fùzǐ zhījiān de géhé.
column7: One long talk cleared away the distance between father and son.
column9: Describes a distance between people or groups that grows from misunderstanding or difference, not a physical gap. It usually goes with 有, 產生 or 消除: 消除隔閡 is to bridge it.

column3: Today most often about quarantine and infection control: 隔离病人, 居家隔离, 隔离区. It also covers keeping things apart in general, such as 隔离带, a divider strip.
column4: 他被隔离了两个星期。
column5: 他被隔離了兩個星期。
column6: Tā bèi gélí le liǎng gè xīngqī.
column7: He was kept in isolation for two weeks.
column9: Today most often about quarantine and infection control: 隔離病人, 居家隔離, 隔離區. It also covers keeping things apart in general, such as 隔離帶, a divider strip.

column3: A set phrase for meetings and discussions where everyone speaks their own mind. It is neutral to positive and often an invitation: 请大家各抒己见.
column4: 开会时，请大家各抒己见。
column5: 開會時，請大家各抒己見。
column6: Kāihuì shí, qǐng dàjiā gèshūjǐjiàn.
column7: During the meeting, please let everyone say what they think.
column9: A set phrase for meetings and discussions where everyone speaks their own mind. It is neutral to positive and often an invitation: 請大家各抒己見.

column3: Written and spoken. It describes ideas, habits, prejudices and traditions that are hard to shake, so it often carries a note of complaint: 根深蒂固的偏见, 观念根深蒂固. 蒂 is the stem of a fruit; think of a plant held fast at root and stem.
column4: 这种偏见在当地根深蒂固。
column5: 這種偏見在當地根深蒂固。
column6: Zhè zhǒng piānjiàn zài dāngdì gēnshēndìgù.
column7: This prejudice is deeply entrenched in the area.
column9: Written and spoken. It describes ideas, habits, prejudices and traditions that are hard to shake, so it often carries a note of complaint: 根深蒂固的偏見, 觀念根深蒂固. 蒂 is the stem of a fruit; think of a plant held fast at root and stem.

column3: Used for the deep cause behind a problem or phenomenon, something to dig down to: 问题的根源, 找出根源. It is more basic than 原因, and usually about something bad or troublesome.
column4: 我们要找出问题的根源。
column5: 我們要找出問題的根源。
column6: Wǒmen yào zhǎochū wèntí de gēnyuán.
column7: We need to find the root of the problem.
column9: Used for the deep cause behind a problem or phenomenon, something to dig down to: 問題的根源, 找出根源. It is more basic than 原因, and usually about something bad or troublesome.

column3: Besides tailing a person (police, detectives, stalkers), it is used for following something over time: 跟踪调查, 跟踪报道, 跟踪服务 for follow-up service.
column4: 警察一直在跟踪那辆车。
column5: 警察一直在跟蹤那輛車。
column6: Jǐngchá yīzhí zài gēnzōng nà liàng chē.
column7: The police have been following that car the whole time.
column9: Besides tailing a person (police, detectives, stalkers), it is used for following something over time: 跟蹤調查, 跟蹤報道, 跟蹤服務 for follow-up service.

column3: Used for fixing a mistake that is already out in the open: a newspaper's 更正启事, a statement, a record, a name on a form. It is a formal correction, not a casual one. Here 更 means to change, not the gèng of 更好 that means more.
column4: 报纸更正了昨天的错误。
column5: 報紙更正了昨天的錯誤。
column6: Bàozhǐ gēngzhèng le zuótiān de cuòwù.
column7: The newspaper corrected yesterday's mistake.
column9: Used for fixing a mistake that is already out in the open: a newspaper's 更正啟事, a statement, a record, a name on a form. It is a formal correction, not a casual one. Here 更 means to change, not the gèng of 更好 that means more.

column3: Mostly a noun in news and policy language, where land is counted and protected: 耕地面积, 保护耕地, 耕地减少.
column4: 这个村的耕地越来越少。
column5: 這個村的耕地越來越少。
column6: Zhège cūn de gēngdì yuèláiyuè shǎo.
column7: This village has less and less farmland.
column9: Mostly a noun in news and policy language, where land is counted and protected: 耕地面積, 保護耕地, 耕地減少.

column3: 品 at the end of a word means a kind of goods or article, as in 产品, 商品, 礼品, 纪念品 and 艺术品. 工艺品 are handicrafts, often bought as souvenirs.
column4: 她在市场上买了几件工艺品。
column5: 她在市場上買了幾件工藝品。
column6: Tā zài shìchǎng shàng mǎi le jǐ jiàn gōngyìpǐn.
column7: She bought a few handicrafts at the market.
column9: 品 at the end of a word means a kind of goods or article, as in 產品, 商品, 禮品, 紀念品 and 藝術品. 工藝品 are handicrafts, often bought as souvenirs.

column3: The mainland's police authority at city and county level. Taiwan has no 公安局: the police there work under a 警察局.
column4: 他去公安局报了案。
column5: 他去公安局報了案。
column6: Tā qù gōng'ānjú bào le àn.
column7: He went to the public security bureau to report it.
column9: The mainland's police authority at city and county level. Taiwan has no 公安局: the police there work under a 警察局.

column3: Spoken, and most often about prices and judgments: 价格公道, 说句公道话 (to say a fair word).
column4: 这家店的价格很公道。
column5: 這家店的價格很公道。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de jiàgé hěn gōngdao.
column7: This shop's prices are fair.
column9: Spoken, and most often about prices and judgments: 價格公道, 說句公道話 (to say a fair word).

column3: Short for 公共关系. It names the work, the department and the person doing it: 公关部, 公关公司, 做公关. A 公关危机 is a PR crisis.
column4: 公司成立了专门的公关部门。
column5: 公司成立了專門的公關部門。
column6: Gōngsī chénglì le zhuānmén de gōngguān bùmén.
column7: The company set up a dedicated public relations department.
column9: Short for 公共關係. It names the work, the department and the person doing it: 公關部, 公關公司, 做公關. A 公關危機 is a PR crisis.

column3: An adverb of disapproval: doing something wrong, forbidden or defiant in plain view and without shame. It goes with verbs like 违反, 撒谎, 挑衅: 公然违法.
column4: 他公然违反了规定。
column5: 他公然違反了規定。
column6: Tā gōngrán wéifǎn le guīdìng.
column7: He openly broke the rules.
column9: An adverb of disapproval: doing something wrong, forbidden or defiant in plain view and without shame. It goes with verbs like 違反, 撒謊, 挑釁: 公然違法.

column3: Work done for the government or an official body, as in 公务员 (civil servant), 公务车 (official car) and 因公务出差 (a business trip on official duty).
column4: 他因为公务去北京出差了。
column5: 他因為公務去北京出差了。
column6: Tā yīnwèi gōngwù qù Běijīng chūchāi le.
column7: He went to Beijing on official business.
column9: Work done for the government or an official body, as in 公務員 (civil servant), 公務車 (official car) and 因公務出差 (a business trip on official duty).

column3: A legal step, done at a notary office (公证处), that gives a document official standing: 办理公证, 公证书. It covers contracts, wills, property deeds and certificates.
column4: 这份文件需要公证。
column5: 這份文件需要公證。
column6: Zhè fèn wénjiàn xūyào gōngzhèng.
column7: This document needs to be notarized.
column9: A legal step, done at a notary office (公證處), that gives a document official standing: 辦理公證, 公證書. It covers contracts, wills, property deeds and certificates.

column3: Mostly about who gets the credit: 抢功劳 is to grab it. 没有功劳也有苦劳 says that even without credit there was hard work, a common way to defend effort that went unrewarded.
column4: 这次成功，大家都有功劳。
column5: 這次成功，大家都有功勞。
column6: Zhè cì chénggōng, dàjiā dōu yǒu gōngláo.
column7: Everyone deserves credit for this success.
column9: Mostly about who gets the credit: 搶功勞 is to grab it. 沒有功勞也有苦勞 says that even without credit there was hard work, a common way to defend effort that went unrewarded.

column3: The built-in effect of a substance or method, for medicines, foods, skincare and exercises: 药物的功效, 有……的功效. 效果 is the result you actually get in a given case.
column4: 这种茶据说有清热的功效。
column5: 這種茶據說有清熱的功效。
column6: Zhè zhǒng chá jùshuō yǒu qīngrè de gōngxiào.
column7: This tea is said to have a cooling effect on the body.
column9: The built-in effect of a substance or method, for medicines, foods, skincare and exercises: 藥物的功效, 有……的功效. 效果 is the result you actually get in a given case.

column3: A written, news-style word. Besides taking a fortress or city, it is used for beating a hard problem: 攻克难关, 攻克技术难题.
column4: 科学家终于攻克了这个难题。
column5: 科學家終於攻克了這個難題。
column6: Kēxuéjiā zhōngyú gōngkè le zhège nántí.
column7: Scientists finally cracked this hard problem.
column9: A written, news-style word. Besides taking a fortress or city, it is used for beating a hard problem: 攻克難關, 攻克技術難題.

column3: A business and news phrase for a product that sells out faster than it can be made. Its opposite is 供过于求, when there is more supply than demand.
column4: 新款手机一上市就供不应求。
column5: 新款手機一上市就供不應求。
column6: Xīnkuǎn shǒujī yī shàngshì jiù gōngbùyìngqiú.
column7: The new phone sold out as soon as it came on the market.
column9: A business and news phrase for a product that sells out faster than it can be made. Its opposite is 供過於求, when there is more supply than demand.

column3: The whole palace complex of a ruler. 殿 alone is one hall inside it or inside a temple, as in 大殿.
column4: 游客参观了古老的宫殿。
column5: 遊客參觀了古老的宮殿。
column6: Yóukè cānguān le gǔlǎo de gōngdiàn.
column7: The tourists visited the ancient palace.
column9: The whole palace complex of a ruler. 殿 alone is one hall inside it or inside a temple, as in 大殿.

column3: Found in official country names, such as 中华人民共和国 and 法兰西共和国. Used alone it simply says what kind of state a country is.
column4: 法国是一个共和国。
column5: 法國是一個共和國。
column6: Fǎguó shì yī gè gònghéguó.
column7: France is a republic.
column9: Found in official country names, such as 中華人民共和國 and 法蘭西共和國. Used alone it simply says what kind of state a country is.

column3: Most often figurative: a song, story or opinion that stirs the same feeling in people. It goes with 引起, 产生 or 得到: 引起共鸣. The physics sense is the same idea with sound waves.
column4: 这首歌引起了很多人的共鸣。
column5: 這首歌引起了很多人的共鳴。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē yǐnqǐ le hěn duō rén de gòngmíng.
column7: This song struck a chord with many people.
column9: Most often figurative: a song, story or opinion that stirs the same feeling in people. It goes with 引起, 產生 or 得到: 引起共鳴. The physics sense is the same idea with sound waves.

column3: Always disapproving: it describes people secretly teaming up to do something wrong or illegal, as in 内外勾结 (insiders working with outsiders) or 官商勾结 (officials and business in league). For a neutral team-up, say 合作.
column4: 他们勾结起来骗取了大量的钱。
column5: 他們勾結起來騙取了大量的錢。
column6: Tāmen gōujié qǐlái piànqǔ le dàliàng de qián.
column7: They colluded to swindle out a large amount of money.
column9: Always disapproving: it describes people secretly teaming up to do something wrong or illegal, as in 內外勾結 (insiders working with outsiders) or 官商勾結 (officials and business in league). For a neutral team-up, say 合作.

column3: Besides a real hook for hanging things, it is also used figuratively for a catch that draws people in, such as a striking opening line in an article or video.
column4: 把外套挂在门后的钩子上。
column5: 把外套掛在門後的鉤子上。
column6: Bǎ wàitào guà zài ménhòu de gōuzi shang.
column7: Hang your coat on the hook behind the door.
column9: Besides a real hook for hanging things, it is also used figuratively for a catch that draws people in, such as a striking opening line in an article or video.

column3: The thinking you do in your head before you write, draw or design something: 构思文章, 构思情节. It is also a noun, and a plan can be called 巧妙 (clever) or 独特 (distinctive).
column4: 他正在构思一部新小说。
column5: 他正在構思一部新小說。
column6: Tā zhèngzài gòusī yī bù xīn xiǎoshuō.
column7: He is working out the plan for a new novel.
column9: The thinking you do in your head before you write, draw or design something: 構思文章, 構思情節. It is also a noun, and a plan can be called 巧妙 (clever) or 獨特 (distinctive).

column3: Said of a person, group or country cut off from others and without support. It can also be a verb done to someone: 被孤立 means to be left out. The set phrase 孤立无援 describes being alone with no help coming.
column4: 他在公司里很孤立，没有人愿意和他合作。
column5: 他在公司裡很孤立，沒有人願意和他合作。
column6: Tā zài gōngsī lǐ hěn gūlì, méiyǒu rén yuànyì hé tā hézuò.
column7: He is very isolated at the company; nobody wants to work with him.
column9: Said of a person, group or country cut off from others and without support. It can also be a verb done to someone: 被孤立 means to be left out. The set phrase 孤立無援 describes being alone with no help coming.

column3: An adverb that goes right before the verb: 姑且试试, 姑且不谈 (leave it aside for now). It suggests that this is not the ideal or final answer, but you will go with it anyway. It sounds a little formal.
column4: 你姑且试一试，不行再换别的办法。
column5: 你姑且試一試，不行再換別的辦法。
column6: Nǐ gūqiě shì yī shì, bù xíng zài huàn bié de bànfǎ.
column7: Try it for now, and if that doesn't work, change to another method.
column9: An adverb that goes right before the verb: 姑且試試, 姑且不談 (leave it aside for now). It suggests that this is not the ideal or final answer, but you will go with it anyway. It sounds a little formal.

column3: The thing you let down is usually something given to you in good faith: 辜负期望 (expectations), 辜负信任 (trust), 辜负好意 (kindness), or 辜负青春 (wasting your youth). It is often negated, as a promise: 不会辜负你.
column4: 我不会辜负你的期望。
column5: 我不會辜負你的期望。
column6: Wǒ bù huì gūfù nǐ de qīwàng.
column7: I won't let your expectations down.
column9: The thing you let down is usually something given to you in good faith: 辜負期望 (expectations), 辜負信任 (trust), 辜負好意 (kindness), or 辜負青春 (wasting your youth). It is often negated, as a promise: 不會辜負你.

column3: A fixed compound: 董 here has nothing to do with supervising. It is also said, often jokingly, of a person or thing hopelessly out of date: 老古董.
column4: 爷爷收藏了很多古董。
column5: 爺爺收藏了很多古董。
column6: Yéye shōucáng le hěn duō gǔdǒng.
column7: Grandpa has collected a lot of antiques.
column9: A fixed compound: 董 here has nothing to do with supervising. It is also said, often jokingly, of a person or thing hopelessly out of date: 老古董.

column3: Describes people, tempers, habits, ideas or noises that are odd in a way that makes you uneasy or puzzled: 脾气古怪, 古怪的想法. It is a bit negative, so it is not a compliment the way 特别 can be.
column4: 他的脾气很古怪，大家都不太敢跟他说话。
column5: 他的脾氣很古怪，大家都不太敢跟他說話。
column6: Tā de píqi hěn gǔguài, dàjiā dōu bù tài gǎn gēn tā shuōhuà.
column7: His temper is so odd that most people don't dare talk to him.
column9: Describes people, tempers, habits, ideas or noises that are odd in a way that makes you uneasy or puzzled: 脾氣古怪, 古怪的想法. It is a bit negative, so it is not a compliment the way 特別 can be.

column3: The ownership stake in a company, counted in 股: 持有股份 (hold shares), 占三成股份 (own 30% of the shares), and 股份公司 for a joint-stock company. The listed shares you trade are 股票.
column4: 他在这家公司有一半的股份。
column5: 他在這家公司有一半的股份。
column6: Tā zài zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu yībàn de gǔfèn.
column7: He owns half of the shares in this company.
column9: The ownership stake in a company, counted in 股: 持有股份 (hold shares), 佔三成股份 (own 30% of the shares), and 股份公司 for a joint-stock company. The listed shares you trade are 股票.

column3: Mostly figurative: the core people who carry a team or organization, as in 骨干教师 (key teachers), 技术骨干 or 业务骨干. It is common in news and work reports, and praises the person as someone relied on. The 干 is read gàn here, the 'tree trunk' one, so the main part of a thing.
column4: 他是我们公司的技术骨干。
column5: 他是我們公司的技術骨幹。
column6: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de jìshù gǔgàn.
column7: He is a key technical person at our company.
column9: Mostly figurative: the core people who carry a team or organization, as in 骨幹教師 (key teachers), 技術骨幹 or 業務骨幹. It is common in news and work reports, and praises the person as someone relied on. The 幹 is read gàn here, the 'tree trunk' one, so the main part of a thing.

column3: People urging others to act, usually with a hint of stirring them up: 鼓动群众, 鼓动大家去… For warm, positive encouragement, say 鼓励 instead. 鼓 is built from a drum and a hand holding a drumstick.
column4: 有人鼓动大家去抵制这家店。
column5: 有人鼓動大家去抵制這家店。
column6: Yǒu rén gǔdòng dàjiā qù dǐzhì zhè jiā diàn.
column7: Someone is urging everyone to boycott this shop.
column9: People urging others to act, usually with a hint of stirring them up: 鼓動群眾, 鼓動大家去… For warm, positive encouragement, say 鼓勵 instead. 鼓 is built from a drum and a hand holding a drumstick.

column3: It admits a point, then turns away from it: 价格固然重要，但质量更重要. It sits after the subject and is usually answered by 但是 or 可是 in the next clause; with 也 it grants both sides: 这样固然好，那样也行.
column4: 钱固然重要，但健康更重要。
column5: 錢固然重要，但健康更重要。
column6: Qián gùrán zhòngyào, dàn jiànkāng gèng zhòngyào.
column7: Money is important, admittedly, but health matters more.
column9: It admits a point, then turns away from it: 價格固然重要，但質量更重要. It sits after the subject and is usually answered by 但是 or 可是 in the next clause; with 也 it grants both sides: 這樣固然好，那樣也行.

column3: 体 here is a state of matter, so 固体 sits with 液体 (liquid) and 气体 (gas). The 固 is the "firm, solid" one of 坚固 and 固定.
column4: 水结冰后就变成了固体。
column5: 水結冰後就變成了固體。
column6: Shuǐ jiébīng hòu jiù biànchéng le gùtǐ.
column7: Once water freezes, it becomes a solid.
column9: 體 here is a state of matter, so 固體 sits with 液體 (liquid) and 氣體 (gas). The 固 is the "firm, solid" one of 堅固 and 固定.

column3: A formal word that goes before a noun, usually with 的: 固有的特点, 固有文化. It says a quality belongs to something by nature or has always been part of it, not added from outside.
column4: 每种语言都有自己固有的特点。
column5: 每種語言都有自己固有的特點。
column6: Měi zhǒng yǔyán dōu yǒu zìjǐ gùyǒu de tèdiǎn.
column7: Every language has its own inherent features.
column9: A formal word that goes before a noun, usually with 的: 固有的特點, 固有文化. It says a quality belongs to something by nature or has always been part of it, not added from outside.

column3: Describes a person who sticks to their own view and won't listen, so it is a criticism: 固执的老人, 固执己见. For sticking to something admirable, say 坚持 instead.
column4: 爷爷很固执，不愿意去医院。
column5: 爺爺很固執，不願意去醫院。
column6: Yéye hěn gùzhí, bù yuànyì qù yīyuàn.
column7: Grandpa is stubborn and refuses to go to the hospital.
column9: Describes a person who sticks to their own view and won't listen, so it is a criticism: 固執的老人, 固執己見. For sticking to something admirable, say 堅持 instead.

column3: The worries about consequences that make you hold back: 有顾虑, 顾虑重重 (full of misgivings), 打消顾虑 (set the worries aside). It can also be a verb: 顾虑太多.
column4: 你不用有顾虑，有问题随时问我。
column5: 你不用有顧慮，有問題隨時問我。
column6: Nǐ bùyòng yǒu gùlǜ, yǒu wèntí suíshí wèn wǒ.
column7: You don't need to hold back; ask me any time you have a question.
column9: The worries about consequences that make you hold back: 有顧慮, 顧慮重重 (full of misgivings), 打消顧慮 (set the worries aside). It can also be a verb: 顧慮太多.

column3: Mostly in the compounds that describe the employer–worker relationship: 雇佣关系, 雇佣兵 (mercenary). In plain speech, hiring someone is 请 or 雇.
column4: 公司雇佣了十名新员工。
column5: 公司雇傭了十名新員工。
column6: Gōngsī gùyōng le shí míng xīn yuángōng.
column7: The company hired ten new employees.
column9: Mostly in the compounds that describe the employer–worker relationship: 雇傭關係, 雇傭兵 (mercenary). In plain speech, hiring someone is 請 or 雇.

column3: The verb for using one is 拄: 拄着拐杖. It covers a cane and crutches alike.
column4: 奶奶拄着拐杖慢慢地走。
column5: 奶奶拄著拐杖慢慢地走。
column6: Nǎinai zhǔzhe guǎizhàng mànmàn de zǒu.
column7: Grandma walks slowly with a cane.
column9: The verb for using one is 拄: 拄著拐杖. It covers a cane and crutches alike.

column3: A polite word for looking out for someone, so 请多关照 is what you say when you join a group or meet someone new. It also means to tell or remind someone: 关照他一声.
column4: 刚来公司，请大家多多关照。
column5: 剛來公司，請大家多多關照。
column6: Gāng lái gōngsī, qǐng dàjiā duōduō guānzhào.
column7: I've just joined the company, so please look after me.
column9: A polite word for looking out for someone, so 請多關照 is what you say when you join a group or meet someone new. It also means to tell or remind someone: 關照他一聲.

column3: What an authority such as a government, court or police station is responsible for: 管辖权 (jurisdiction), 管辖范围, 归…管辖. It is formal and rarely said of ordinary managing, which is 管.
column4: 这个案件不归我们法院管辖。
column5: 這個案件不歸我們法院管轄。
column6: Zhège ànjiàn bù guī wǒmen fǎyuàn guǎnxiá.
column7: This case is not under the jurisdiction of our court.
column9: What an authority such as a government, court or police station is responsible for: 管轄權 (jurisdiction), 管轄範圍, 歸…管轄. It is formal and rarely said of ordinary managing, which is 管.

column3: Used for putting a policy, principle or decision fully into practice: 贯彻方针, 贯彻精神, often as 贯彻落实. It is official language, and the object is always something abstract. 贯 began as a picture of two shells strung together.
column4: 学校认真贯彻了上级的指示。
column5: 學校認真貫徹了上級的指示。
column6: Xuéxiào rènzhēn guànchè le shàngjí de zhǐshì.
column7: The school carried out its superiors' instructions carefully.
column9: Used for putting a policy, principle or decision fully into practice: 貫徹方針, 貫徹精神, often as 貫徹落實. It is official language, and the object is always something abstract. 貫 began as a picture of two shells strung together.

column3: The watering of fields and crops, so it turns up with 农田, 庄稼 and 水利: 灌溉系统, 灌溉渠 (irrigation ditch). It is not used for watering a houseplant, which is 浇水.
column4: 农民用河水灌溉农田。
column5: 農民用河水灌溉農田。
column6: Nóngmín yòng héshuǐ guàngài nóngtián.
column7: Farmers irrigate their fields with river water.
column9: The watering of fields and crops, so it turns up with 農田, 莊稼 and 水利: 灌溉系統, 灌溉渠 (irrigation ditch). It is not used for watering a houseplant, which is 澆水.

column3: Besides a bright glow, it means honorable or glorious, and in that sense it is almost always negated: 不光彩 for something shameful, 不太光彩 for a bit disreputable. One old account sees 光 as fire over a person's head.
column4: 他做的事不太光彩。
column5: 他做的事不太光彩。
column6: Tā zuò de shì bù tài guāngcǎi.
column7: What he did is not very honorable.
column9: Besides a bright glow, it means honorable or glorious, and in that sense it is almost always negated: 不光彩 for something shameful, 不太光彩 for a bit disreputable. One old account sees 光 as fire over a person's head.

column3: Rays that shoot out, often in a figurative or poetic sense: 光芒四射 praises someone or something that shines brilliantly, and 万丈光芒 is a glow stretching far. It is more written than 光.
column4: 太阳升起，万丈光芒洒满大地。
column5: 太陽升起，萬丈光芒灑滿大地。
column6: Tàiyáng shēngqǐ, wànzhàng guāngmáng sǎ mǎn dàdì.
column7: The sun rises and its rays spill over the whole land.
column9: Rays that shoot out, often in a figurative or poetic sense: 光芒四射 praises someone or something that shines brilliantly, and 萬丈光芒 is a glow stretching far. It is more written than 光.

column3: It opens a clause that gives the real reason or bottom line, after surface reasons have been listed: 归根到底，问题出在…. It is a set phrase, common in speeches and arguments, in speech and writing.
column4: 归根到底，这是态度问题。
column5: 歸根到底，這是態度問題。
column6: Guīgēndàodǐ, zhè shì tàidù wèntí.
column7: In the final analysis, this is a question of attitude.
column9: It opens a clause that gives the real reason or bottom line, after surface reasons have been listed: 歸根到底，問題出在…. It is a set phrase, common in speeches and arguments, in speech and writing.

column3: A somewhat formal word for giving back something borrowed or taken, such as library books, a deposit or land. In everyday speech 还 alone does the job (还书, 还钱).
column4: 请在下周五之前把书归还图书馆。
column5: 請在下週五之前把書歸還圖書館。
column6: Qǐng zài xià zhōuwǔ zhīqián bǎ shū guīhuán túshūguǎn.
column7: Please return the book to the library before next Friday.
column9: A somewhat formal word for giving back something borrowed or taken, such as library books, a deposit or land. In everyday speech 還 alone does the job (還書, 還錢).

column3: The size, model or grade of a product: things come in different 规格, and a buyer asks which one. It also describes the level of an event, so 高规格 means a top-level reception or meeting.
column4: 这种螺丝有好几种规格，你要哪种？
column5: 這種螺絲有好幾種規格，你要哪種？
column6: Zhè zhǒng luósī yǒu hǎo jǐ zhǒng guīgé, nǐ yào nǎ zhǒng?
column7: This kind of screw comes in several sizes. Which one do you want?
column9: The size, model or grade of a product: things come in different 規格, and a buyer asks which one. It also describes the level of an event, so 高規格 means a top-level reception or meeting.

column3: The written rules of a company, school or government office. It is usually paired with 制度 as 规章制度, and you follow it (遵守规章) or break it (违反规章).
column4: 员工必须遵守公司的规章制度。
column5: 員工必須遵守公司的規章制度。
column6: Yuángōng bìxū zūnshǒu gōngsī de guīzhāng zhìdù.
column7: Employees must obey the company's rules and regulations.
column9: The written rules of a company, school or government office. It is usually paired with 制度 as 規章制度, and you follow it (遵守規章) or break it (違反規章).

column3: Sticks as things to hit with: weapons in a fight, or a way of punishing. 棍棒教育 is the old idea of bringing up children by beating them.
column4: 一群人拿着棍棒冲了过来。
column5: 一群人拿著棍棒衝了過來。
column6: Yī qún rén názhe gùnbàng chōng le guòlái.
column7: A group of people came rushing over with sticks.
column9: Sticks as things to hit with: weapons in a fight, or a way of punishing. 棍棒教育 is the old idea of bringing up children by beating them.

column3: National defense as a field of government and the military. It mostly appears at the front of compounds such as 国防部 (the defense ministry), 国防预算 and 国防教育.
column4: 政府今年增加了国防预算。
column5: 政府今年增加了國防預算。
column6: Zhèngfǔ jīnnián zēngjiā le guófáng yùsuàn.
column7: The government increased its defense budget this year.
column9: National defense as a field of government and the military. It mostly appears at the front of compounds such as 國防部 (the defense ministry), 國防預算 and 國防教育.

column3: On the mainland, the State Council: the government's cabinet, led by the premier. Taiwan's cabinet is the 行政院. For the United States the same word means the State Department.
column4: 国务院发布了新的通知。
column5: 國務院發布了新的通知。
column6: Guówùyuàn fābù le xīn de tōngzhī.
column7: The State Council issued a new notice.
column9: On the mainland, the State Council: the government's cabinet, led by the premier. Taiwan's cabinet is the 行政院. For the United States the same word means the State Department.

column3: Praise for someone who decides quickly and sticks to it, or for a decision itself. It goes with leaders and with 措施 (measures): 采取果断措施 is to take decisive action. The 果 here is its sense of resolute, not fruit.
column4: 她做决定很果断，从来不犹豫。
column5: 她做決定很果斷，從來不猶豫。
column6: Tā zuò juédìng hěn guǒduàn, cónglái bù yóuyù.
column7: She is decisive when she makes decisions and never hesitates.
column9: Praise for someone who decides quickly and sticks to it, or for a decision itself. It goes with leaders and with 措施 (measures): 採取果斷措施 is to take decisive action. The 果 here is its sense of resolute, not fruit.

column3: A polite, modest reply to a compliment: you say it about the praise you received, never about someone else. 您过奖了 is the usual form, often followed by a bit of self-deprecation.
column4: 您过奖了，我还有很多地方要学。
column5: 您過獎了，我還有很多地方要學。
column6: Nín guòjiǎng le, wǒ hái yǒu hěn duō dìfang yào xué.
column7: You flatter me. I still have a lot to learn.
column9: A polite, modest reply to a compliment: you say it about the praise you received, never about someone else. 您過獎了 is the usual form, often followed by a bit of self-deprecation.

column3: A fault or mistake that was not meant, so it is set against 故意 (on purpose). In law it is negligence, as in 过失致人死亡 (causing a death through negligence).
column4: 这次事故是由于工作人员的过失造成的。
column5: 這次事故是由於工作人員的過失造成的。
column6: Zhè cì shìgù shì yóuyú gōngzuò rényuán de guòshī zàochéng de.
column7: This accident was caused by the staff's negligence.
column9: A fault or mistake that was not meant, so it is set against 故意 (on purpose). In law it is negligence, as in 過失致人死亡 (causing a death through negligence).

column3: To step in and ask about something, as an outsider or one in charge. It turns up most in the negative: 不过问 means to leave it alone, and 无权过问 means it is none of your business.
column4: 他从来不过问孩子的学习。
column5: 他從來不過問孩子的學習。
column6: Tā cónglái bù guòwèn háizi de xuéxí.
column7: He never gets involved in his children's studies.
column9: To step in and ask about something, as an outsider or one in charge. It turns up most in the negative: 不過問 means to leave it alone, and 無權過問 means it is none of your business.

column3: Said of something you enjoy so fully that you feel completely satisfied: a spicy meal, a game, a sports match. It is often a complement: 玩得很过瘾. As verb plus object (瘾, a craving), it can be split: 过了一把瘾.
column4: 这顿火锅吃得真过瘾！
column5: 這頓火鍋吃得真過癮！
column6: Zhè dùn huǒguō chī de zhēn guòyǐn!
column7: This hot pot meal was so satisfying!
column9: Said of something you enjoy so fully that you feel completely satisfied: a spicy meal, a game, a sports match. It is often a complement: 玩得很過癮. As verb plus object (癮, a craving), it can be split: 過了一把癮.

column3: The number follows it: 海拔三千米. A place is said to have a high or low 海拔, and the word comes up for mountains, plateaus and cities.
column4: 这个地方海拔很高，空气比较稀薄。
column5: 這個地方海拔很高，空氣比較稀薄。
column6: Zhège dìfang hǎibá hěn gāo, kōngqì bǐjiào xībó.
column7: This place is at a high elevation, and the air is rather thin.
column9: The number follows it: 海拔三千米. A place is said to have a high or low 海拔, and the word comes up for mountains, plateaus and cities.

column3: A written word for the seaside, used for resort areas and coastal towns: 海滨城市, 海滨浴场 (a swimming beach). In plain speech people say 海边.
column4: 我们在海滨度过了一个愉快的周末。
column5: 我們在海濱度過了一個愉快的週末。
column6: Wǒmen zài hǎibīn dùguò le yī gè yúkuài de zhōumò.
column7: We spent a pleasant weekend at the seaside.
column9: A written word for the seaside, used for resort areas and coastal towns: 海濱城市, 海濱浴場 (a swimming beach). In plain speech people say 海邊.

column3: Vague or unclear, said of an answer, a reply or a position. The negative 不含糊 flips it: someone who does a job 一点儿不含糊 does it without cutting corners, and you are impressed.
column4: 他回答得很含糊，没说清楚到底来不来。
column5: 他回答得很含糊，沒說清楚到底來不來。
column6: Tā huídá de hěn hánhu, méi shuō qīngchu dàodǐ lái bù lái.
column7: His answer was vague, and he did not say clearly whether he was coming.
column9: Vague or unclear, said of an answer, a reply or a position. The negative 不含糊 flips it: someone who does a job 一點兒不含糊 does it without cutting corners, and you are impressed.

column3: The small talk at the start of a meeting, before business begins. As a verb it is usually given a short count: 寒暄几句, 寒暄了一番. It pairs cold with warm because the first thing people comment on when they meet is the weather.
column4: 两人见面后寒暄了几句，就开始谈正事。
column5: 兩人見面後寒暄了幾句，就開始談正事。
column6: Liǎng rén jiànmiàn hòu hánxuān le jǐ jù, jiù kāishǐ tán zhèngshì.
column7: The two exchanged a few pleasantries after meeting, then got down to business.
column9: The small talk at the start of a meeting, before business begins. As a verb it is usually given a short count: 寒暄幾句, 寒暄了一番. It pairs cold with warm because the first thing people comment on when they meet is the weather.

column3: A written, slightly formal word for what is seldom seen: a rare disease, a rare event, a rare talent. It is more bookish than 少见, and 十分罕见 or 极为罕见 are common.
column4: 这种病在儿童中非常罕见。
column5: 這種病在兒童中非常罕見。
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng zài értóng zhōng fēicháng hǎnjiàn.
column7: This disease is extremely rare in children.
column9: A written, slightly formal word for what is seldom seen: a rare disease, a rare event, a rare talent. It is more bookish than 少見, and 十分罕見 or 極為罕見 are common.

column3: A strong, serious word for defending something that matters: rights, sovereignty, dignity, the truth. The object is usually abstract. For guarding a person or a thing, 保护 is the everyday choice.
column4: 我们要坚决捍卫自己的合法权益。
column5: 我們要堅決捍衛自己的合法權益。
column6: Wǒmen yào jiānjué hànwèi zìjǐ de héfǎ quányì.
column7: We must firmly defend our legal rights and interests.
column9: A strong, serious word for defending something that matters: rights, sovereignty, dignity, the truth. The object is usually abstract. For guarding a person or a thing, 保護 is the everyday choice.

column3: Ranks or lines of people, and in figurative use the group one joins: 加入……的行列 is to join the ranks of something, 跻身……行列 to make it into a group. The 行 here is read háng, row, not xíng.
column4: 越来越多的人加入了跑步的行列。
column5: 越來越多的人加入了跑步的行列。
column6: Yuè lái yuè duō de rén jiārù le pǎobù de hángliè.
column7: More and more people have joined the ranks of runners.
column9: Ranks or lines of people, and in figurative use the group one joins: 加入……的行列 is to join the ranks of something, 躋身……行列 to make it into a group. The 行 here is read háng, row, not xíng.

column3: Travel in space, as against 航空, flight within the atmosphere. It forms 航天员 (astronaut), 航天局 (space agency) and 航天事业 (the space program). This is the mainland word; Taiwan says 太空 (太空人 for an astronaut) and 航太 for aerospace.
column4: 中国的航天事业发展得很快。
column5: 中國的航天事業發展得很快。
column6: Zhōngguó de hángtiān shìyè fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
column7: China's space program is developing fast.
column9: Travel in space, as against 航空, flight within the atmosphere. It forms 航天員 (astronaut), 航天局 (space agency) and 航天事業 (the space program). This is the mainland word; Taiwan says 太空 (太空人 for an astronaut) and 航太 for aerospace.

column3: A ship or aircraft traveling along its route, for a stretch of time: 在海上航行, 航行速度. It is for ships above all; a plane's flight is more often 飞行.
column4: 这艘船正在太平洋上航行。
column5: 這艘船正在太平洋上航行。
column6: Zhè sōu chuán zhèngzài Tàipíngyáng shàng hángxíng.
column7: This ship is sailing on the Pacific Ocean.
column9: A ship or aircraft traveling along its route, for a stretch of time: 在海上航行, 航行速度. It is for ships above all; a plane's flight is more often 飛行.

column3: Praise for a bold, free and generous spirit, in a person's manner or in an artwork: 豪迈的笑声 (hearty laughter), 气概豪迈, a poem in a 豪迈 style. It is a little literary.
column4: 他豪迈地举起酒杯。
column5: 他豪邁地舉起酒杯。
column6: Tā háomài de jǔqǐ jiǔbēi.
column7: He raised his glass with a bold gesture.
column9: Praise for a bold, free and generous spirit, in a person's manner or in an artwork: 豪邁的笑聲 (hearty laughter), 氣概豪邁, a poem in a 豪邁 style. It is a little literary.

column3: To use up time, money, energy or materials, and it suggests a lot is lost for the result: 耗费大量时间, 耗费精力. 花 is the neutral word for spending, with no sense of waste.
column4: 这件事耗费了我们很多时间。
column5: 這件事耗費了我們很多時間。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hàofèi le wǒmen hěn duō shíjiān.
column7: This matter took up a lot of our time.
column9: To use up time, money, energy or materials, and it suggests a lot is lost for the result: 耗費大量時間, 耗費精力. 花 is the neutral word for spending, with no sense of waste.

column3: Mostly seen in 呵呵, the sound of a chuckle, and in 呵护 (to look after with tenderness). In online chat 呵呵 can come across as cold or dismissive rather than friendly.
column4: 他呵呵地笑了起来。
column5: 他呵呵地笑了起來。
column6: Tā hē hē de xiào le qǐlái.
column7: He started to chuckle.
column9: Mostly seen in 呵呵, the sound of a chuckle, and in 呵護 (to look after with tenderness). In online chat 呵呵 can come across as cold or dismissive rather than friendly.

column3: To go into business together, sharing the money put in and the profit. 合伙人 is a partner (in a firm, a restaurant), and 伙 is the same one found in 伙伴.
column4: 他们俩合伙开了一家餐馆。
column5: 他們倆合夥開了一家餐館。
column6: Tāmen liǎ héhuǒ kāi le yī jiā cānguǎn.
column7: The two of them opened a restaurant together as partners.
column9: To go into business together, sharing the money put in and the profit. 合夥人 is a partner (in a firm, a restaurant), and 夥 is the same one found in 夥伴.

column3: A gentle, kindly manner that puts people at ease, often said of elders, teachers and doctors. 和蔼可亲 (kindly and approachable) is the usual set phrase, and a voice, smile or expression can be 和蔼 too.
column4: 王老师说话总是很和蔼。
column5: 王老師說話總是很和藹。
column6: Wáng lǎoshī shuōhuà zǒngshì hěn hé'ǎi.
column7: Teacher Wang always speaks very kindly.
column9: A gentle, kindly manner that puts people at ease, often said of elders, teachers and doctors. 和藹可親 (kindly and approachable) is the usual set phrase, and a voice, smile or expression can be 和藹 too.

column3: Used for ending a dispute by agreement, whether between two sides in a lawsuit, two countries, or friends and family after a quarrel. The other side comes after 与, as in 与他和解, and 庭外和解 is a settlement out of court.
column4: 他们终于和解了。
column5: 他們終於和解了。
column6: Tāmen zhōngyú héjiě le.
column7: They finally made up.
column9: Used for ending a dispute by agreement, whether between two sides in a lawsuit, two countries, or friends and family after a quarrel. The other side comes after 與, as in 與他和解, and 庭外和解 is a settlement out of court.

column3: Describes how people live together: a family, neighbors, or two nations. It is a state, so it sits in phrases like 家庭和睦 and 和睦相处, rather than being something you do.
column4: 邻居们相处得很和睦。
column5: 鄰居們相處得很和睦。
column6: Línjūmen xiāngchǔ de hěn hémù.
column7: The neighbors get along very harmoniously.
column9: Describes how people live together: a family, neighbors, or two nations. It is a state, so it sits in phrases like 家庭和睦 and 和睦相處, rather than being something you do.

column3: Two uses: as an adjective for someone who is cold-hearted (一个狠心的人), and as a verb for steeling yourself to do something hard, often as 下狠心 or 狠下心.
column4: 他狠心把狗送走了。
column5: 他狠心把狗送走了。
column6: Tā hěnxīn bǎ gǒu sòng zǒu le.
column7: He steeled himself and sent the dog away.
column9: Two uses: as an adjective for someone who is cold-hearted (一個狠心的人), and as a verb for steeling yourself to do something hard, often as 下狠心 or 狠下心.

column3: A sound word with a few jobs: humming a tune (哼歌), a grunt or groan of pain, and a scornful snort written 哼!
column4: 她一边做饭，一边哼着歌。
column5: 她一邊做飯，一邊哼著歌。
column6: Tā yībiān zuòfàn, yībiān hēng zhe gē.
column7: She hummed a song while cooking.
column9: A sound word with a few jobs: humming a tune (哼歌), a grunt or groan of pain, and a scornful snort written 哼!

column3: Said of news, a film, a trial or an event that has everyone talking. It works as a verb (这件事轰动了全城) and as a noun after 引起, and 轰动一时 means a sensation for a while.
column4: 这部电影在全国引起了轰动。
column5: 這部電影在全國引起了轟動。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài quánguó yǐnqǐ le hōngdòng.
column7: The movie caused a sensation across the country.
column9: Said of news, a film, a trial or an event that has everyone talking. It works as a verb (這件事轟動了全城) and as a noun after 引起, and 轟動一時 means a sensation for a while.

column3: Dry or warm something with dry heat, not by boiling: 烘干 is to dry out, 烘焙 to bake, and 烘烤 to roast or toast.
column4: 他把湿衣服放在火边烘干。
column5: 他把濕衣服放在火邊烘乾。
column6: Tā bǎ shī yīfu fàng zài huǒ biān hōng gān.
column7: He put the wet clothes by the fire to dry.
column9: Dry or warm something with dry heat, not by boiling: 烘乾 is to dry out, 烘焙 to bake, and 烘烤 to roast or toast.

column3: The opposite of 微观 (microscopic). It means looking at the whole picture rather than the details, and turns up mostly in formal or technical talk: 宏观经济 is macroeconomics and 宏观调控 is government steering of the economy.
column4: 政府要从宏观上控制物价。
column5: 政府要從宏觀上控制物價。
column6: Zhèngfǔ yào cóng hóngguān shàng kòngzhì wùjià.
column7: The government must control prices from the big-picture level.
column9: The opposite of 微觀 (microscopic). It means looking at the whole picture rather than the details, and turns up mostly in formal or technical talk: 宏觀經濟 is macroeconomics and 宏觀調控 is government steering of the economy.

column3: Describes big, impressive things, such as buildings, projects and plans, with a sense of awe: 宏伟的建筑, 宏伟的计划. It is not said of a person; a great person is 伟大.
column4: 故宫的建筑非常宏伟。
column5: 故宮的建築非常宏偉。
column6: Gùgōng de jiànzhù fēicháng hóngwěi.
column7: The buildings of the Forbidden City are magnificent.
column9: Describes big, impressive things, such as buildings, projects and plans, with a sense of awe: 宏偉的建築, 宏偉的計劃. It is not said of a person; a great person is 偉大.

column3: Used for coaxing or soothing a child (哄孩子睡觉), and for fooling or sweet-talking someone into something (哄人). Read hōng, it is the roar of a crowd, as in 哄堂大笑, the whole room bursting into laughter.
column4: 妈妈正在哄宝宝睡觉。
column5: 媽媽正在哄寶寶睡覺。
column6: Māma zhèngzài hǒng bǎobao shuìjiào.
column7: Mom is getting the baby to sleep.
column9: Used for coaxing or soothing a child (哄孩子睡覺), and for fooling or sweet-talking someone into something (哄人). Read hōng, it is the roar of a crowd, as in 哄堂大笑, the whole room bursting into laughter.

column3: Louder and angrier than 喊. People 吼 when furious or excited, and lions, engines and the wind can too, as in 北风怒吼.
column4: 他气得对着我大吼。
column5: 他氣得對著我大吼。
column6: Tā qì de duìzhe wǒ dà hǒu.
column7: He was so angry he yelled at me.
column9: Louder and angrier than 喊. People 吼 when furious or excited, and lions, engines and the wind can too, as in 北風怒吼.

column3: The worry is about what you leave behind: family, money or home that would pull at you while you push ahead. It is nearly always negated or removed, as in 没有后顾之忧 and 解除后顾之忧, and belongs to written and formal speech.
column4: 公司帮他安排好家人，让他没有后顾之忧。
column5: 公司幫他安排好家人，讓他沒有後顧之憂。
column6: Gōngsī bāng tā ānpái hǎo jiārén, ràng tā méiyǒu hòugùzhīyōu.
column7: The company took care of his family, so he had nothing to worry about back home.
column9: The worry is about what you leave behind: family, money or home that would pull at you while you push ahead. It is nearly always negated or removed, as in 沒有後顧之憂 and 解除後顧之憂, and belongs to written and formal speech.

column3: The support work behind the front line: supplies, transport, housing and meals. It began with armies, but is used for any organization, as in 后勤部门, 后勤人员 and 后勤保障.
column4: 他在学校负责后勤工作。
column5: 他在學校負責後勤工作。
column6: Tā zài xuéxiào fùzé hòuqín gōngzuò.
column7: He is in charge of support services at the school.
column9: The support work behind the front line: supplies, transport, housing and meals. It began with armies, but is used for any organization, as in 後勤部門, 後勤人員 and 後勤保障.

column3: It only goes before another word: 候选人 is a candidate and 候选名单 the shortlist. The same 候选 is used for nominated works and songs.
column4: 她是这次选举的候选人之一。
column5: 她是這次選舉的候選人之一。
column6: Tā shì zhè cì xuǎnjǔ de hòuxuǎn rén zhī yī.
column7: She is one of the candidates in this election.
column9: It only goes before another word: 候選人 is a candidate and 候選名單 the shortlist. The same 候選 is used for nominated works and songs.

column3: Warmer and more emotional than 叫 or 喊. You call out to someone, and a feeling or duty can call to you, as in 祖国的呼唤 and 良知的呼唤.
column4: 妈妈在门口呼唤着孩子的名字。
column5: 媽媽在門口呼喚著孩子的名字。
column6: Māma zài ménkǒu hūhuàn zhe háizi de míngzi.
column7: Mom stood at the door calling her child's name.
column9: Warmer and more emotional than 叫 or 喊. You call out to someone, and a feeling or duty can call to you, as in 祖國的呼喚 and 良知的呼喚.

column3: A long, loud, piercing sound made by something moving fast: wind, a train, bullets, a siren. It is mostly written, in phrases like 北风呼啸 and 呼啸而过, to rush past with a roar.
column4: 一列火车呼啸而过。
column5: 一列火車呼嘯而過。
column6: Yī liè huǒchē hūxiào ér guò.
column7: A train roared past.
column9: A long, loud, piercing sound made by something moving fast: wind, a train, bullets, a siren. It is mostly written, in phrases like 北風呼嘯 and 呼嘯而過, to rush past with a roar.

column3: A public appeal, usually from an expert, an official or a group to the public, and common in news: 呼吁大家 and 发出呼吁. It works as a verb and as a noun.
column4: 专家呼吁大家多喝水。
column5: 專家呼籲大家多喝水。
column6: Zhuānjiā hūyù dàjiā duō hē shuǐ.
column7: Experts urge everyone to drink more water.
column9: A public appeal, usually from an expert, an official or a group to the public, and common in news: 呼籲大家 and 發出呼籲. It works as a verb and as a noun.

column3: An adverb that goes before a verb: doing something carelessly or at random, as in 胡乱吃, 胡乱猜 and 胡乱花钱. It sounds disapproving, and 胡 works the same way in 胡说 and 胡闹.
column4: 他胡乱吃了几口就走了。
column5: 他胡亂吃了幾口就走了。
column6: Tā húluàn chī le jǐ kǒu jiù zǒu le.
column7: He bolted down a few bites and left.
column9: An adverb that goes before a verb: doing something carelessly or at random, as in 胡亂吃, 胡亂猜 and 胡亂花錢. It sounds disapproving, and 胡 works the same way in 胡說 and 胡鬧.

column3: The general word for facial hair, beard and mustache together. In everyday speech 胡子 is more common, and 胡须 is what you write or say of an older man or a long beard. The 胡 here is thought to come from a word for the dewlap of an animal, the part that hangs down from the chin.
column4: 他留着一把长胡须。
column5: 他留著一把長鬍鬚。
column6: Tā liú zhe yī bǎ cháng húxū.
column7: He wears a long beard.
column9: The general word for facial hair, beard and mustache together. In everyday speech 鬍子 is more common, and 鬍鬚 is what you write or say of an older man or a long beard. The 鬍 here is thought to come from a word for the dewlap of an animal, the part that hangs down from the chin.

column3: A general or written word for lakes as a group, such as the lakes of a region: 湖泊污染, 湖泊面积. A single named lake is just 湖, as in 太湖. Taiwan reads the 泊 as bó; the mainland says pō.
column4: 青海湖是中国最大的湖泊。
column5: 青海湖是中國最大的湖泊。
column6: Qīnghǎi Hú shì Zhōngguó zuìdà de húpō.
column7: Qinghai Lake is the largest lake in China.
