column9: A general or written word for lakes as a group, such as the lakes of a region: 湖泊污染, 湖泊面積. A single named lake is just 湖, as in 太湖. Taiwan reads the 泊 as bó; the mainland says pō.

column3: 瓣 is also the measure word for petals and for the natural sections of fruit and garlic: 一瓣蒜 is a clove of garlic and 一瓣橘子 a segment of a mandarin orange.
column4: 地上落满了白色的花瓣。
column5: 地上落滿了白色的花瓣。
column6: Dìshang luò mǎn le báisè de huābàn.
column7: The ground was covered with white petals.
column9: 瓣 is also the measure word for petals and for the natural sections of fruit and garlic: 一瓣蒜 is a clove of garlic and 一瓣橘子 a segment of a mandarin orange.

column3: 蕾 almost never stands alone. Besides 花蕾 there is the more literary 蓓蕾, which is also used for children or talents that have yet to bloom.
column4: 春天到了，树枝上长出了花蕾。
column5: 春天到了，樹枝上長出了花蕾。
column6: Chūntiān dào le, shùzhī shàng zhǎng chū le huālěi.
column7: Spring has come, and buds have appeared on the branches.
column9: 蕾 almost never stands alone. Besides 花蕾 there is the more literary 蓓蕾, which is also used for children or talents that have yet to bloom.

column3: Describes things that look rich and showy: clothes, buildings, a stage, or language and style (华丽的辞藻). When the style is overdone it can mean flashy rather than beautiful. 华 comes from a character that began as a picture of a plant in flower, the original form of 花.
column4: 她穿着一件华丽的礼服。
column5: 她穿著一件華麗的禮服。
column6: Tā chuān zhe yī jiàn huálì de lǐfú.
column7: She wore a gorgeous gown.
column9: Describes things that look rich and showy: clothes, buildings, a stage, or language and style (華麗的辭藻). When the style is overdone it can mean flashy rather than beautiful. 華 comes from a character that began as a picture of a plant in flower, the original form of 花.

column3: 化 here is short for 化学, so 化肥 is the manufactured kind of fertilizer, as against 有机肥, organic fertilizer. The same short 化 is in 化工 and 化验.
column4: 农民给田里施了很多化肥。
column5: 農民給田裡施了很多化肥。
column6: Nóngmín gěi tián lǐ shī le hěn duō huàféi.
column7: The farmers put a lot of chemical fertilizer on the field.
column9: 化 here is short for 化學, so 化肥 is the manufactured kind of fertilizer, as against 有機肥, organic fertilizer. The same short 化 is in 化工 and 化驗.

column3: A lab test of blood, urine, water or food: 化验血液 is to have blood tested, 化验单 the lab report and 化验结果 the result.
column4: 医生让他去化验血液。
column5: 醫生讓他去化驗血液。
column6: Yīshēng ràng tā qù huàyàn xuèyè.
column7: The doctor sent him to have his blood tested.
column9: A lab test of blood, urine, water or food: 化驗血液 is to have blood tested, 化驗單 the lab report and 化驗結果 the result.

column3: Used to criticize overdoing it: adding an unneeded extra touch that spoils something already good, as in 不要画蛇添足. It comes from an old story of a drawing contest in which the man who finished first gave his snake legs and lost.
column4: 这篇文章已经很好了，再改就是画蛇添足了。
column5: 這篇文章已經很好了，再改就是畫蛇添足了。
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng yǐjīng hěn hǎo le, zài gǎi jiù shì huàshétiānzú le.
column7: This essay is already good; changing it more would just be gilding the lily.
column9: Used to criticize overdoing it: adding an unneeded extra touch that spoils something already good, as in 不要畫蛇添足. It comes from an old story of a drawing contest in which the man who finished first gave his snake legs and lost.

column3: In Taiwan the microphone is usually 麦克风, and 话筒 mostly the phone handset (拿起话筒 is to pick up the receiver); on the mainland 话筒 is also the everyday word for a handheld microphone, on stage or in a meeting.
column4: 请把话筒递给后面的同学。
column5: 請把話筒遞給後面的同學。
column6: Qǐng bǎ huàtǒng dì gěi hòumiàn de tóngxué.
column7: Please pass the microphone to the student in back.
column9: In Taiwan the microphone is usually 麥克風, and 話筒 mostly the phone handset (拿起話筒 is to pick up the receiver); on the mainland 話筒 is also the everyday word for a handheld microphone, on stage or in a meeting.

column3: Used for bringing something back to how it was or really happened: a file after a mistake, a crime scene, the facts of an event. 还 also has the reading hái, "still", but in this word it is huán, "to return".
column4: 警方正在还原事故现场。
column5: 警方正在還原事故現場。
column6: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài huányuán shìgù xiànchǎng.
column7: The police are reconstructing the scene of the accident.
column9: Used for bringing something back to how it was or really happened: a file after a mistake, a crime scene, the facts of an event. 還 also has the reading hái, "still", but in this word it is huán, "to return".

column3: Describes a place with no people and little growth: a wasteland, an abandoned village, a bare mountainside. 荒 alone marks land left wild, as in 荒地 and 荒山.
column4: 这片土地十分荒凉，几乎没有人住。
column5: 這片土地十分荒涼，幾乎沒有人住。
column6: Zhè piàn tǔdì shífēn huāngliáng, jīhū méiyǒu rén zhù.
column7: This land is utterly desolate, and almost no one lives there.
column9: Describes a place with no people and little growth: a wasteland, an abandoned village, a bare mountainside. 荒 alone marks land left wild, as in 荒地 and 荒山.

column3: Strongly critical: said of ideas, claims, arguments or situations that make no sense, as in 荒谬的理论 or 荒谬的局面.
column4: 这个说法太荒谬了，没有人会相信。
column5: 這個說法太荒謬了，沒有人會相信。
column6: Zhège shuōfǎ tài huāngmiù le, méiyǒu rén huì xiāngxìn.
column7: This claim is too absurd; no one will believe it.
column9: Strongly critical: said of ideas, claims, arguments or situations that make no sense, as in 荒謬的理論 or 荒謬的局面.

column3: Said of behavior, excuses or ideas that go against common sense, often as a scolding: 太荒唐了! It can also describe a reckless, wild way of living. Here 唐 is not the dynasty; the character can mean "to exaggerate" or "empty".
column4: 你竟然为了这点小事就辞职，太荒唐了！
column5: 你竟然為了這點小事就辭職，太荒唐了！
column6: Nǐ jìngrán wèile zhè diǎn xiǎoshì jiù cízhí, tài huāngtáng le!
column7: You quit over such a small thing? That is ridiculous!
column9: Said of behavior, excuses or ideas that go against common sense, often as a scolding: 太荒唐了! It can also describe a reckless, wild way of living. Here 唐 is not the dynasty; the character can mean "to exaggerate" or "empty".

column3: The partner of 皇帝. A king's wife is 王后 instead, and a queen who rules in her own right is 女王. 后 was itself an old word for a ruler.
column4: 皇后陪着皇帝一起出席了典礼。
column5: 皇后陪著皇帝一起出席了典禮。
column6: Huánghòu péizhe huángdì yīqǐ chūxí le diǎnlǐ.
column7: The empress attended the ceremony together with the emperor.
column9: The partner of 皇帝. A king's wife is 王后 instead, and a queen who rules in her own right is 女王. 后 was itself an old word for a ruler.

column3: A written, storytelling idiom for the moment a puzzle clicks, often followed by 原来 ("so that's it") or preceded by 这才. 恍 can mean a hazy state of mind, or snapping out of that state.
column4: 听了他的解释，我才恍然大悟。
column5: 聽了他的解釋，我才恍然大悟。
column6: Tīngle tā de jiěshì, wǒ cái huǎngrándàwù.
column7: Only after hearing his explanation did it suddenly dawn on me.
column9: A written, storytelling idiom for the moment a puzzle clicks, often followed by 原來 ("so that's it") or preceded by 這才. 恍 can mean a hazy state of mind, or snapping out of that state.

column3: The thing that sways comes right after it: 晃脑袋 shakes the head, 晃瓶子 shakes a bottle. It is also in 摇晃 and 晃来晃去. The same character read huǎng means to dazzle or flash past.
column4: 他一边说话，一边晃着手里的杯子。
column5: 他一邊說話，一邊晃著手裡的杯子。
column6: Tā yībiān shuōhuà, yībiān huàng zhe shǒu li de bēizi.
column7: While talking, he kept swirling the glass in his hand.
column9: The thing that sways comes right after it: 晃腦袋 shakes the head, 晃瓶子 shakes a bottle. It is also in 搖晃 and 晃來晃去. The same character read huǎng means to dazzle or flash past.

column3: Almost always about money spent freely and without thought, as in 挥霍无度. It also takes time and youth: 挥霍青春 is to waste one's best years.
column4: 他把父母留下的钱都挥霍光了。
column5: 他把父母留下的錢都揮霍光了。
column6: Tā bǎ fùmǔ liúxià de qián dōu huīhuò guāng le.
column7: He squandered all the money his parents left him.
column9: Almost always about money spent freely and without thought, as in 揮霍無度. It also takes time and youth: 揮霍青春 is to waste one's best years.

column3: Praises achievements, history, careers and victories more often than light itself: 辉煌的成就, 辉煌的历史. It can also describe a brilliantly lit building.
column4: 这支球队取得了辉煌的成绩。
column5: 這支球隊取得了輝煌的成績。
column6: Zhè zhī qiúduì qǔdé le huīhuáng de chéngjì.
column7: This team has achieved brilliant results.
column9: Praises achievements, history, careers and victories more often than light itself: 輝煌的成就, 輝煌的歷史. It can also describe a brilliantly lit building.

column3: A heavy word: the regret felt over a mistake that cannot be undone, as in 悔恨不已 or 充满悔恨. 恨 can mean "to regret" as well as "to hate".
column4: 他对自己当年的决定充满悔恨。
column5: 他對自己當年的決定充滿悔恨。
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ dāngnián de juédìng chōngmǎn huǐhèn.
column7: He is full of remorse over his decision back then.
column9: A heavy word: the regret felt over a mistake that cannot be undone, as in 悔恨不已 or 充滿悔恨. 恨 can mean "to regret" as well as "to hate".

column3: Total destruction on a large scale: a city, a species, the planet, a dream. For a broken cup or fence, 弄坏 or 毁坏 is the word.
column4: 战争可能毁灭整个城市。
column5: 戰爭可能毀滅整個城市。
column6: Zhànzhēng kěnéng huǐmiè zhěnggè chéngshì.
column7: War can destroy an entire city.
column9: Total destruction on a large scale: a city, a species, the planet, a dream. For a broken cup or fence, 弄壞 or 毀壞 is the word.

column3: A formal, news-style word: leaders, ministers and envoys 会晤, as in 两国领导人会晤. Friends meeting up say 见面.
column4: 两国外长将于明天在北京会晤。
column5: 兩國外長將於明天在北京會晤。
column6: Liǎngguó wàizhǎng jiāng yú míngtiān zài Běijīng huìwù.
column7: The two countries' foreign ministers will meet in Beijing tomorrow.
column9: A formal, news-style word: leaders, ministers and envoys 會晤, as in 兩國領導人會晤. Friends meeting up say 見面.

column3: Works as a verb (贿赂官员) and as a noun (收受贿赂). Giving a bribe is 行贿, taking one 受贿.
column4: 他因接受贿赂被判了刑。
column5: 他因接受賄賂被判了刑。
column6: Tā yīn jiēshòu huìlù bèi pàn le xíng.
column7: He was sentenced for accepting bribes.
column9: Works as a verb (賄賂官員) and as a noun (收受賄賂). Giving a bribe is 行賄, taking one 受賄.

column3: The meat-and-fish side of a menu, against 素: 荤菜 is a meat dish, and 荤素搭配 means a mix of both. 荤 also means racy or dirty, as in 荤笑话 or 荤段子, a dirty joke.
column4: 他不吃荤，只吃素菜。
column5: 他不吃葷，只吃素菜。
column6: Tā bù chī hūn, zhǐ chī sùcài.
column7: He does not eat meat, only vegetarian dishes.
column9: The meat-and-fish side of a menu, against 素: 葷菜 is a meat dish, and 葷素搭配 means a mix of both. 葷 also means racy or dirty, as in 葷笑話 or 葷段子, a dirty joke.

column3: A condition usually follows: 浑身发抖, 浑身是汗, 浑身无力. It is more vivid than 全身, with the feeling spread over the whole body. 浑 can mean "muddy", and also "whole, all over", which is the sense here.
column4: 他浑身是汗，累得说不出话来。
column5: 他渾身是汗，累得說不出話來。
column6: Tā húnshēn shì hàn, lèi de shuō bù chū huà lái.
column7: He was drenched in sweat, too tired to speak.
column9: A condition usually follows: 渾身發抖, 渾身是汗, 渾身無力. It is more vivid than 全身, with the feeling spread over the whole body. 渾 can mean "muddy", and also "whole, all over", which is the sense here.

column3: Used for mixing up things that should stay apart, usually abstract ones: 混淆概念, 混淆是非. 混淆视听 is to mislead the public. Taiwan reads 淆 yáo, not xiáo.
column4: 不要把这两个概念混淆了。
column5: 不要把這兩個概念混淆了。
column6: Bùyào bǎ zhè liǎng ge gàiniàn hùnxiáo le.
column7: Don't mix up these two concepts.
column9: Used for mixing up things that should stay apart, usually abstract ones: 混淆概念, 混淆是非. 混淆視聽 is to mislead the public. Taiwan reads 淆 yáo, not xiáo.

column3: Describes water and air that are cloudy, as in 混浊的河水, 混浊的空气; old, dull eyes can be 混浊 too. 浑浊 is the same word.
column4: 河水很混浊，不能直接喝。
column5: 河水很混濁，不能直接喝。
column6: Héshuǐ hěn hùnzhuó, bù néng zhíjiē hē.
column7: The river water is murky and cannot be drunk directly.
column9: Describes water and air that are cloudy, as in 混濁的河水, 混濁的空氣; old, dull eyes can be 混濁 too. 渾濁 is the same word.

column3: The flame you see rising off something burning. For a small flame on a candle or stove, speech often says 火苗.
column4: 火焰越烧越高，照亮了整个院子。
column5: 火焰越燒越高，照亮了整個院子。
column6: Huǒyàn yuè shāo yuè gāo, zhào liàng le zhěnggè yuànzi.
column7: The flames rose higher and higher and lit up the whole courtyard.
column9: The flame you see rising off something burning. For a small flame on a candle or stove, speech often says 火苗.

column3: One of China's Four Great Inventions (四大发明), with the compass, papermaking and printing. 火药味 is the smell of gunpowder, and also the tension just before an argument. 药 covers more than medicine, which is why it fits an explosive.
column4: 火药是中国人发明的。
column5: 火藥是中國人發明的。
column6: Huǒyào shì Zhōngguórén fāmíng de.
column7: Gunpowder was invented by the Chinese.
column9: One of China's Four Great Inventions (四大發明), with the compass, papermaking and printing. 火藥味 is the smell of gunpowder, and also the tension just before an argument. 藥 covers more than medicine, which is why it fits an explosive.

column3: The money of a country or system, not the cash in your hand (that is 钱). 币 turns up across money words: 硬币 coin, 纸币 banknote, 外币 foreign currency, 人民币.
column4: 不同国家使用不同的货币。
column5: 不同國家使用不同的貨幣。
column6: Bùtóng guójiā shǐyòng bùtóng de huòbì.
column7: Different countries use different currencies.
column9: The money of a country or system, not the cash in your hand (that is 錢). 幣 turns up across money words: 硬幣 coin, 紙幣 banknote, 外幣 foreign currency, 人民幣.

column3: The laughter is mocking and aimed at someone's mistake or weakness; often passive: 被人讥笑, 遭到讥笑.
column4: 他被同学讥笑，心里很难过。
column5: 他被同學譏笑，心裡很難過。
column6: Tā bèi tóngxué jīxiào, xīnli hěn nánguò.
column7: He was laughed at by his classmates and felt very sad.
column9: The laughter is mocking and aimed at someone's mistake or weakness; often passive: 被人譏笑, 遭到譏笑.

column3: Names the condition of hunger or describes starving people, as in 饥饿感 or 死于饥饿. In everyday speech "I'm hungry" is just 我饿了.
column4: 他饥饿难忍，一口气吃了三碗饭。
column5: 他飢餓難忍，一口氣吃了三碗飯。
column6: Tā jī'è nánrěn, yīkǒuqì chī le sān wǎn fàn.
column7: Unable to bear his hunger, he ate three bowls of rice in one go.
column9: Names the condition of hunger or describes starving people, as in 飢餓感 or 死於飢餓. In everyday speech "I'm hungry" is just 我餓了.

column3: Two uses: motorized, as in 机动车 and 机动车道, and flexible, as in 机动时间 or 机动安排. 机 carries both ideas: a machine, and being quick and flexible.
column4: 我们的时间比较机动，可以随时调整。
column5: 我們的時間比較機動，可以隨時調整。
column6: Wǒmen de shíjiān bǐjiào jīdòng, kěyǐ suíshí tiáozhěng.
column7: Our schedule is fairly flexible and can be adjusted anytime.
column9: Two uses: motorized, as in 機動車 and 機動車道, and flexible, as in 機動時間 or 機動安排. 機 carries both ideas: a machine, and being quick and flexible.

column3: A friendly word for someone who reacts quickly and handles situations smartly, often a child or young helper. It is about quick wits in the moment, while 聪明 is cleverness in general.
column4: 这个孩子很机灵，一学就会。
column5: 這個孩子很機靈，一學就會。
column6: Zhège háizi hěn jīling, yī xué jiù huì.
column7: This child is sharp and picks things up right away.
column9: A friendly word for someone who reacts quickly and handles situations smartly, often a child or young helper. It is about quick wits in the moment, while 聰明 is cleverness in general.

column3: Used for state, military and business secrets, as a noun or before a noun: 机密文件, 泄露机密. It is heavier and more official than 秘密, which also covers everyday secrets. In 密, the character is read as something hidden in the mountains, hence secret.
column4: 这是公司的机密文件，请不要外传。
column5: 這是公司的機密文件，請不要外傳。
column6: Zhè shì gōngsī de jīmì wénjiàn, qǐng bùyào wàichuán.
column7: This is a confidential company document, so please don't pass it on.
column9: Used for state, military and business secrets, as a noun or before a noun: 機密文件, 泄露機密. It is heavier and more official than 秘密, which also covers everyday secrets. In 密, the character is read as something hidden in the mountains, hence secret.

column3: Praises quick thinking in a tight spot: a clever answer, a way out of an awkward moment. It describes people, replies and reactions, and is about presence of mind more than book smarts.
column4: 他用机智的回答化解了尴尬。
column5: 他用機智的回答化解了尷尬。
column6: Tā yòng jīzhì de huídá huàjiě le gāngà.
column7: He defused the awkward moment with a quick-witted answer.
column9: Praises quick thinking in a tight spot: a clever answer, a way out of an awkward moment. It describes people, replies and reactions, and is about presence of mind more than book smarts.

column3: The everyday word of genetics (基因组, 转基因食品), and also used figuratively for a trait built into a company, a team or a culture, as in 创新基因.
column4: 这种病和基因有关。
column5: 這種病和基因有關。
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng hé jīyīn yǒuguān.
column7: This disease is related to genes.
column9: The everyday word of genetics (基因組, 轉基因食品), and also used figuratively for a trait built into a company, a team or a culture, as in 創新基因.

column3: Takes something inside a person as its object: 激发兴趣, 激发灵感, 激发潜力, 激发斗志. The one doing it is a teacher, a book, a setback or a place.
column4: 好老师能激发学生的兴趣。
column5: 好老師能激發學生的興趣。
column6: Hǎo lǎoshī néng jīfā xuésheng de xìngqù.
column7: A good teacher can spark students' interest.
column9: Takes something inside a person as its object: 激發興趣, 激發靈感, 激發潛力, 激發鬥志. The one doing it is a teacher, a book, a setback or a place.

column3: Encouraging people toward a goal with rewards, praise or an example: 激励员工, 激励自己. As a noun it is an incentive, as in 激励机制 and 奖金激励.
column4: 老板用奖金激励员工。
column5: 老闆用獎金激勵員工。
column6: Lǎobǎn yòng jiǎngjīn jīlì yuángōng.
column7: The boss motivates employees with bonuses.
column9: Encouraging people toward a goal with rewards, praise or an example: 激勵員工, 激勵自己. As a noun it is an incentive, as in 激勵機制 and 獎金激勵.

column3: Used in advice and warnings, right before a verb: 及早发现, 及早治疗, 及早准备. It means doing it early enough that it is not too late. 及 is drawn as a hand grabbing a person: to reach someone.
column4: 有问题要及早解决。
column5: 有問題要及早解決。
column6: Yǒu wèntí yào jízǎo jiějué.
column7: If there's a problem, solve it early.
column9: Used in advice and warnings, right before a verb: 及早發現, 及早治療, 及早準備. It means doing it early enough that it is not too late. 及 is drawn as a hand grabbing a person: to reach someone.

column3: Used for ranks and grades in a system with fixed levels, such as officials' ranks, hotels, referees, meetings or competitions: 高级别, 同一级别, 什么级别. 别 here is a suffix for a category, as in 性别 and 派别.
column4: 这两个球队不在同一个级别。
column5: 這兩個球隊不在同一個級別。
column6: Zhè liǎng ge qiúduì bù zài tóngyī ge jíbié.
column7: These two teams are not in the same league.
column9: Used for ranks and grades in a system with fixed levels, such as officials' ranks, hotels, referees, meetings or competitions: 高級別, 同一級別, 什麼級別. 別 here is a suffix for a category, as in 性別 and 派別.

column3: The furthest point a person or thing can go: 体力的极限, 挑战极限, 达到极限. Also a technical term in math, and the 极限 of 极限运动, extreme sports.
column4: 他已经到了体力的极限。
column5: 他已經到了體力的極限。
column6: Tā yǐjīng dào le tǐlì de jíxiàn.
column7: He has reached the limit of his strength.
column9: The furthest point a person or thing can go: 體力的極限, 挑戰極限, 達到極限. Also a technical term in math, and the 極限 of 極限運動, extreme sports.

column3: A more written 'even if', much like 即使. The second half usually has 也 or 还 to answer it, and 即便如此 means 'even so'.
column4: 即便下雨，我们也要去。
column5: 即便下雨，我們也要去。
column6: Jíbiàn xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains, we're going.
column9: A more written 'even if', much like 即使. The second half usually has 也 or 還 to answer it, and 即便如此 means 'even so'.

column3: A criticism, mostly written: wanting quick results and profit without thinking of the long run. It is aimed at people, companies, policies or schools, as in 急功近利的做法, and often follows 不能 or 不要.
column4: 做学问不能急功近利。
column5: 做學問不能急功近利。
column6: Zuò xuéwèn bùnéng jígōngjìnlì.
column7: You can't go after quick profit when you pursue scholarship.
column9: A criticism, mostly written: wanting quick results and profit without thinking of the long run. It is aimed at people, companies, policies or schools, as in 急功近利的做法, and often follows 不能 or 不要.

column3: Describes a sharp, sudden change and sits before a verb or noun: 急剧增加, 急剧下降, 急剧变化. It is for changes in numbers and situations, not for a person hurrying.
column4: 近年来，物价急剧上涨。
column5: 近年來，物價急劇上漲。
column6: Jìnnián lái, wùjià jíjù shàngzhǎng.
column7: In recent years, prices have risen sharply.
column9: Describes a sharp, sudden change and sits before a verb or noun: 急劇增加, 急劇下降, 急劇變化. It is for changes in numbers and situations, not for a person hurrying.

column3: Eager, urgent wanting, shown in a person's manner or voice: 急切的心情, 急切地问, 急切需要. It carries feeling; for a situation that is merely urgent, 紧急 is the word. 切 is read qiè here, 'eager'; as 'to cut' it is qiē.
column4: 他急切地想知道结果。
column5: 他急切地想知道結果。
column6: Tā jíqiè de xiǎng zhīdào jiéguǒ.
column7: He was eager to know the result.
column9: Eager, urgent wanting, shown in a person's manner or voice: 急切的心情, 急切地問, 急切需要. It carries feeling; for a situation that is merely urgent, 緊急 is the word. 切 is read qiè here, 'eager'; as 'to cut' it is qiē.

column3: A warning against wanting results before putting in the time, common for study, training, reform and new managers. It usually appears as advice: 不能急于求成, 不要急于求成.
column4: 学外语不能急于求成。
column5: 學外語不能急於求成。
column6: Xué wàiyǔ bùnéng jíyúqiúchéng.
column7: You can't rush things when learning a foreign language.
column9: A warning against wanting results before putting in the time, common for study, training, reform and new managers. It usually appears as advice: 不能急於求成, 不要急於求成.

column3: Describes a person or a mood without patience: 性格急躁, 急躁情绪. It can also mean acting too hastily, and 别急躁 is common advice to someone about to rush.
column4: 他性格急躁，做事不够冷静。
column5: 他性格急躁，做事不夠冷靜。
column6: Tā xìnggé jízào, zuòshì bùgòu lěngjìng.
column7: He is impatient by nature and not calm enough in his work.
column9: Describes a person or a mood without patience: 性格急躁, 急躁情緒. It can also mean acting too hastily, and 別急躁 is common advice to someone about to rush.

column3: A form and résumé word: it is asked on applications and files, and usually answered with a province and city, as in 籍贯：浙江杭州. Where someone was born or lives now can be different.
column4: 请在表格里填写你的籍贯。
column5: 請在表格裡填寫你的籍貫。
column6: Qǐng zài biǎogé lǐ tiánxiě nǐ de jíguàn.
column7: Please fill in your ancestral home on the form.
column9: A form and résumé word: it is asked on applications and files, and usually answered with a province and city, as in 籍貫：浙江杭州. Where someone was born or lives now can be different.

column3: The formal written record of a meeting: 会议纪要, 座谈会纪要. It sets down the decisions and main points, not every word, and is sent around at work and in government.
column4: 会后请把会议纪要发给大家。
column5: 會後請把會議紀要發給大家。
column6: Huì hòu qǐng bǎ huìyì jìyào fā gěi dàjiā.
column7: After the meeting, please send everyone the minutes.
column9: The formal written record of a meeting: 會議紀要, 座談會紀要. It sets down the decisions and main points, not every word, and is sent around at work and in government.

column3: Third place in a contest, after 冠军 and 亚军. It is used in sports, quizzes and talent shows, and goes with 获得, 夺得 and 拿到.
column4: 中国队获得了女子双打的季军。
column5: 中國隊獲得了女子雙打的季軍。
column6: Zhōngguó duì huòdé le nǚzǐ shuāngdǎ de jìjūn.
column7: The Chinese team won third place in women's doubles.
column9: Third place in a contest, after 冠軍 and 亞軍. It is used in sports, quizzes and talent shows, and goes with 獲得, 奪得 and 拿到.

column3: A sign from small clues that something is happening or about to: 有...的迹象, 没有任何迹象, 好转的迹象. A verb like 表明 or 显示 often goes with it. Taiwan reads the first syllable jī.
column4: 经济出现了好转的迹象。
column5: 經濟出現了好轉的跡象。
column6: Jīngjì chūxiàn le hǎozhuǎn de jìxiàng.
column7: The economy has shown signs of improving.
column9: A sign from small clues that something is happening or about to: 有...的跡象, 沒有任何跡象, 好轉的跡象. A verb like 表明 or 顯示 often goes with it. Taiwan reads the first syllable jī.

column3: Often takes hope or feeling as its object: 寄托希望, 寄托哀思, 寄托思念, with 在 for where it is placed. It can also mean leaving something in another person's care.
column4: 父母把希望寄托在孩子身上。
column5: 父母把希望寄託在孩子身上。
column6: Fùmǔ bǎ xīwàng jìtuō zài háizi shēnshang.
column7: Parents place their hopes on their children.
column9: Often takes hope or feeling as its object: 寄託希望, 寄託哀思, 寄託思念, with 在 for where it is placed. It can also mean leaving something in another person's care.

column3: A deep, still quiet, often at night or in empty places: 寂静的夜晚, 一片寂静. It is more literary than 安静, which is also for asking people to be quiet. In Taiwan 寂 is read jí.
column4: 深夜的街道一片寂静。
column5: 深夜的街道一片寂靜。
column6: Shēnyè de jiēdào yī piàn jìjìng.
column7: The street is perfectly quiet late at night.
column9: A deep, still quiet, often at night or in empty places: 寂靜的夜晚, 一片寂靜. It is more literary than 安靜, which is also for asking people to be quiet. In Taiwan 寂 is read jí.

column3: For things that are already bad and get worse: 矛盾加剧, 病情加剧, 竞争加剧. It can take an object (加剧危机) or stand alone.
column4: 污染加剧了环境问题。
column5: 污染加劇了環境問題。
column6: Wūrǎn jiājù le huánjìng wèntí.
column7: Pollution has made the environmental problems worse.
column9: For things that are already bad and get worse: 矛盾加劇, 病情加劇, 競爭加劇. It can take an object (加劇危機) or stand alone.

column3: Something of another kind is mixed in, usually followed by 着: 夹杂着雨, 夹杂着英语, 夹杂着不满. It is a thing mixed into something larger, not a deliberate mix. 夹 shows one person holding two others under his arm, or two people sandwiching one. Taiwan reads 夹 jiá here.
column4: 他说话时夹杂着不少英语单词。
column5: 他說話時夾雜著不少英語單詞。
column6: Tā shuōhuà shí jiāzá zhe bùshǎo Yīngyǔ dāncí.
column7: He mixes quite a few English words into his speech.
column9: Something of another kind is mixed in, usually followed by 著: 夾雜著雨, 夾雜著英語, 夾雜著不滿. It is a thing mixed into something larger, not a deliberate mix. 夾 shows one person holding two others under his arm, or two people sandwiching one. Taiwan reads 夾 jiá here.

column3: A written, banquet-style word for fine dishes, found in toasts, menus and descriptions, most often in the set phrase 美酒佳肴. It is not for an ordinary meal.
column4: 桌上摆满了美酒佳肴。
column5: 桌上擺滿了美酒佳餚。
column6: Zhuōshang bǎimǎn le měijiǔ jiāyáo.
column7: The table was piled with fine wine and delicacies.
column9: A written, banquet-style word for fine dishes, found in toasts, menus and descriptions, most often in the set phrase 美酒佳餚. It is not for an ordinary meal.

column3: Describes everyday, home-style things in set phrases: 家常菜 (home cooking), 家常便饭, 拉家常 (to chat about daily life). It is rarely used on its own.
column4: 我最爱吃妈妈做的家常菜。
column5: 我最愛吃媽媽做的家常菜。
column6: Wǒ zuì ài chī māma zuò de jiācháng cài.
column7: I love my mom's home cooking best.
column9: Describes everyday, home-style things in set phrases: 家常菜 (home cooking), 家常便飯, 拉家常 (to chat about daily life). It is rarely used on its own.

column3: A casual word for a person, friendly or scolding depending on tone: 这家伙, 你这个家伙, 好家伙. It is not polite for a stranger. It can also mean a tool or a weapon.
column4: 那个家伙又迟到了。
column5: 那個傢伙又遲到了。
column6: Nàge jiāhuo yòu chídào le.
column7: That guy is late again.
column9: A casual word for a person, friendly or scolding depending on tone: 這傢伙, 你這個傢伙, 好家伙. It is not polite for a stranger. It can also mean a tool or a weapon.

column3: Said of a name, story, song, or brand that practically everyone in the country has heard of. It is a written, slightly formal praise, and often sits before a noun with 的, as in 家喻户晓的明星.
column4: 这部电影的主角在全国家喻户晓。
column5: 這部電影的主角在全國家喻戶曉。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de zhǔjué zài quánguó jiāyùhùxiǎo.
column7: The lead of this movie is a household name across the country.
column9: Said of a name, story, song, or brand that practically everyone in the country has heard of. It is a written, slightly formal praise, and often sits before a noun with 的, as in 家喻戶曉的明星.

column3: Before a noun it means the most advanced: 尖端技术, 尖端科学. It is also the literal tip of a pointed thing, though for a pencil or needle people more often say 尖. 尖 is built from small 小 and large 大, a shape that widens from a point.
column4: 这家公司专门研究尖端技术。
column5: 這家公司專門研究尖端技術。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānmén yánjiū jiānduān jìshù.
column7: This company specializes in cutting-edge technology.
column9: Before a noun it means the most advanced: 尖端技術, 尖端科學. It is also the literal tip of a pointed thing, though for a pencil or needle people more often say 尖. 尖 is built from small 小 and large 大, a shape that widens from a point.

column3: Praise for a person, will, or spirit that bends under pressure but does not break: 坚韧的性格, 坚韧不拔. It is used for character far more than for physical objects.
column4: 她有坚韧的性格，从不轻易放弃。
column5: 她有堅韌的性格，從不輕易放棄。
column6: Tā yǒu jiānrèn de xìnggé, cóngbù qīngyì fàngqì.
column7: She has a tough character and never gives up easily.
column9: Praise for a person, will, or spirit that bends under pressure but does not break: 堅韌的性格, 堅韌不拔. It is used for character far more than for physical objects.

column3: Used for solid things like a wall, a floor, or a body, and just as often for abstract ones: 坚实的基础 is a solid foundation, 坚实的步伐 a steady stride.
column4: 这座桥的基础非常坚实。
column5: 這座橋的基礎非常堅實。
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo de jīchǔ fēicháng jiānshí.
column7: The foundation of this bridge is very solid.
column9: Used for solid things like a wall, a floor, or a body, and just as often for abstract ones: 堅實的基礎 is a solid foundation, 堅實的步伐 a steady stride.

column3: Physical hardness of materials such as rock, shell, ice, or metal. A hard question is 难, and hard work is 辛苦; neither is 坚硬.
column4: 这种木头非常坚硬。
column5: 這種木頭非常堅硬。
column6: Zhè zhǒng mùtou fēicháng jiānyìng.
column7: This kind of wood is extremely hard.
column9: Physical hardness of materials such as rock, shell, ice, or metal. A hard question is 難, and hard work is 辛苦; neither is 堅硬.

column3: On the mainland it is mostly owning up to your own mistakes (做检讨, 写检讨); in Taiwan it is just as often a review of what went right and wrong, as in 检讨会.
column4: 他在会上检讨了自己的错误。
column5: 他在會上檢討了自己的錯誤。
column6: Tā zài huìshang jiǎntǎo le zìjǐ de cuòwù.
column7: He admitted his mistakes at the meeting.
column9: On the mainland it is mostly owning up to your own mistakes (做檢討, 寫檢討); in Taiwan it is just as often a review of what went right and wrong, as in 檢討會.

column3: A verb plus object, so other words go between the two: 剪了彩, 为新店剪彩. The ribbon is cut by a guest of honor to open a shop, bridge, or exhibition.
column4: 市长为新商场剪彩。
column5: 市長為新商場剪彩。
column6: Shìzhǎng wèi xīn shāngchǎng jiǎncǎi.
column7: The mayor cut the ribbon for the new mall.
column9: A verb plus object, so other words go between the two: 剪了彩, 為新店剪彩. The ribbon is cut by a guest of honor to open a shop, bridge, or exhibition.

column3: Takes an object that was complicated: 简化手续, 简化程序. The opposite is 复杂化. Written with 汉字, it names the reform that produced the simplified characters.
column4: 新系统简化了申请手续。
column5: 新系統簡化了申請手續。
column6: Xīn xìtǒng jiǎnhuà le shēnqǐng shǒuxù.
column7: The new system simplified the application process.
column9: Takes an object that was complicated: 簡化手續, 簡化程序. The opposite is 複雜化. Written with 漢字, it names the reform that produced the simplified characters.

column3: Describes buildings, equipment, and living conditions that are crude and bare: 条件简陋, 设备简陋. Mildly negative, and people also say it modestly about their own home.
column4: 山里的学校条件很简陋。
column5: 山裡的學校條件很簡陋。
column6: Shānlǐ de xuéxiào tiáojiàn hěn jiǎnlòu.
column7: The school in the mountains has very basic facilities.
column9: Describes buildings, equipment, and living conditions that are crude and bare: 條件簡陋, 設備簡陋. Mildly negative, and people also say it modestly about their own home.

column3: The counterpart is 繁体字, traditional characters; Taiwan calls them 正体字. 体 here is a style of writing, as in 字体.
column4: 我在学校学的是简体字。
column5: 我在學校學的是簡體字。
column6: Wǒ zài xuéxiào xué de shì jiǎntǐzì.
column7: What I learned at school was simplified characters.
column9: The counterpart is 繁體字, traditional characters; Taiwan calls them 正體字. 體 here is a style of writing, as in 字體.

column3: Describes an explanation or summary that is short but covers the main points. It goes with verbs of telling: 简要介绍, 简要说明, 简要汇报.
column4: 请你简要地介绍一下自己。
column5: 請你簡要地介紹一下自己。
column6: Qǐng nǐ jiǎnyào de jièshào yīxià zìjǐ.
column7: Please briefly introduce yourself.
column9: Describes an explanation or summary that is short but covers the main points. It goes with verbs of telling: 簡要介紹, 簡要說明, 簡要匯報.

column3: Praise for someone who has seen and learned a lot, usually from travel or long experience rather than books. It describes the person, either as a predicate or before 的 and a noun: 见多识广的人.
column4: 他走过很多地方，见多识广。
column5: 他走過很多地方，見多識廣。
column6: Tā zǒuguo hěn duō dìfang, jiànduōshíguǎng.
column7: He has been to many places and is worldly and well informed.
column9: Praise for someone who has seen and learned a lot, usually from travel or long experience rather than books. It describes the person, either as a predicate or before 的 and a noun: 見多識廣的人.

column3: A considered opinion or insight, weightier than 看法. It goes with 有 and with praise like 独到 and 深刻: 独到的见解 is an original view.
column4: 她对这个问题有独到的见解。
column5: 她對這個問題有獨到的見解。
column6: Tā duì zhège wèntí yǒu dúdào de jiànjiě.
column7: She has an original view on this problem.
column9: A considered opinion or insight, weightier than 看法. It goes with 有 and with praise like 獨到 and 深刻: 獨到的見解 is an original view.

column3: What you pick up by traveling and meeting people. It is a mass noun that goes with 增长 or 丰富: 增长见闻, and 所见所闻 is "all I saw and heard".
column4: 旅行让我增长了不少见闻。
column5: 旅行讓我增長了不少見聞。
column6: Lǚxíng ràng wǒ zēngzhǎng le bùshǎo jiànwén.
column7: Traveling broadened my experience quite a bit.
column9: What you pick up by traveling and meeting people. It is a mass noun that goes with 增長 or 豐富: 增長見聞, and 所見所聞 is "all I saw and heard".

column3: Praise for ordinary people who step in against a crime or danger without being asked. It turns up in news and awards: 见义勇为奖, 见义勇为的市民.
column4: 他因见义勇为被授予荣誉称号。
column5: 他因見義勇為被授予榮譽稱號。
column6: Tā yīn jiànyìyǒngwéi bèi shòuyǔ róngyù chēnghào.
column7: He was given an honorary title for his act of courage.
column9: Praise for ordinary people who step in against a crime or danger without being asked. It turns up in news and awards: 見義勇為獎, 見義勇為的市民.

column3: The ordinary word for a spy, in news and in stories: 派间谍, 商业间谍. Spying as an activity is 间谍活动.
column4: 他被怀疑是外国间谍。
column5: 他被懷疑是外國間諜。
column6: Tā bèi huáiyí shì wàiguó jiàndié.
column7: He is suspected of being a foreign spy.
column9: The ordinary word for a spy, in news and in stories: 派間諜, 商業間諜. Spying as an activity is 間諜活動.

column3: As a verb it takes the length of the gap straight after it: 间隔三天. As a noun it is the gap itself, in space or in time: 保持间隔.
column4: 两次治疗要间隔一周。
column5: 兩次治療要間隔一週。
column6: Liǎng cì zhìliáo yào jiàngé yī zhōu.
column7: Leave a week between the two treatments.
column9: As a verb it takes the length of the gap straight after it: 間隔三天. As a noun it is the gap itself, in space or in time: 保持間隔.

column3: A collective term for naval ships of every size, used in military news and reports: 海军舰艇, 舰艇编队. For one big ship, 军舰 is the everyday word.
column4: 海军的舰艇驶出了港口。
column5: 海軍的艦艇駛出了港口。
column6: Hǎijūn de jiàntǐng shǐ chū le gǎngkǒu.
column7: The navy ships sailed out of the harbor.
column9: A collective term for naval ships of every size, used in military news and reports: 海軍艦艇, 艦艇編隊. For one big ship, 軍艦 is the everyday word.

column3: Trampling something underfoot, and just as often figuratively: 践踏人权, 践踏尊严. In the figurative use it is strong criticism, common in news and speeches.
column4: 请不要践踏草坪。
column5: 請不要踐踏草坪。
column6: Qǐng bùyào jiàntà cǎopíng.
column7: Please do not trample the lawn.
column9: Trampling something underfoot, and just as often figuratively: 踐踏人權, 踐踏尊嚴. In the figurative use it is strong criticism, common in news and speeches.

column3: Liquid flying up and scattering: 水花四溅. What gets hit comes after it, often with 到: 溅到衣服上, or the amount with 了: 溅了一身泥.
column4: 汽车开过，水溅到了我身上。
column5: 汽車開過，水濺到了我身上。
column6: Qìchē kāiguò, shuǐ jiàn dào le wǒ shēnshang.
column7: The car drove past and water splashed onto me.
column9: Liquid flying up and scattering: 水花四濺. What gets hit comes after it, often with 到: 濺到衣服上, or the amount with 了: 濺了一身泥.

column3: To tell genuine from fake, or one kind from another, by close examination: 鉴别真伪, 鉴别真假. It is done by experts, for antiques, jewelry, or test samples.
column4: 专家正在鉴别这幅画的真假。
column5: 專家正在鑑別這幅畫的真假。
column6: Zhuānjiā zhèngzài jiànbié zhè fú huà de zhēnjiǎ.
column7: Experts are examining whether this painting is genuine.
column9: To tell genuine from fake, or one kind from another, by close examination: 鑑別真偽, 鑑別真假. It is done by experts, for antiques, jewelry, or test samples.

column3: A formal opener in reports and official notices: 鉴于 plus the reason, then a comma and what was decided. It is not used for casual reasons in speech, where 因为 is natural.
column4: 鉴于天气不好，比赛推迟了。
column5: 鑒於天氣不好，比賽推遲了。
column6: Jiànyú tiānqì bù hǎo, bǐsài tuīchí le.
column7: In view of the bad weather, the match was postponed.
column9: A formal opener in reports and official notices: 鑒於 plus the reason, then a comma and what was decided. It is not used for casual reasons in speech, where 因為 is natural.

column3: Spoken, for accepting something less than ideal because there is no better choice: 将就一下, 将就着用.
column4: 没有别的了，你就将就一下吧。
column5: 沒有別的了，你就將就一下吧。
column6: Méiyǒu bié de le, nǐ jiù jiāngjiu yīxià ba.
column7: There is nothing else, so make do with this.
column9: Spoken, for accepting something less than ideal because there is no better choice: 將就一下, 將就著用.

column3: Stiff because it cannot bend or relax: a neck, a smile, or a manner of acting (动作僵硬, 表情僵硬). Hard like rock is 坚硬, not this word.
column4: 坐了一整天，我的脖子有点僵硬。
column5: 坐了一整天，我的脖子有點僵硬。
column6: Zuò le yī zhěngtiān, wǒ de bózi yǒudiǎn jiāngyìng.
column7: After sitting all day, my neck is a bit stiff.
column9: Stiff because it cannot bend or relax: a neck, a smile, or a manner of acting (動作僵硬, 表情僵硬). Hard like rock is 堅硬, not this word.

column3: A reward from someone above for good work or behavior, such as a parent, teacher, or boss. It works as a verb (奖赏孩子) and a noun (得到奖赏), a broad, slightly formal word where speech often says 奖励.
column4: 老师奖赏了表现好的学生。
column5: 老師獎賞了表現好的學生。
column6: Lǎoshī jiǎngshǎng le biǎoxiàn hǎo de xuésheng.
column7: The teacher rewarded the students who behaved well.
column9: A reward from someone above for good work or behavior, such as a parent, teacher, or boss. It works as a verb (獎賞孩子) and a noun (得到獎賞), a broad, slightly formal word where speech often says 獎勵.

column3: The verb that goes with it is 划: 划桨 is to row, and 船桨 is a boat's oar.
column4: 他用力划桨，小船慢慢向前。
column5: 他用力划槳，小船慢慢向前。
column6: Tā yònglì huá jiǎng, xiǎochuán mànmàn xiàng qián.
column7: He rowed hard, and the little boat slowly moved forward.
column9: The verb that goes with it is 划: 划槳 is to row, and 船槳 is a boat's oar.

column3: A formal, somewhat literary word for something big or inevitable arriving: night (夜幕降临), a disaster, a festival, a baby, or a god. It is not used for a guest who simply comes over.
column4: 夜幕降临，路灯亮了。
column5: 夜幕降臨，路燈亮了。
column6: Yèmù jiànglín, lùdēng liàng le.
column7: Night fell, and the streetlights came on.
column9: A formal, somewhat literary word for something big or inevitable arriving: night (夜幕降臨), a disaster, a festival, a baby, or a god. It is not used for a guest who simply comes over.

column3: Works for lines and roads, but also for hands and legs (双手交叉) and for subjects or jobs that overlap (交叉学科, a cross-disciplinary field).
column4: 两条路在前面交叉。
column5: 兩條路在前面交叉。
column6: Liǎng tiáo lù zài qiánmiàn jiāochā.
column7: The two roads cross up ahead.
column9: Works for lines and roads, but also for hands and legs (雙手交叉) and for subjects or jobs that overlap (交叉學科, a cross-disciplinary field).

column3: Talks aimed at settling a dispute or getting something done, between governments or with a company or office. The pattern is 向/与 someone 交涉, and 严正交涉 is a firm diplomatic protest.
column4: 我们已经向公司交涉过了。
column5: 我們已經向公司交涉過了。
column6: Wǒmen yǐjīng xiàng gōngsī jiāoshè guo le.
column7: We have already taken it up with the company.
column9: Talks aimed at settling a dispute or getting something done, between governments or with a company or office. The pattern is 向/與 someone 交涉, and 嚴正交涉 is a firm diplomatic protest.

column3: Said of a person, often a child or a pampered girl, who can't take hardship or discomfort and complains easily. It can be mild teasing or a criticism; it is also used of fragile plants or things that need careful handling.
column4: 她从小很娇气，一点苦都吃不了。
column5: 她從小很嬌氣，一點苦都吃不了。
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo hěn jiāoqì, yīdiǎn kǔ dōu chī bù liǎo.
column7: She has been delicate since she was little and can't put up with any hardship.
column9: Said of a person, often a child or a pampered girl, who can't take hardship or discomfort and complains easily. It can be mild teasing or a criticism; it is also used of fragile plants or things that need careful handling.

column3: The worry of waiting, with time pressing: 焦急地等待 is the usual phrase, and 焦急万分 is extremely anxious. 焦 is burnt or scorched; think of 焦急 as burning with worry.
column4: 他焦急地等着医生的消息。
column5: 他焦急地等著醫生的消息。
column6: Tā jiāojí de děngzhe yīshēng de xiāoxi.
column7: He waited anxiously for news from the doctor.
column9: The worry of waiting, with time pressing: 焦急地等待 is the usual phrase, and 焦急萬分 is extremely anxious. 焦 is burnt or scorched; think of 焦急 as burning with worry.

column3: Said of getting through something by luck rather than by merit. 侥幸心理 is the gambler's hope that it will turn out all right this time, and 心存侥幸 is to count on luck.
column4: 他心存侥幸，没有系安全带。
column5: 他心存僥倖，沒有繫安全帶。
column6: Tā xīn cún jiǎoxìng, méiyǒu jì ānquándài.
column7: Counting on luck, he didn't fasten his seat belt.
column9: Said of getting through something by luck rather than by merit. 僥倖心理 is the gambler's hope that it will turn out all right this time, and 心存僥倖 is to count on luck.

column3: Stirring food, paint, concrete, anything that has to be mixed evenly; the usual ending is 均匀 (搅拌均匀). 搅拌机 is a mixer, and 水泥搅拌车 a cement truck.
column4: 把鸡蛋和面粉搅拌均匀。
column5: 把雞蛋和麵粉攪拌均勻。
column6: Bǎ jīdàn hé miànfěn jiǎobàn jūnyún.
column7: Stir the eggs and the flour until evenly mixed.
column9: Stirring food, paint, concrete, anything that has to be mixed evenly; the usual ending is 均勻 (攪拌均勻). 攪拌機 is a mixer, and 水泥攪拌車 a cement truck.

column3: Paying money to an authority, in a formal way: taxes, fees, fines, insurance premiums, dues. In everyday speech 交 does the same job (交税, 交学费); at a shop you 付钱.
column4: 他每年都按时缴纳税款。
column5: 他每年都按時繳納稅款。
column6: Tā měi nián dōu ànshí jiǎonà shuìkuǎn.
column7: He pays his taxes on time every year.
column9: Paying money to an authority, in a formal way: taxes, fees, fines, insurance premiums, dues. In everyday speech 交 does the same job (交稅, 交學費); at a shop you 付錢.

column3: A contest of strength or skill between two sides, such as teams, rivals or countries. It can be a real match or a quiet struggle (暗中较量), and the pattern is 与/和 someone 较量.
column4: 明天两队将在决赛中较量。
column5: 明天兩隊將在決賽中較量。
column6: Míngtiān liǎng duì jiāng zài juésài zhōng jiàoliàng.
column7: Tomorrow the two teams will face each other in the final.
column9: A contest of strength or skill between two sides, such as teams, rivals or countries. It can be a real match or a quiet struggle (暗中較量), and the pattern is 與/和 someone 較量.

column3: As a noun, the manners and decency that come from how a person was raised: 有教养 is well-bred, and 没教养 is a sharp insult aimed at a person and their parents. On its own, as the verb to teach, 教 is read jiāo; in this word it is jiào.
column4: 他很有教养，从不打断别人说话。
column5: 他很有教養，從不打斷別人說話。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu jiàoyǎng, cóngbù dǎduàn biérén shuōhuà.
column7: He is well mannered and never interrupts other people.
column9: As a noun, the manners and decency that come from how a person was raised: 有教養 is well-bred, and 沒教養 is a sharp insult aimed at a person and their parents. On its own, as the verb to teach, 教 is read jiāo; in this word it is jiào.

column3: A layer of society grouped by income, work or education: 中产阶层, 知识阶层, 高收入阶层. 阶级 is the sharper word for a class in the Marxist sense.
column4: 这项政策对中产阶层影响最大。
column5: 這項政策對中產階層影響最大。
column6: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè duì zhōngchǎn jiēcéng yǐngxiǎng zuì dà.
column7: This policy affects the middle class the most.
column9: A layer of society grouped by income, work or education: 中產階層, 知識階層, 高收入階層. 階級 is the sharper word for a class in the Marxist sense.

column3: A written, formal "all" that mostly lives in set phrases: 人人皆知, 皆大欢喜, 比比皆是. In speech 都 does this job.
column4: 这件事人人皆知。
column5: 這件事人人皆知。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì rénrén jiē zhī.
column7: Everybody knows about this.
column9: A written, formal "all" that mostly lives in set phrases: 人人皆知, 皆大歡喜, 比比皆是. In speech 都 does this job.

column3: Bringing something bad into the open, usually by reporters or investigators: 揭露真相, 揭露黑幕, 揭露丑闻. What is exposed is wrongdoing, not a pleasant surprise.
column4: 记者揭露了这家公司的丑闻。
column5: 記者揭露了這家公司的醜聞。
column6: Jìzhě jiēlù le zhè jiā gōngsī de chǒuwén.
column7: A reporter exposed the scandal of this company.
column9: Bringing something bad into the open, usually by reporters or investigators: 揭露真相, 揭露黑幕, 揭露醜聞. What is exposed is wrongdoing, not a pleasant surprise.

column3: Mostly about holding yourself back: 节制饮食, 节制花费. 有节制 means moderate, and 毫无节制 means without any restraint.
column4: 他喝酒很有节制。
column5: 他喝酒很有節制。
column6: Tā hē jiǔ hěn yǒu jiézhì.
column7: He is moderate in his drinking.
column9: Mostly about holding yourself back: 節制飲食, 節制花費. 有節制 means moderate, and 毫無節制 means without any restraint.

column3: In science it is to crystallize. In everyday writing it is the figurative noun, the fruit of long effort: 智慧的结晶, 心血的结晶. 爱情的结晶 is a gentle way to say a couple's child.
column4: 这部小说是他多年心血的结晶。
column5: 這部小說是他多年心血的結晶。
column6: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō shì tā duōnián xīnxuè de jiéjīng.
column7: This novel is the fruit of many years of his hard work.
column9: In science it is to crystallize. In everyday writing it is the figurative noun, the fruit of long effort: 智慧的結晶, 心血的結晶. 愛情的結晶 is a gentle way to say a couple's child.

column3: A set phrase for effort given without holding anything back, in speech and in writing. It fits promises (我会竭尽全力), rescue and care, and sport. 竭尽 (to use up) is the verb and 全力 (all one's strength) its object.
column4: 医生竭尽全力抢救病人。
column5: 醫生竭盡全力搶救病人。
column6: Yīshēng jiéjìnquánlì qiǎngjiù bìngrén.
column7: The doctors did everything they could to save the patient.
column9: A set phrase for effort given without holding anything back, in speech and in writing. It fits promises (我會竭盡全力), rescue and care, and sport. 竭盡 (to use up) is the verb and 全力 (all one's strength) its object.

column3: The employer is the one who does it, so it is often seen in the passive, 被解雇. In speech people also say 炒鱿鱼, slang for getting fired.
column4: 他因为迟到太多次被公司解雇了。
column5: 他因為遲到太多次被公司解僱了。
column6: Tā yīnwèi chídào tài duō cì bèi gōngsī jiěgù le.
column7: He was fired by the company for being late too many times.
column9: The employer is the one who does it, so it is often seen in the passive, 被解僱. In speech people also say 炒魷魚, slang for getting fired.

column3: Cutting open a body to study it, and also figuratively taking a problem or a person apart to analyze it: 解剖问题. 解剖学 is anatomy. The mainland reads 剖 as pōu, while Taiwan reads it pǒu.
column4: 学生在课堂上解剖了一只青蛙。
column5: 學生在課堂上解剖了一隻青蛙。
column6: Xuésheng zài kètáng shàng jiěpōu le yī zhī qīngwā.
column7: The students dissected a frog in class.
column9: Cutting open a body to study it, and also figuratively taking a problem or a person apart to analyze it: 解剖問題. 解剖學 is anatomy. The mainland reads 剖 as pōu, while Taiwan reads it pǒu.

column3: Said of a group that stops existing as a group: a band, club, company, assembly or parliament. It is also the order a commander gives to dismiss a lined-up crowd, 解散!
column4: 公司决定解散这个部门。
column5: 公司決定解散這個部門。
column6: Gōngsī juédìng jiěsàn zhège bùmén.
column7: The company decided to disband this department.
column9: Said of a group that stops existing as a group: a band, club, company, assembly or parliament. It is also the order a commander gives to dismiss a lined-up crowd, 解散!

column3: Something large and organized falling apart: an empire, an alliance, a family, a company. It is also what is done to an old ship or car when it is taken apart for scrap.
column4: 这个大家族渐渐解体了。
column5: 這個大家族漸漸解體了。
column6: Zhège dàjiāzú jiànjiàn jiětǐ le.
column7: This big family gradually fell apart.
column9: Something large and organized falling apart: an empire, an alliance, a family, a company. It is also what is done to an old ship or car when it is taken apart for scrap.

column3: Staying on guard against danger, as police and soldiers do: 加强戒备, 戒备森严 (heavily guarded). It can also be a person's wariness toward someone, as in 心存戒备. 戒 shows a weapon held up as a warning.
column4: 警方加强了对机场的戒备。
column5: 警方加強了對機場的戒備。
column6: Jǐngfāng jiāqiáng le duì jīchǎng de jièbèi.
column7: The police stepped up security at the airport.
column9: Staying on guard against danger, as police and soldiers do: 加強戒備, 戒備森嚴 (heavily guarded). It can also be a person's wariness toward someone, as in 心存戒備. 戒 shows a weapon held up as a warning.

column3: Mostly a line between abstract things that you draw or cross: 划清界限 is to draw a clear line and distance yourself from someone, and 打破界限 is to break down a boundary.
column4: 工作和生活之间应该有明确的界限。
column5: 工作和生活之間應該有明確的界限。
column6: Gōngzuò hé shēnghuó zhījiān yīnggāi yǒu míngquè de jièxiàn.
column7: There should be a clear boundary between work and life.
column9: Mostly a line between abstract things that you draw or cross: 劃清界限 is to draw a clear line and distance yourself from someone, and 打破界限 is to break down a boundary.

column3: The object is usually a tool, method or outside force that you rely on to get something done: 借助网络, 借助工具, 借助外力. The result follows, often after 来 or 才.
column4: 他借助字典读懂了这篇文章。
column5: 他借助字典讀懂了這篇文章。
column6: Tā jièzhù zìdiǎn dúdǒng le zhè piān wénzhāng.
column7: He understood this article with the help of a dictionary.
column9: The object is usually a tool, method or outside force that you rely on to get something done: 借助網絡, 借助工具, 借助外力. The result follows, often after 來 or 才.

column3: How someone eats, reads or listens when thoroughly enjoying it. It follows a verb with 得 (吃得津津有味, 听得津津有味) or comes before it with 地, and it is always positive.
column4: 孩子们津津有味地吃着冰淇淋。
column5: 孩子們津津有味地吃著冰淇淋。
column6: Háizimen jīnjīnyǒuwèi de chīzhe bīngqílín.
column7: The children ate their ice cream with great relish.
column9: How someone eats, reads or listens when thoroughly enjoying it. It follows a verb with 得 (吃得津津有味, 聽得津津有味) or comes before it with 地, and it is always positive.

column3: It describes time, tasks and situations (时间紧迫, 形势紧迫), not a person's feeling; to say you feel rushed, use 着急.
column4: 时间很紧迫，我们得马上出发。
column5: 時間很緊迫，我們得馬上出發。
column6: Shíjiān hěn jǐnpò, wǒmen děi mǎshàng chūfā.
column7: Time is very tight; we have to leave right away.
column9: It describes time, tasks and situations (時間緊迫, 形勢緊迫), not a person's feeling; to say you feel rushed, use 著急.

column3: Often set against 雪中送炭, help that arrives when someone truly needs it; 锦上添花 is the pleasant extra on top of something already good, so it is usually said of good news, gifts and honors.
column4: 他本来就很优秀，再得个奖更是锦上添花。
column5: 他本來就很優秀，再得個獎更是錦上添花。
column6: Tā běnlái jiù hěn yōuxiù, zài dé gè jiǎng gèng shì jǐnshàngtiānhuā.
column7: He was already excellent, and winning an award is the icing on the cake.
column9: Often set against 雪中送炭, help that arrives when someone truly needs it; 錦上添花 is the pleasant extra on top of something already good, so it is usually said of good news, gifts and honors.

column3: A written connector: the second step goes further than the first, as in 先…，进而…, or a result spreads on (…，进而影响整个社会). It sounds formal in speech.
column4: 我们先了解情况，进而提出解决办法。
column5: 我們先了解情況，進而提出解決辦法。
column6: Wǒmen xiān liǎojiě qíngkuàng, jìn'ér tíchū jiějué bànfǎ.
column7: We first understand the situation, and then go on to propose a solution.
column9: A written connector: the second step goes further than the first, as in 先…，進而…, or a result spreads on (…，進而影響整個社會). It sounds formal in speech.

column3: Used for moving up in rank or title inside an organization (晋升为经理, 职称晋升); in casual talk about getting promoted, 升职 is the everyday word.
column4: 他工作努力，去年晋升为部门经理。
column5: 他工作努力，去年晉升為部門經理。
column6: Tā gōngzuò nǔlì, qùnián jìnshēng wéi bùmén jīnglǐ.
column7: He works hard and was promoted to department manager last year.
column9: Used for moving up in rank or title inside an organization (晉升為經理, 職稱晉升); in casual talk about getting promoted, 升職 is the everyday word.

column3: It stresses soaking for a long time, so it goes with beans, rice, laundry and the like, and often with 在…里: 浸泡在水里. For a quick steep like tea, 泡 alone is enough.
column4: 豆子要先用水浸泡一夜。
column5: 豆子要先用水浸泡一夜。
column6: Dòuzi yào xiān yòng shuǐ jìnpào yī yè.
column7: The beans must first be soaked in water overnight.
column9: It stresses soaking for a long time, so it goes with beans, rice, laundry and the like, and often with 在…裡: 浸泡在水裡. For a quick steep like tea, 泡 alone is enough.

column3: The plant part in the set 根, 茎, 叶 (root, stem, leaf), as in school science; it is mostly a written, technical word.
column4: 这种花的茎很长，叶子很小。
column5: 這種花的莖很長，葉子很小。
column6: Zhè zhǒng huā de jīng hěn cháng, yèzi hěn xiǎo.
column7: This kind of flower has a long stem and small leaves.
column9: The plant part in the set 根, 莖, 葉 (root, stem, leaf), as in school science; it is mostly a written, technical word.

column3: Both characters belong to the loom and to the map: 经 is the warp and longitude, 纬 the woof and latitude. In daily life you mostly meet it in 经纬度, a place's coordinates; on its own it is literary.
column4: 请把这个地点的经纬度发给我。
column5: 請把這個地點的經緯度發給我。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège dìdiǎn de jīngwěi dù fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send me this place's longitude and latitude.
column9: Both characters belong to the loom and to the map: 經 is the warp and longitude, 緯 the woof and latitude. In daily life you mostly meet it in 經緯度, a place's coordinates; on its own it is literary.

column3: You disturb or alert someone by what you do, usually someone who should not have noticed, or someone important: 惊动了警察, 别惊动他.
column4: 小声点，别惊动了邻居。
column5: 小聲點，別驚動了鄰居。
column6: Xiǎoshēng diǎn, bié jīngdòng le línjū.
column7: Keep it down; don't disturb the neighbors.
column9: You disturb or alert someone by what you do, usually someone who should not have noticed, or someone important: 驚動了警察, 別驚動他.

column3: Wonder at something new or unexpected, as a feeling (感到惊奇) or as how someone speaks or looks (惊奇地发现, 惊奇的目光).
column4: 他惊奇地发现，门是开着的。
column5: 他驚奇地發現，門是開著的。
column6: Tā jīngqí de fāxiàn, mén shì kāizhe de.
column7: He was surprised to find that the door was open.
column9: Wonder at something new or unexpected, as a feeling (感到驚奇) or as how someone speaks or looks (驚奇地發現, 驚奇的目光).

column3: Praise for someone who does a job carefully and steadily, without cutting corners, often over many years: 兢兢业业地工作, 兢兢业业干了一辈子. It describes work or duty, not a task done once.
column4: 他在这家公司兢兢业业工作了三十年。
column5: 他在這家公司兢兢業業工作了三十年。
column6: Tā zài zhè jiā gōngsī jīngjīngyèyè gōngzuò le sānshí nián.
column7: He has worked conscientiously at this company for thirty years.
column9: Praise for someone who does a job carefully and steadily, without cutting corners, often over many years: 兢兢業業地工作, 兢兢業業幹了一輩子. It describes work or duty, not a task done once.

column3: Said of someone who plans every expense, so it is mild praise for thrift: 精打细算过日子. It fits money, materials and time.
column4: 她买东西总是精打细算，从不乱花钱。
column5: 她買東西總是精打細算，從不亂花錢。
column6: Tā mǎi dōngxi zǒngshì jīngdǎxìsuàn, cóng bù luàn huā qián.
column7: She always counts every penny when she shops and never wastes money.
column9: Said of someone who plans every expense, so it is mild praise for thrift: 精打細算過日子. It fits money, materials and time.

column3: The best part of something, mostly of culture, ideas, books or a body of work; its opposite is 糟粕, the worthless leftovers, as in the saying 取其精华，去其糟粕.
column4: 这本书是他多年研究的精华。
column5: 這本書是他多年研究的精華。
column6: Zhè běn shū shì tā duōnián yánjiū de jīnghuá.
column7: This book is the essence of his many years of research.
column9: The best part of something, mostly of culture, ideas, books or a body of work; its opposite is 糟粕, the worthless leftovers, as in the saying 取其精華，去其糟粕.

column3: To cut something down to what is needed: staff, procedures, an organization or a text (精简人员, 精简机构, 精简内容). It is a deliberate cut, usually of something that grew too big.
column4: 公司决定精简人员，减少开支。
column5: 公司決定精簡人員，減少開支。
column6: Gōngsī juédìng jīngjiǎn rényuán, jiǎnshǎo kāizhī.
column7: The company decided to trim its staff and cut expenses.
column9: To cut something down to what is needed: staff, procedures, an organization or a text (精簡人員, 精簡機構, 精簡內容). It is a deliberate cut, usually of something that grew too big.

column3: It says how finely something is made or planned: instruments, machines, designs (精密仪器, 精密的计划). For how exact a number or statement is, use 精确.
column4: 这台精密仪器价格很高。
column5: 這台精密儀器價格很高。
column6: Zhè tái jīngmì yíqì jiàgé hěn gāo.
column7: This precision instrument is very expensive.
column9: It says how finely something is made or planned: instruments, machines, designs (精密儀器, 精密的計劃). For how exact a number or statement is, use 精確.

column3: It says how exact a number, time, measurement or description is (精确的数字, 精确到秒), and can be used for a statement too: 精确地说.
column4: 请告诉我精确的时间。
column5: 請告訴我精確的時間。
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ jīngquè de shíjiān.
column7: Please tell me the exact time.
column9: It says how exact a number, time, measurement or description is (精確的數字, 精確到秒), and can be used for a statement too: 精確地說.

column3: The object is a subject or skill (精通英语, 精通法律), never a person. It claims real mastery, well beyond 会 or 懂, and is common on résumés.
column4: 她精通三种语言。
column5: 她精通三種語言。
column6: Tā jīngtōng sān zhǒng yǔyán.
column7: She is fluent in three languages.
column9: The object is a subject or skill (精通英語, 精通法律), never a person. It claims real mastery, well beyond 會 or 懂, and is common on résumés.

column3: Mostly an adverb before a verb of making or caring: 精心准备, 精心设计, 精心安排. After 得 it can take 很: 照顾得很精心.
column4: 妈妈精心准备了一桌饭菜。
column5: 媽媽精心準備了一桌飯菜。
column6: Māma jīngxīn zhǔnbèi le yī zhuō fàncài.
column7: Mom carefully prepared a whole table of dishes.
column9: Mostly an adverb before a verb of making or caring: 精心準備, 精心設計, 精心安排. After 得 it can take 很: 照顧得很精心.

column3: One sense of 益 is "all the more"; it began as water over a vessel, the old form of 溢, to overflow: think of it as "more". Praise for craftsmanship, products or skills: it is common in formal praise and slogans, and describes an attitude of never being satisfied with good enough.
column4: 他对自己的作品总是精益求精。
column5: 他對自己的作品總是精益求精。
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ de zuòpǐn zǒngshì jīngyìqiújīng.
column7: He always keeps improving his own work.
column9: One sense of 益 is "all the more"; it began as water over a vessel, the old form of 溢, to overflow: think of it as "more". Praise for craftsmanship, products or skills: it is common in formal praise and slogans, and describes an attitude of never being satisfied with good enough.

column3: It describes small things made with fine detail and care: food, gifts, crafts, decor, a face (精致的点心, 精致的包装). It is not used for big abstract things.
column4: 这家店的点心做得很精致。
column5: 這家店的點心做得很精緻。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de diǎnxin zuò de hěn jīngzhì.
column7: The pastries at this shop are made with great delicacy.
column9: It describes small things made with fine detail and care: food, gifts, crafts, decor, a face (精緻的點心, 精緻的包裝). It is not used for big abstract things.

column3: Mostly met in 颈椎病, the neck and shoulder trouble from long hours at a desk or on a phone; people say 颈椎疼 or 保护颈椎.
column4: 长时间低头玩手机对颈椎不好。
column5: 長時間低頭玩手機對頸椎不好。
column6: Cháng shíjiān dītóu wán shǒujī duì jǐngzhuī bù hǎo.
column7: Looking down at your phone for a long time is bad for your neck.
column9: Mostly met in 頸椎病, the neck and shoulder trouble from long hours at a desk or on a phone; people say 頸椎疼 or 保護頸椎.

column3: Staying on guard against danger or wrongdoing: 提高警惕, 保持警惕, 警惕骗局. The thing to watch for follows it directly, and it is common in warnings and news.
column4: 要警惕诈骗电话。
column5: 要警惕詐騙電話。
column6: Yào jǐngtì zhàpiàn diànhuà.
column7: Be on guard against scam calls.
column9: Staying on guard against danger or wrongdoing: 提高警惕, 保持警惕, 警惕騙局. The thing to watch for follows it directly, and it is common in warnings and news.

column3: The candidate is the subject: 竞选总统, 竞选班长. The voters do the 选 or 投票, so 竞选 is not what they do.
column4: 她打算竞选班长。
column5: 她打算競選班長。
column6: Tā dǎsuàn jìngxuǎn bānzhǎng.
column7: She plans to run for class president.
column9: The candidate is the subject: 競選總統, 競選班長. The voters do the 選 or 投票, so 競選 is not what they do.

column3: Praise for devotion to one's work, meaning your profession or post: 敬业精神, 爱岗敬业. It describes how someone treats their job, a trait employers and schools like to name.
column4: 他对工作非常敬业，从不迟到。
column5: 他對工作非常敬業，從不遲到。
column6: Tā duì gōngzuò fēicháng jìngyè, cóng bù chídào.
column7: He is very dedicated to his work and is never late.
column9: Praise for devotion to one's work, meaning your profession or post: 敬業精神, 愛崗敬業. It describes how someone treats their job, a trait employers and schools like to name.

column3: Mostly not a physical border but a level of attainment of mind, art or skill: 思想境界, 艺术境界, 达到…的境界. A higher 境界 means a deeper or more refined level.
column4: 他的书法已经达到了很高的境界。
column5: 他的書法已經達到了很高的境界。
column6: Tā de shūfǎ yǐjīng dádào le hěn gāo de jìngjiè.
column7: His calligraphy has reached a very high level.
column9: Mostly not a physical border but a level of attainment of mind, art or skill: 思想境界, 藝術境界, 達到…的境界. A higher 境界 means a deeper or more refined level.

column3: The alcohol of disinfecting (酒精消毒) and of the lab burner (酒精灯), and the alcohol content of a drink (酒精度). The drink itself is 酒.
column4: 伤口要先用酒精消毒。
column5: 傷口要先用酒精消毒。
column6: Shāngkǒu yào xiān yòng jiǔjīng xiāodú.
column7: Disinfect the wound with alcohol first.
column9: The alcohol of disinfecting (酒精消毒) and of the lab burner (酒精燈), and the alcohol content of a drink (酒精度). The drink itself is 酒.
